stayed at Quality Inn Bez Krishna, near Diamond Park, Visakhapatnam, from 31 July 2026 to 10 August 2026, and unfortunately, this was one of the most unpleasant hotel experiences I have had. I was initially given Room 209, which was considerably smaller than expected. I raised the issue multiple times with the staff and eventually had to escalate it through email before my room was changed to Room 205. While I appreciate that the room was eventually changed, I should not have had to repeatedly follow up for a basic room-related concern to be addressed. The bigger problem, however, was the behaviour of certain staff members. Throughout my 10-day stay, I felt repeatedly ignored and treated differently from my colleagues and other guests who accompanied me. The difference was particularly noticeable during breakfast. Staff would approach my colleagues and ask whether they wanted complimentary items or services such as live dosa and coffee, while I was never once offered these things throughout my entire stay. One incident may be insignificant, but when you experience the same kind of differential treatment repeatedly, it becomes difficult to ignore. There were also occasions when my calls were not attended to or my requests were not properly responded to. The attitude of certain reception staff was dismissive, condescending and unnecessarily rude. I would specifically mention Padma, the part-time/night receptionist, and Geetha, the HR cum morning receptionist. My interactions with both were extremely unpleasant. On one occasion, I waited around 10 minutes simply because Padma was on another call while I was waiting to get her name so I could accurately mention her in my feedback. I found this extremely unprofessional. The lack of basic assistance continued even at checkout. I was again left to manage my suitcases myself, and one of my suitcases fell while I was handling them. I nearly fell as well. What disappointed me most was not simply the room issue or the lack of luggage assistance. It was the overall attitude. I consistently felt unwelcome, looked down upon and treated differently from other guests. Hotel hospitality should be about treating every guest with basic courtesy and professionalism. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here. I would strongly recommend that the management seriously review the behaviour of the reception staff and the customer-service standards at this property. Based on my experience between 31 July and 10 August 2026, I would not stay here again and would not recommend this property to others. If there is any option of negitive ratings i would legit give a solid -10

We booked two rooms for three people and stayed for one night. One of the main reasons we chose this hotel was to assess whether its conference hall would be suitable for an upcoming meeting. Unfortunately, the overall experience was very disappointing. The hotel appears to be severely lacking in maintenance and is almost crumbling from the inside. The rooms were neglected, the service was limited, and the Wi-Fi did not work properly during our stay. When we inspected the conference hall, there was a strong and unbearable smell. However, considering its condition at the time, we simply could not gather the confidence to book it for our meeting. The most unpleasant part of the stay was spotting a rat in the restaurant while having breakfast. Although some of the items in the complimentary breakfast were good, seeing a rat completely spoiled the experience. The only real positive is the location. The hotel is situated in a prime area and is very easily accessible. Overall, the property urgently needs major improvements in maintenance, cleanliness, hygiene, and service. Its excellent location alone is not enough to make up for the poor experience.

This hotel has the potential to be one of the best budget stays because of its prime location near RK Beach in Visakhapatnam. However, the management needs to focus on proper hygiene, regular pest control, timely repairs, and overall maintenance to provide a better guest experience. My final advice is to visit the hotel and inspect the room before booking. Don't rely solely on the photos shown online, as they do not accurately reflect the current condition of the property. text_light: ⭐ 0/5 – Worst hotel experience. Families with babies, please think twice before booking. This was one of the most disappointing hotel stays I have ever experienced. I traveled from Hyderabad to Visakhapatnam with my wife and our 1-year-old baby. I intentionally booked a Superior Room with a King Size Bed, as clearly mentioned in the booking, because our baby's safety while sleeping was the most important factor. After reaching the hotel, I was shocked to find two separate single beds (approximately 6×3 ft each) instead of the promised king-size bed. These beds could not even be joined together. I repeatedly requested the reception to either provide the room that I had paid for, change the room, or arrange an alternative. Every request was simply rejected with "Not possible." They even refused to refund my money. What is the purpose of advertising and accepting bookings for a King Size Bed when you cannot provide one? If I had been informed honestly before check-in, I would have immediately chosen another hotel. I don't mind losing money when it comes to my child's safety, but after arriving late with a 1-year-old baby and finding no rooms available elsewhere, you left us with no option. This is unacceptable and completely irresponsible toward families with young children Because almost every hotel nearby was fully occupied, I had no option but to stay. The entire night turned into a nightmare. My wife had to sleep with our baby on one narrow bed, surrounding the baby with pillows to prevent a fall, while I slept separately. Neither of us slept peacefully for even a few hours because we were constantly worried about our child's safety. This completely ruined our family trip. The problems didn't stop there: The mattress was extremely hard and uncomfortable. There is no hand shower in the bathroom. The only option is the fixed overhead shower, so even if you don't want a full shower (including getting your hair wet), you have no choice. A TV was installed only for decoration—no cable channels, no Wi-Fi, and nothing to watch. The room security and privacy were also concerning and did not make us feel safe. To the hotel owner/ Group: Selling a room with facilities that are not actually provided is completely unacceptable. Guests choose rooms based on the information you advertise. For parents with infants, a king-size bed is not a luxury—it is a safety requirement. Ignoring genuine concerns and refusing to provide any solution shows a complete lack of responsibility and customer care. I strongly advise families with babies and young children to avoid this hotel unless you first verify the exact room and bed type in writing. Don't rely solely on the booking description, because my experience was completely different from what was promised.

I stayed at Zostel Visakhapatnam for 4 days, and honestly, it was a really fun experience. The property is located in a well-connected area and is quite close to the beach. It’s not exactly walkable in Vizag’s weather 😅, but it’s definitely not too far either, so getting around was pretty convenient. A special shoutout to Praveen, who received me when I arrived, and Pooja, the Community Manager. Both of them were incredibly kind, welcoming, and accommodating throughout my stay. They also gave me some really good local food recommendations, which made exploring Vizag even better. They even hosted a trek to Yarada, which was one of the highlights of the trip. And of course, the Zostel nights! 😄 The community vibe is what really makes the experience. I met a bunch of new people, spent the night playing games, chatting, and taking part in different activities. It’s one of those places where you can arrive knowing absolutely no one and somehow end up spending the whole night with a group of strangers who don’t feel like strangers anymore. Overall, I’d definitely recommend staying at Zostel at least once — even if it’s just for a day — to experience the community, meet new people, and get a taste of that fun, spontaneous travel vibe. Would definitely come back! ❤️

Staying for 14 days gave me enough time to experience the property, meet different people, and really feel comfortable and at home. One of the best things about staying here is the opportunity to meet and interact with new people from different places, making the stay even more memorable. The staff members are extremely friendly, helpful, and professional. A special mention goes to Monin Khan garu, Praveen, and VC Pooja, who were always approachable, supportive, and ensured that guests felt comfortable throughout my stay. Their hospitality was exceptional and truly made my 14-day stay even more enjoyable. A special appreciation goes to VC Pooja, who planned multiple activities and games during my stay. These activities were a great way to meet people, have fun, and create wonderful memories. I enjoyed participating in all the games, but Mafia was definitely my favorite! Thank you, Pooja, for all your efforts and for making my stay even more memorable. Praveen was also very good at planning trekking activities and different trips, which made the stay even more exciting and enjoyable. His efforts helped us explore new places, spend quality time together, and create some really good memories during my time at Zostel. The food was another highlight of my stay. Chef Naidu prepared delicious meals with amazing taste and quality. A special mention for his fish curry — I absolutely loved it! Every dish was flavorful and made with great care, and his cooking definitely added to the overall experience. Overall, Vizag Zostel offers an excellent combination of comfort, hospitality, community, food, activities, and convenience. I highly recommend it to solo travelers, backpackers, working professionals, and anyone looking for a friendly and enjoyable place to stay. My 14-day stay was truly memorable, and I’m grateful to Monin Khan garu, Praveen, VC Pooja, Chef Naidu, and the entire Zostel team for all their efforts in making my stay so special. My stay at Five Elements Hotel was unfortunately a very disappointing experience. On the day of arrival, we were provided two rooms as per our booking. While the rooms themselves were just about average, the air-conditioning in the second room was not working. We immediately reported the issue, but the staff initially seemed reluctant to change the room and were also unable to resolve the AC problem. Only after repeated follow-ups and considerable persistence was another room finally provided. The dining experience was equally disappointing. During breakfast, most of the spread was empty and we had to specifically ask for almost everything, as very little was readily available. Lunch was even more frustrating. Despite having a menu, most of the items we requested were apparently unavailable. We asked for something as basic as dal fry and rice, but even that could not be provided. Eventually, they somehow managed to serve us khichdi and egg bhurji. However, the most uncomfortable and irritating part of the entire stay was the constant expectation and repeated requests for tips. Almost every interaction seemed to involve someone asking for a tip: housekeeping staff, waiters, reception personnel and even managerial staff. Being repeatedly asked for tips throughout the stay made the entire experience extremely unpleasant and unprofessional. Overall, the poor handling of the room issue, limited food availability, disappointing breakfast service and, above all, the persistent requests for tips made this a very bad experience for us. I would not recommend Five Elements Hotel based on my experience, and I personally would not consider staying here again.

Oberoi, Bangalore. We visited the hotel for breakfast on a weekend and were prepared to dine as paying customers. To our surprise, we were denied entry because we were not staying at the hotel. This was particularly shocking for a property that is widely regarded as one of Bangalore’s premier luxury hotels. What made the situation even more disappointing was that it was only after we requested to speak with a manager that the conversation changed. The staff member at the front desk informed us that in her two years at the hotel, no one had ever asked to come for breakfast on a weekend without being a resident guest. We found that response quite baffling, as welcoming diners who wish to experience a hotel’s restaurants is standard practice at many leading luxury hotels around the world. Eventually, a table was arranged for us, and we were allowed to dine. However, by that point, the experience had already left a sour impression. The issue was not whether a table was ultimately provided, but the feeling of being unwelcome from the moment we arrived. Luxury hospitality is not defined solely by beautiful properties or excellent food. It is defined by how guests are treated. Unfortunately, our interaction at The Oberoi fell far short of the warmth, grace, and hospitality that the brand is known for. I hope management reviews this experience and ensures that future guests, whether hotel residents or local patrons, are welcomed with the same courtesy and professionalism one would expect from a hotel of this calibre.

A well-lit workspace, reliable high-speed internet, and ergonomic seating created an ideal setting for long hours of preparation, virtual meetings, and correspondence. Large windows invited natural light during the day, while the evenings offered a calm, ambient atmosphere that made unwinding effortless after a full day of engagements. What stood out consistently was the attentiveness of the service. The staff operated with quiet precision—always courteous, always efficient, and remarkably perceptive. Requests were handled promptly, often before they had the chance to become urgent. This level of responsiveness removed the small frictions that can accumulate during business travel, allowing me to remain focused on my work. Dining at the hotel became an integral part of the routine. Early breakfasts were well-organized and timely, catering perfectly to packed schedules. The variety and quality ensured that even on the busiest mornings, there was a sense of nourishment rather than haste. Evenings, when time allowed, offered a more relaxed dining experience—an opportunity to decompress while enjoying thoughtfully prepared meals in a setting that encouraged quiet reflection. Over the course of the ten days, the hotel revealed its greatest strength: consistency. Each day unfolded with the same level of care, cleanliness, and professionalism. Housekeeping maintained impeccable standards, ensuring that returning to the room always felt like stepping into a refreshed and orderly space. This reliability created a subtle but powerful sense of stability amidst the unpredictability of business commitments. There was also a distinct sense of privacy and discretion throughout the property—an essential quality for any business traveler. Whether in common areas or within the room, the environment supported both focus and rest without distraction. As the stay came to an end, it became clear that The Elanza Hotel had done more than provide accommodation—it had functioned as a dependable extension of the workplace, while still preserving the comforts of a well-appointed retreat. It allowed for productivity without strain, and relaxation without excess. In the context of a demanding business trip, such a balance is not merely appreciated—it is remembered.

text_light: We stayed here with my husband and our 4-year-old son. The location is probably the best thing about this place. It is right next to Garuda Mall, close to Cubbon Park and Commercial Street, and the metro is nearby. It was very easy to get around, and the rooms were also nicely designed. Unfortunately, we had some serious concerns with cleanliness. I noticed one cockroach in our room, which I could have ignored as an isolated incident. But during breakfast, I picked up a bowl and found a cockroach inside it. After that, I started wiping the bowls and plates before using them, especially since I was travelling with a young child. The bigger concern was the cold milk at breakfast. My son found the food a little spicy and asked for milk. Since the hot milk was too hot, I poured some cold milk into a bowl first and noticed very tiny, worm-like larvae moving in the milk. I was honestly shocked. What scared me most was thinking that if I had put cornflakes or Chocos in the bowl first and then poured the milk, I might not have noticed them and could have unknowingly consumed them. I’ve stayed at many hotels, and this was a first for me. The property itself has a lot going for it, especially the location and rooms. But pest control, cleanliness of utensils and proper food checks really need attention. With these things improved, this could be a really good place to stay.

text_light: The hotel’s online check-in process seems pointless. They require you to upload all your documents, email addresses, phone numbers, and other details in advance, yet during check-in they spend another 20–30 minutes collecting the exact same information. To make matters worse, they insist on obtaining the email address of every guest, which feels like unnecessary data collection rather than a genuine operational requirement. The rooms are spacious, but the bedding is extremely poor from an ergonomic standpoint. The mattress was so uncomfortable that it caused significant back discomfort. We requested either a room change or a replacement bed, but both requests were declined. Instead, the hotel provided an extra mattress so we could sleep on the floor, which was the only way we could get a comfortable night’s sleep. The work chair in the room was equally uncomfortable. We also requested that it be replaced with the chair from an unoccupied room, but that request was refused as well. Overall, while the rooms are large, the inefficient check-in process, excessive collection of personal information and the hotel’s unwillingness to address basic comfort issues made for a disappointing stay.

text_light: I had a very disappointing experience at Olive Richmond Circle. I was a solo traveller from Mumbai and had pre-booked my stay in advance, clearly selecting and paying for a specific room. However, when I arrived at around 11:45 PM I was told that the room I had paid for was not available. With no real option at that hour, I was forced to accept a tiny, box-like room for the night. Trying to be understanding, I agreed to adjust for 24 hours — but things only got worse. During the night, I discovered bed bugs in the room. At around 2 AM, I had to rush to reception and request another room. Surprisingly, the next room they gave me was exactly the one I had originally booked which raises the question. why wasn’t it given to me in the first place? Unfortunately, the issues didn’t end there. In that room, I found something extremely disturbing 30–50 dead honeybees stuffed behind a cupboard…clearly showing a complete lack of cleaning and hygiene. At that point, I requested a refund and wanted to leave, but the hotel refused to refund me. Instead, I was shifted yet again to another room. Even after finally getting a decent room, the service remained poor: No basic amenities like water, bucket, etc were provided unless I called repeatedly (10+ times) WiFi was unstable / AC was not working constantly disconnecting Staff seemed untrained and unhelpful Overall, this was a very, very bad experience. The property does not live up to its photos or ratings. The only positive is the location. Everything else was extremely disappointing. I would strongly advise others to not rely on the online ratings and be cautious before booking.

Clean and quiet stay, but watch out for the stairs and extension fees ​I booked a Double Deluxe AC room yesterday at 9 AM for a standard 12 PM to 12 PM slot, at a total cost of ₹1,700. I ended up arriving at 5 PM for check-in and was assigned a penthouse room located above the 6th floor. Keep in mind that the lift only goes up to the 6th floor, so you have to take the stairs to reach the top. ​The room itself was a highlight—neat, clean, and offering a completely silent atmosphere, which was great for relaxing. It was also a very welcome touch to have comforting, authentic Kerala food available. ​On the downside, when I asked for a brief 2-hour extension past the 12 PM check-out, I was asked to pay an extra ₹500, which felt a bit steep. Overall, a clean and peaceful place, but be aware of the top-floor accessibility and strict late-checkout fees.

Although the hotel is in the Majestic area, which can be quite busy and crowded, it is situated in what I would consider one of the better locations within Majestic. Anand Rao Circle is nearby, and the hotel is conveniently positioned for getting around Bangalore. Most major parts of the city can be reached fairly easily by cab, and the Bangalore Metro is also accessible, making the hotel particularly convenient for both business and leisure travellers. The rooms were clean, comfortable and surprisingly spacious, even in the base category. The bathrooms are decent and well maintained, and the air conditioning worked well. The standard room also has a proper work desk, two single sofas and a tea table, which gives you enough space whether you’re travelling for business or simply want to relax in the room. Housekeeping was also good. The room was cleaned every day and the overall cleanliness of the property was maintained well. But for me, the best part of this hotel is the food. The breakfast buffet was genuinely good, with a decent variety and good quality. I also ordered food to my room on a few occasions, and the food was consistently good. Another nice feature is the bar on the ground floor. It has a good selection of alcoholic beverages, along with some good food options and a few combinations that are worth trying. It is a convenient place to unwind in the evening without having to leave the hotel. I also noticed something that I really appreciated about the food service. The chef is frequently around the restaurant, talking to guests and asking for feedback. That personal interaction is a nice touch and shows that there is someone genuinely interested in knowing what guests think about the food and service. There is, however, one area where I feel the hotel could improve — the check-in experience for guests who book online. When I arrived for check-in, the first question from the front desk was whether I had booked online or directly. When I said online, I was simply told, without much warmth or even a smile, that check-in is at 12 noon. I understand that hotels have policies and cannot always accommodate early check-in, but the way the information is communicated makes a difference. A more welcoming approach from the front desk would definitely improve the first impression. Interestingly, if you book directly with the hotel, they offer a 24-hour check-in/check-out arrangement, which can be a significant advantage depending on your travel schedule. So this is something I would recommend travellers clarify before booking. Overall, I had a good experience at I V Sanctum. It is a clean, comfortable and reasonably priced 3-star hotel in a very convenient part of Bangalore. The central location, spacious base rooms, good housekeeping and especially the quality of the food make it a good value-for-money option. With a little more warmth and hospitality at the front desk, particularly during check-in, the overall guest experience could be even better. Overall, a good hotel, a great location within Majestic, and very good food for the price. I would consider staying here again.

We stayed at the GRT’s Lotus Apartment Hotel on Burkit Road, Chennai (A higher end serviced apartment) We were told the other 2 locations close by have been closed down because they were developed on leased properties. There is car parking available within the property, however it’s NOT covered. The Chennai heat can make your car super hot like a furnace if you park for 30 minutes also & then move out The staff right from the security guard (Mr. Mohan) to reception staff (Ms Mozhi & Ms Shobhana Devi) were extremely cordial. Right from checking into the place to leaving, all of them always had a smile & were pleasant to help us when needed & also assisted in giving us right directions to places we enquired about. The room that we checked into was a Junior Suite room & was extremely neatly maintained. The AC n fan is something you can’t do without in Chennai any time of the year. The room has a small kitchenette with a small refrigerator which was a great help to keep fruits fresh that we had carried along. There is no option to open windows and let fresh air in. The house-keeping staff will take time to attend but did a good job & provided us with anything asked for. The place has a small eat out area for the morning breakfast which can seat about 15-20 people only at a time & it is open between 7:30 AM & 10:30 AM only. Any other meal or food has to be ordered from outside to be delivered by Swiggy or Zomato which was clearly informed to us at the reception too when we checked in. The area was kept very clean during breakfast time & everything was extremely tasty & well made, except the idlies. We were confident that the idly would be the safest bet to have in Chennai, however that was not to be. The Upma, the live counter for dosa & omelette, the chutney’s, sambar, the bread, the sweets, fruits & beverages made up for not so good idli. Overall I would rate The Lotus Apartment Hotel a ‘5 on 5’

We reached Saravana Golden Fruits after midnight, having just landed in Chennai, exhausted from a long journey. Instead of a warm welcome, we were met by a receptionist who was overtly grumpy and made us feel as though we were being processed for a crime rather than checked into a hotel we had paid full price for. This is not a reflection on the individual alone, it is squarely a management failing. Staff dealing with late-night arrivals should be trained to welcome, assist and guide tired guests, not left to take out their frustrations on them. The rooms themselves were dirty and carried a persistent smell of damp. The air conditioning unit appeared never to have been cleaned since installation, switching it on sent visible clouds of dust into the room, the very air we were meant to be breathing. Hospitality is not a luxury add-on when guests are paying full price for it; it is the basic service being promised. On every count - cleanliness, maintenance and guest care, this hotel falls well short of any 3 or 4 star standard. We will not be returning, and I would strongly advise others to look elsewhere.

text_light: Comfortable stay in a convenient location ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Had a pleasant stay at The Saibaba Hotel in T. Nagar, Chennai. The hotel was clean, comfortable, and well maintained. The staff were generally friendly and helpful, and the location was very convenient for shopping, restaurants, and getting around Chennai. One area that could be improved is the customer service at the breakfast area. It would be great to have a slightly more customer-centric approach, especially towards guests who are still enjoying their breakfast within the stated breakfast hours. For example, breakfast is available until 10:00 AM, so guests who enter at 9:30 AM should still be able to enjoy their meal comfortably. While I understand that the service ends at 10:00 AM, switching off the air-conditioning and TV immediately at closing time can make guests feel a little rushed or uncomfortable. A little more attention to guest comfort and hospitality in the breakfast area would make the overall experience even better. Overall, it was a good stay and I would consider staying here again on my next visit to Chennai.

⭐ 1/5 – Extremely Disappointing Stay. Terrible Hygiene, Poor Maintenance and Unacceptable Facilities Our stay at K11 Hotels on Sarojini Road was an extremely disappointing and unpleasant experience. The rooms were very dirty, and the bedsheets had what appeared to be bloodstains. The hygiene was so poor that we did not even feel comfortable eating in the room. The toilet flush was not working at all. Although the staff attempted to repair it twice, the issue remained completely unresolved. My mother found it extremely difficult to use the toilet and suffered a lot of discomfort because of this. It was unacceptable that such a basic facility was not functioning. To make matters worse, the bathroom water was brown in colour, and the toilet bowl had visible stains. The entire hotel had an unpleasant stench, making the stay even more unbearable. Despite having No Smoking signs displayed inside the hotel, the corridors smelled strongly of cigarette smoke. This added to the already terrible environment and raised further concerns about the hotel's cleanliness and maintenance. For a room costing INR 3,800 per night, we expected much better standards of hygiene, maintenance, and basic facilities. The hotel seriously needs to improve its housekeeping and ensure that rooms are properly inspected before being given to guests. My advice to anyone considering booking this hotel: Please inspect the room thoroughly before confirming your booking or making payment. Do not rely solely on the pictures shown online. This was an extremely unpleasant experience, especially considering the difficulties my mother had to endure. I will definitely never book this hotel again, and I would not recommend it to anyone looking for a clean, hygienic, and comfortable stay.

I booked this hotel because I was looking for something around T. Nagar, and the pictures and reviews online looked quite promising. Unfortunately, the actual experience was very different. When we arrived, we were told that the full amount had to be paid before we could even check in. I had requested to pay an advance and the balance later, but that was refused. Since it was already close to 9 PM, we didn’t have much choice and went ahead with the payment. I had specifically booked a twin-sharing room. The moment we entered, we were taken aback by how small it was. The door opens almost directly onto the bed, with the bathroom immediately opposite one of the beds. The AC also didn’t work properly initially, and when we increased the fan speed, it made such a loud noise that it was impossible to sleep. To make matters worse, the towel provided was of such poor quality that it was practically impossible to dry ourselves with it. The next day, we requested a larger room and, thankfully, the person at reception accommodated our request. However, the new room was only marginally bigger, and the bathroom was still quite disappointing. We also noticed small cockroaches in the room, which was extremely unpleasant and raised serious concerns about the overall hygiene. At this point, I’m honestly just hoping I don’t end up carrying any unwanted “souvenirs” back home. The photographs online are, in my opinion, extremely misleading and make the rooms appear much more spacious and pleasant than they actually are. There is also no restaurant within the hotel, so you have to step out for food or anything else you may need. Another major issue is the smell of cigarette smoke throughout the hotel, which was particularly unpleasant. But the worst part of our stay was the noise at night. Guests in other rooms were extremely loud, and we could barely sleep. This continued until around 2 AM. We requested the hotel to intervene, and although we were told they would look into it, the noise continued. It was disappointing that the hotel staff did not proactively address the disturbance. The one positive thing I can say is that the person at reception was courteous and reasonably accommodating, especially when we requested a change of room. Overall, though, I would not recommend this hotel. The misleading photographs, tiny rooms, poor bathroom experience, cockroaches and hygiene concerns, cigarette smell, lack of an in-house restaurant and, most importantly, the lack of proper attention to guests’ comfort at night made this a very disappointing stay.

One of the Worst Hotel Experiences I’ve Had in Chennai Boulevard by Design Hotel, Chennai — DO NOT GO BY THE PHOTOS OR THE RATING. Pls read this review and take your decision carefully. Honestly, this was an extremely disappointing stay. From the moment I entered the room, it felt like a dirty, shady budget hotel that desperately needs maintenance and basic hygiene. ROOM — TERRIBLE The room was stinking badly the moment we entered. To make things worse, there were mice/rodents in the room. Yes, you read that correctly. The mice kept making noises throughout the night, making it almost impossible to sleep. No kettle for tea/coffee — a basic facility that you expect in a hotel of this category. No proper handwash in the bathroom. Instead, they had basic/desi soap. No hot water, which is simply unacceptable for a hotel charging what it does. Overall cleanliness and maintenance were far below what you would expect. The room clearly needs serious pest control and renovation. The entire experience was uncomfortable from the minute we entered until I checked out. LOCATION / VIEW — YOU GET A CONSTRUCTION SITE Don't expect any meaningful "view" from the room. Our window opened to a construction site, with JCBs, dumpers and construction activity right outside. Not exactly the relaxing hotel experience you expect. BREAKFAST — COLD & DISAPPOINTING Breakfast was another major letdown. Almost everything was cold. Very limited variety. Nothing seemed freshly prepared or properly maintained at serving temperature. The selection was so poor that even a small 2-star hotel can offer a better breakfast spread. For a hotel charging a premium, this breakfast was nowhere close to acceptable. OVERALL EXPERIENCE The biggest problem is that this hotel seems to have a huge gap between what it appears to be online and what you actually experience after checking in. A hotel room should at the very least be: clean + hygienic + pest-free + basic amenities + hot water + peaceful enough to sleep. This hotel failed on multiple basic expectations. Mice in the room, foul smell, no hot water, no handwash, no kettle, cold breakfast and a construction-site view — that's not a premium hotel experience. I strongly recommend potential guests to read the recent negative reviews carefully before booking and not blindly rely on the overall rating or photographs. For the price being charged, there are far better options in Chennai. Would I stay here again? Absolutely NOT. Would I recommend it to others? Definitely NOT. If a good night's sleep is important to you, think twice and about the Mice before booking this hotel.

The rooms are clean, decent and reasonably comfortable. However, the bathrooms are quite small and congested. The overall property, including the dining area, feels rather cramped, messy and poorly ventilated at peak hours despite the restaurant does manage to cater to a relatively large number of guests. One positive aspect was the staff support. The majority of the differently abled staff I interacted with were extremely polite, hardworking and genuinely helpful. Their attitude was commendable. Unfortunately, my experience with the front desk was a major disappointment. The front-desk officers I interacted with were unpleasant and displayed very poor communication and customer-service skills. My booking was mishandled and I received an email indicating that cancellation had been initiated. Despite having this evidence, the matter was subsequently denied rather than being handled transparently. More importantly, nobody had the courtesy to contact me directly, even though I was the person who had made the booking. The lack of coordination between staff and the messy booking process created completely unnecessary anxiety, particularly for someone travelling from another country for a business engagement. Booking issues can happen, but they should be resolved with clear communication, accountability and basic courtesy not with dismissive or disrespectful behaviour. I would also suggest greater transparency around the rates and deals displayed on the hotel website and booking platforms. The actual rates and offers can differ from what one may reasonably understand from the promotional photographs and deal listings, which can be misleading. Overall, the property has some positives, particularly clean rooms and hardworking staff, but customer-centred policies and front-desk service need significant improvement. Reasonable policies are important, but they should be implemented with flexibility, communication and respect for the guest. A hotel should never make a travelling guest feel that resolving a booking issue is an additional problem they have to fight through.

This hotel was ranking well on my list, and although the price was a little above my budget, I decided to go for it. Unfortunately, the stay came with quite a few issues. My colleague and I went to use the gym, but there was no gym attendant present. We walked in and used one of the machines, and as soon as I sat on the thigh lifter, a metal rod suddenly fell and hit me on my forehead. Thankfully, it wasn’t a serious injury, but it could have been much worse. What upset me more was the way the situation was handled afterwards. There was no immediate effort from the hotel staff to check what had happened. They did not even check the CCTV until I specifically asked them to. There was also no proper acknowledgement of the incident or any consideration of the issue while billing. For me, this is not about expecting special treatment or compensation. It is about basic courtesy, responsibility, and concern when a guest gets injured using a facility in the hotel. The other issues the small room, the AC problem, etc. could have been overlooked. But the way the gym incident was handled left a much worse impression than the actual problems with the stay. I chose this hotel despite it being slightly above my budget because of its good reviews and overall ranking. Unfortunately, the experience did not live up to those expectations.

Welcome to the Treebo experience, where taking your money is a high-speed sport, but returning it requires a sworn affidavit. They will happily snatch 50% of your cash upfront to secure your booking—efficiency at its finest! But the real magic happens when they owe you a refund. Suddenly, they develop selective amnesia. You are expected to formally "claim" your money back, as if they don't already have your bank details on a silver platter and the exact refund amount printed on *their own* voucher. It is a truly brilliant business model: play dumb, make the process as tedious as possible, and quietly pocket the cash when the exhausted customer finally forgets about it. Bravo. If you dare to follow up, you are treated to their absolute marvel of a customer support system. It is entirely WhatsApp-based and specifically engineered to make you lose your will to live. Prepare to be dazzled by a soulless auto-responder spitting out copy-pasted corporate drivel like, "This is not the outcome you desire," while doing absolutely nothing to actually assist you. If you enjoy funding accidental donations and being patronized by an algorithm, this is the place for you. Otherwise, do yourself a massive favor and stay as far away from this useless establishment as humanly possible.

We visited Ramada Hotel as a group of five for the buffet. The total cost was around ₹11,500, including taxes — approximately ₹2,300 per person. Unfortunately, the buffet spread was very disappointing for the price. The non-vegetarian options were extremely limited. There was only one chicken gravy, while most of the non-veg options were fish-based. The main disappointment was the basa fish. They served basa fish as the primary fish option, including fish 65 and fish gravy. For a premium hotel buffet at around ₹11,500 for five people, we expected much better seafood variety such as prawns, crab, and better fish options, along with more chicken dishes. Instead, a significant portion of the non-veg spread was based on basa fish, which felt like a very basic and cost-saving choice for a buffet at this price. For a hotel of this category, the menu variety was far below our expectations. Overall, we felt the buffet was not value for money and was a disappointing experience. ₹11,500 for five people with such a limited non-veg spread, especially with so much basa fish, was simply not worth it.

⭐ 1/5 — Extremely Disappointing Experience. Definitely NOT a 4-Star Hotel This was one of the most disappointing hotel experiences I have had. I am a businessman and travel frequently, so I am saying this after thinking carefully and comparing the level of service with what a hotel charging this kind of money should actually provide. The condition of the hotel is absolutely unacceptable for a property calling itself a 4-star hotel. The bathroom was not properly clean. The hair dryer was not working. The intercoms were not working properly. The service was extremely slow and frustrating. The doors were damaged and poorly maintained. Even the basic infrastructure looked neglected and poorly managed. The check-in process was ridiculously slow and unnecessarily time-consuming. After paying such a high amount, you expect a smooth and professional arrival experience — instead, it was another disappointment. And the breakfast was equally disappointing. The quality, variety and overall experience were nowhere close to what one would expect from a 4-star property. For the price being charged, this level of breakfast is simply unacceptable. Honestly, this hotel feels like it is charging 4-star prices while delivering a completely different level of service and maintenance. There is a huge gap between what they charge and what they actually provide. I strongly advise people to THINK TWICE before booking this hotel. Do not be impressed merely by the “4-star” tag. You are paying a premium price, but the experience does not justify it in any way. For the amount of money we were charged, I expected cleanliness, functioning facilities, prompt service, proper maintenance and professional hospitality. Unfortunately, almost every one of these basic expectations was missed. This hotel is, in my opinion, a serious disappointment and the “4-star” label is extremely misleading when compared with the actual experience. Very poor maintenance. Very poor service. Poor cleanliness. Poor check-in experience. Poor breakfast. Broken/defective facilities. Overall: HIGH PRICE + LOW QUALITY + POOR SERVICE = A HOTEL I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TO ANYONE. If you value your money and expect a proper 4-star experience, I would strongly recommend considering other options instead.

Terrible Experience I have stayed at this hotel with my family on several occasions because of its convenient location near the international airport while traveling. Unfortunately, this was one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had. The problems started even before check-in. No one seemed to take responsibility for confirming the accommodation. I had to make at least four different calls just to get basic confirmation, and even then, there was no clear or reliable response. Upon arrival, there was hardly any welcome or assistance from the hotel staff, except for the valet drivers at the entrance. The condition of the room was extremely disappointing. There was a strong, unpleasant smell, dirty sheets, used amenities, only one coffee cup, and uncleared garbage bins. The bathroom was equally problematic. If you enjoy showering under a waterfall, then you might appreciate their shower — the water flows above and around the showerhead rather than properly through it. On top of that, the water took more than 10 minutes to drain. The housekeeping and maintenance standards were extremely poor, and it honestly felt as though there was no proper supervision or inspection of the rooms. I found empty cigarette packets inside the wardrobe, and the electronic safe was not working. The condition of the corridors was also unacceptable. Several areas had leaking ceilings, a persistent bad odour, and visible signs of water seepage. The overall appearance of the corridors and affected rooms was terrible and clearly in need of proper maintenance. The in-house restaurant was another major disappointment. The customer service was poor, and the food quality was equally disappointing. Room service was practically non-existent. Despite having a room service menu, they were unable to provide most of the listed items and could offer only a few South Indian tiffin options. Even basic snacks and juices were unavailable at around 7 PM when I needed something for my children. Shockingly, we were advised to order food through Swiggy or Zomato instead. For a hotel charging around ₹5,000, this is simply unacceptable. Overall, the entire experience — from the reservation and check-in to the room, housekeeping, maintenance, corridors, restaurant, and room service — was extremely disappointing. For the price we paid, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, service, and hospitality. I will definitely not be staying at this hotel again, and based on this experience, I cannot recommend it to anyone.

Very Disappointing Experience!!!! I had a very bad experience at this hotel and would not recommend it to others. I booked the hotel for one day and, before making the reservation, I clearly informed the staff that I needed an early-morning check-in and would be checking out the following morning. I also specifically asked about the check-out time. The person at the reception who handled my reservation informed me that the normal check-out time was 10:00 AM, with a maximum extension until 11:00 AM, and assured me that, in my case, I could check out by 8:00 AM without any additional payment. I checked in as agreed. However, the first room I was given was in an unacceptable condition. There were used plates and glasses in the wash basin, the bed did not have a proper bedsheet, and the room had an unpleasant smell. I immediately complained to the reception, after which they apologized and changed my room. The basic room amenities were also not provided initially. I had to repeatedly request them from the staff, which was very inconvenient. The next morning, at around 7:30 AM, a room boy came to my room and asked whether I was ready to check out. I told him that I would be ready in about 15 minutes. At approximately 7:50 AM, I reached the reception to complete the check-out process. At this point, a different receptionist was on duty. To my surprise, he informed me that I had to pay for another full day because, according to him, I had checked in early and was checking out late. I explained that the person who had handled my reservation had clearly told me that I could stay until 8:00 AM without any additional charge. Instead of addressing the issue professionally, the receptionist became extremely rude and started shouting at me. He repeatedly stated that he was the manager and that he had no knowledge of the earlier agreement. He refused to contact the staff member who had made my reservation, despite my repeated requests. The situation became even more concerning when he locked the sliding entrance door while I was inside and told me that I would not be allowed to leave unless I made the payment. I found this behavior completely unacceptable and intimidating. I questioned why I should have to pay a full day's room charge for only a short additional period. Eventually, after a heated argument, he agreed to accept ₹1,000 as an additional payment, which I paid in order to resolve the situation and leave. What upset me even more was that he then told the room boy that if I did not make the payment, the amount would be deducted from the room boy's salary. I felt very sorry for the employee, who appeared to have no involvement in the issue. Overall, the experience was extremely disappointing—from the poor condition of the room and lack of basic amenities to the way the check-out dispute was handled. The surrounding area of the hotel was also poorly maintained and unclean. I strongly recommend that management look into this incident, particularly the conduct of the receptionist who was on duty that morning. Clear communication between shifts and proper adherence to the commitments made during booking would have prevented this entire situation. I would strongly advise anyone considering this hotel to confirm the check-in and check-out terms in writing before booking, especially if an early check-in or early check-out is involved.

However as soon as we stepped out of the lift any concerns we may have had disappeared. The reception area is clean and modern and the team are welcoming. Our room was very spacious, clean and comfortable. We had a twin room and the beds were very comfortable. There was loads of space to store stuff, so we could keep our room tidy. There was a kettle to make tea and coffee plus a big work top and extra sink, which I guess would be helpful if you wanted to order food deliveries. We had 2 chairs and a coffee table which were useful for sitting watching TV in the evening. The room had a smart TV and we were able to watch a movie on Amazon Prime. Air con and fans were efficient and welcome after the heat of Chennai. Bathroom was spacious and had a great shower with plenty of hot water. Location may not be in the prettiest area of Chennai but it is easy to get around with auto rickshaws. Added bonus is the Express Mall, just a 10 minute walk from hotel. Lots of shops, Smart Bazaar supermarket, some restaurants and a food court. It was also quiet at night so we were able to sleep well. All in all we really enjoyed our 5 night stay. Big thank you to Krishna and the team for looking after us. Highly recommended.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Had a pleasant stay at La Woods hotel, Chennai. The rooms are spacious, clean, and well-maintained, with a comfortable and spacious bed. The bathroom was also clean and hygienic, and all the basic amenities, including water bottles and other essentials, were provided. The check-in process was smooth, and the property is well-lit with a pleasant ambience. The staff were courteous and helpful, and overall, the service was good. One of the highlights of our stay was the complimentary breakfast. It was a buffet with a good variety of options, and we particularly liked that items such as puris, dosas, etc. were prepared fresh and served hot. The breakfast was definitely a nice addition to the stay. However, there were a few areas that could be improved. We had an issue with the shower and requested a bucket and mug, but we had to follow up two to three times before they were provided. There was also a slight mix-up with our in-room dining order. Another significant issue was the air conditioning. The room felt quite warm despite setting the AC to 18°C, which was the lowest temperature available. Since there was no fan or alternative cooling option, the room remained uncomfortable at times. Improving the AC/cooling system would make a noticeable difference to the overall guest experience. Apart from these issues, we had a good and comfortable stay. The cleanliness, spacious rooms, breakfast, ambience, and courteous staff were all positives. With a little more attention to service coordination, the overall experience could be even better.

Disappointing Stay Despite a Good Location The hotel has a good location, but unfortunately, my stay was quite disappointing. I encountered several basic cleanliness, hygiene, and maintenance issues during my stay: 1. Stains on the bedsheets. 2. Water leakage in the toilet. 3. The toilet water gun/jet spray was not working. 4. No handwash or shower gel was provided. 5. The room intercom was not working. As a result, every time I needed assistance, I had to go downstairs to the reception to speak with the hotel staff. 6. I was allotted a room on the 4th floor, but the lift only goes up to the 3rd floor. I had to use the stairs from the 3rd to the 4th floor, including while carrying my luggage. 7. Rats were running around in the kitchen area, which was particularly concerning from a hygiene perspective. 8. The kitchen/breakfast area was not properly cleaned. 9. The dining space is extremely small and uncomfortable. I requested an alternative room, but I was informed that no other room was available. The location is definitely a plus, but considering the condition of the room, cleanliness, hygiene, and overall facilities, I feel this property is worth around ₹1,000–₹1,300 per night at most. If the room is priced significantly higher than that, I would not recommend staying here. I would also strongly recommend skipping the breakfast at this property. There are several good restaurants nearby that generally open around 7:00 AM, and in my experience, it would be better to have breakfast outside rather than pay extra for breakfast at this hotel. Overall, the location is good, but the property needs significant improvement in terms of cleanliness, hygiene, maintenance, pest control, room facilities, and breakfast arrangements. In view of the hygiene concerns observed in the kitchen and breakfast area, I would also respectfully request the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to kindly inspect the food preparation and kitchen facilities of this property and verify whether the applicable food safety, hygiene, sanitation, and pest-control standards are being properly maintained. I hope the hotel management and Agoda Company Pte. Ltd. take these concerns seriously and take appropriate corrective measures to provide a cleaner, safer, and more hygienic experience for future guests.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ We absolutely love GRT and its services! The staff hospitality, food, cleanliness, and overall service have always been amazing. They have never let us down. We have been regular customers since 2017, and that itself says how much we love GRT and the entire team. ❤️ However, I do have one disappointment that I hope the management will consider, especially for regular customers. We were supposed to arrive early morning on 22nd September at around 5 AM with our 2-year-old daughter. When I made our reservation from London, around five months before our trip, I asked about early check-in. I was told that it could not be guaranteed, but that once we arrived or closer to the date, the hotel would see what they could do. Based on that assurance, I decided to book the room starting from 21st September, even though we were still in London and had not even departed. I was willing to pay for an extra night because I trusted that the hotel would try to help us as regular customers. Unfortunately, when I asked about this later, I was told that nothing could be done—not even a small discount or consideration for the unused portion of the booking. This was quite disappointing, particularly because we have been loyal customers since 2017. I completely understand that hotel policies and room availability have to be considered. At the same time, I feel that long-standing regular customers could perhaps be given some flexibility or goodwill in situations like this, especially when travelling with a small child. Having said that, I still genuinely love GRT and the entire team. ❤️ The food, cleanliness, hospitality, and service are consistently excellent, and we have always enjoyed our stays. I’m sharing this feedback because we truly value GRT and hope the management will consider offering a little more flexibility to loyal, returning customers in situations like ours. 🙏

If you're looking for a clean, affordable, and super-friendly stay near Pondy Bazaar in Chennai, Itsy Delux Inn is an absolute winner. My recent visit left me impressed, and I'll be returning without a doubt! From the check-in process, the staff stood out with their warmth and attentiveness. They greeted us with genuine smiles and went above and beyond—allowing us to drop off our luggage hours before official check-in time and even letting us use the room to freshen up and change after checkout when our next plans were delayed. This level of flexibility and hospitality is rare and truly appreciable, especially for travelers juggling tight schedules. The rooms are compact (perfect for short business trips or quick getaways), but what they lack in size, they make up for in spotless cleanliness and freshness. Everything smelled amazing—no musty odors or dust anywhere. Amenities were spot-on: a reliable AC to beat Chennai's heat, a functional TV with good channels, and a small but efficient toilet with basic toiletries. The beds were comfy, and housekeeping kept things impeccable throughout our stay. Breakfast was complimentary and a decent start to the day, featuring South Indian classics like steaming hot upma and fluffy idlis with chutney and sambar. Options were limited (no variety like dosas or continental items), but it was fresh, filling, and hassle-free—no need to step out early. Location-wise, it's ideally tucked near Pondy Bazaar, making shopping, street food, and local sights a breeze. Parking was available if needed, and the overall vibe felt safe and convenient. In short, Itsy Delux Inn delivers excellent value for money with top-notch staff service and pristine rooms. Super place for Pondy Bazaar or Chennai visits—I've already bookmarked it for my next trip! 5/5 stars – Highly recommended for budget-conscious travelers seeking comfort and kindness.

The next day, I requested an extension of only 4 hours and even offered to pay an additional ₹1,000. However, the receptionist refused and insisted that I pay another ₹1,800, which was almost the full room tariff again. What disappointed me most was not the charge itself, but the way I was treated. I waited at the reception for nearly 45 minutes, politely explaining my situation and requesting some consideration. There was absolutely no flexibility or willingness to help. To make matters worse, I noticed that another guest who had checked in early in the morning was allowed to stay until around 11:00 AM the next day while paying only one day's tariff. This made the treatment seem inconsistent and unfair. The receptionist's attitude was rude and unprofessional. Instead of explaining the hotel policy respectfully, I was told words to the effect of: "If you cannot pay the amount, why come to a hotel? Stay somewhere else. If you like it, stay; otherwise take your bag and leave." As a paying customer, I found this extremely disrespectful. I understand that hotels have policies, but guests should be treated with courtesy and professionalism. The room was acceptable, but the customer service at the reception was very poor. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the behavior and training of the front desk staff.

Hotel Grand Palace Coimbatore is a good hotel in terms of both services and locality. It is located in a market area, yet the surroundings and property are very clean, and it is easy to walk around and access nearby shops and facilities. The rooms were very spacious and clean, which made the stay comfortable. Toiletries were provided in the room, and the overall cleanliness was well maintained. The view from the window was also great, adding to the experience. The hotel operates across multiple floors and has a clean, properly working lift, which is convenient, especially for families and guests carrying luggage. The check-in and check-out process was smooth and did not take much time. One of the best things about the stay was the room service. The staff responded quickly, and the service was very good and efficient. Another convenient feature is the food arrangement. Guests are allowed to order food through online food delivery apps, which is always useful when you want more choices. The hotel also has food options available through nearby restaurants without charging any additional delivery or service fees, which is a thoughtful facility for guests. Overall, Hotel Grand Palace is a comfortable and well-maintained option for staying in Coimbatore. The spacious rooms, cleanliness, convenient location, smooth service and flexible food options make it a good choice for both short and longer stays.

I am currently staying at Park Plaza Coimbatore for one night, and unfortunately my experience has been very disappointing from the moment we arrived. As soon as we entered and enquired about a room for our family of four, the older gentleman at reception immediately told us that we could not stay in one room. We asked whether an extra bed could be added, but there was no willingness to help or discuss possible options. It felt more like an attempt to push us into booking two rooms rather than finding a reasonable solution. We were then shown rooms by a younger staff member. First, we saw a smaller room, followed by a Deluxe Room with a queen bed and a sofa bed. When we asked whether all four of us could stay there for just one night, the younger staff member politely said it should be fine. We explained that the receptionist downstairs had told us otherwise, so he went to clarify. We then overheard the reception staff saying, “Why did you show them that room?” which was both uncomfortable and highly unprofessional. The attitude of the older receptionist throughout our stay has been disappointing. He was cold, rude, dismissive, and completely lacking in basic hospitality skills. There was no warmth or welcoming attitude whatsoever. To make matters worse, we repeatedly requested extra pillows, bedsheets, and towels. My father personally asked several times, yet our requests were repeatedly dismissed and ignored. It should not be this difficult for paying guests to receive basic room amenities. The lack of responsiveness and courtesy only added to our frustration. The younger staff member we dealt with was polite and helpful, but unfortunately the behaviour of the receptionist overshadowed the entire experience. First impressions matter, and this hotel failed badly in that regard. There are many hotels in Coimbatore that value their guests and provide professional customer service. We will complete our one-night stay, but we will not be returning. Management seriously needs to address the attitude of certain front desk staff and provide proper customer service training, as the current standard is simply not acceptable.

The man at the reception told us that it was coming straight from the boiler and hence it would take time. I felt like the lone security guard sitting alone at the fag end of a goods train for sometime and then decided to shower up in cold water. The actuator on the health faucet wasn't working. I had to work with the tap to ensure it wouldn't splash everything with its pressure. The bathroom was so spacious and very clean and I absolutely loved it. The number 9 on the phone wasn't working. I was more than glad to do that since the room had enough and more room to run around and I gladly accepted it as exercise. My only recommendation to the management - get your folks to be a bit serious about the systems related to electricity and water. Overall, a very interesting experience.

Very Poor Experience – Serious Issues with Cleanliness, Location Information & Management Response We had a very disappointing stay at Arcadia. Unfortunately, except for its proximity to the airport, almost every aspect of our experience was unsatisfactory. The hotel location shown on Google was incorrect. It indicated that the hotel was opposite the medical college, so we travelled all the way there only to find that the hotel was not at that location. After asking several people, we understood that we had to travel back in the opposite direction, past KMCH. When we raised this issue at reception, the response from the person in charge was extremely poor. Instead of acknowledging the inconvenience caused by the incorrect location, he initially tried to defend it. Only after we spent considerable time explaining and proving the issue did he say that he would check it. It was surprising that such an important location error was either unknown to the management or had not been addressed. For first-time guests, incorrect directions can cause significant inconvenience, wasted time and unnecessary confusion. The cleanliness of the rooms was even more concerning. The room did not appear to have been properly cleaned. The pillows and bedsheets seemed to have been merely rearranged rather than replaced. Most seriously, the bed provided to us had a visible period blood stain that had not been cleaned. This is completely unacceptable for any hotel and raises serious concerns about basic hygiene standards. After complaining, we were moved to another room on a different floor. However, there was no responsible staff member available there to handle the issue; only the security guard was present to receive the complaint and communicate information regarding the room change. The intercom phone was not working, so for every requirement or complaint we had to physically go to reception. There was also a very unpleasant smell in the corridor, apparently due to poorly maintained or unclean floor mats outside the rooms. A housekeeping trolley carrying used linen and toiletries such as shampoo, soap, shaving and dental kits remained outside the room for much of the day, adding to the unpleasant smell and overall unhygienic environment. The food quality was also very poor. Pongal was extremely plain and seemed to contain little beyond cooked rice. The dosa and idli were disappointing, and the vada was excessively oily. Overall, the breakfast experience was well below expectations. At reception, lemon water was provided, but there were only used glasses available and no clean unused glasses. Even after we specifically requested a clean glass, one was not provided. Instead, the lemon-water container was eventually taken back to the pantry, with staff saying it was not good and therefore could not be served. Most disappointing was the lack of proper response and ownership from the management despite multiple concerns being raised. Overall, this was a very disappointing experience with serious shortcomings in cleanliness, hygiene, maintenance, food quality and customer service. The location near the airport is convenient, but that alone cannot compensate for such poor housekeeping and management standards. Very poor cleanliness and extremely disappointing management. Significant improvement is required before I could recommend this hotel to others. The room tariff is excessively high and completely unjustified for the standard of accommodation and service provided. The amount charged is comparable to, or even higher than, what one might expect at a 5-star hotel, but unfortunately, the service, cleanliness, maintenance and overall guest experience were of a very poor standard. At this price point, guests have every right to expect professional service, excellent hygiene and properly maintained rooms. What we experienced was nowhere close to the value expected for the amount charged. Extremely poor value for money and highly disappointing service.

Disappointing stay, especially for guests needing wheelchair assistance I booked the room for one night, and the booking experience itself was flawless. The person in charge was very helpful and patiently clarified all my doubts. I had specifically requested wheelchair access, and the hotel confirmed that it would be available. They also informed us that complimentary breakfast was included and explained that, since they don’t have a restaurant inside the property, breakfast would be arranged from Hotel Annapoorna next door. Unfortunately, the actual experience was very different. We reached the hotel around 10 PM and requested a wheelchair from the security person. He was completely clueless and asked us to check with reception, which was on the first floor. We were then told to take the wheelchair ourselves, with no staff member available to assist us. We somehow managed to get it, and the security person eventually brought it near the car. However, the wheelchair was very small and not in good condition. The elderly security person tried to push it towards the main entrance but struggled to do so. In the end, he had to walk/limp all the way to the first floor with us, which was honestly quite difficult to watch. Once we reached the first floor, the front desk assigned us a room that was at the far end from the lift. For someone with a fractured leg, walking that distance was extremely difficult. Considering that I had specifically informed the hotel about the wheelchair requirement in advance, I expected much better planning and assistance. Things got worse when we asked about dinner. We were simply told to manage it ourselves through Swiggy or Zomato. A few minutes later, at around 11 PM, we were asked to place our breakfast order for the next morning. We were then told that only one plate of breakfast would be complimentary and that any additional breakfast would be charged separately. We were quite surprised by this, especially when the booking was presented as including complimentary breakfast. We were also told that they could not even provide coffee or tea from outside. Overall, the booking process and initial communication were good, but the actual stay and service were a big disappointment. The hotel may be suitable for a basic overnight stay if you don't need much assistance, but I would not recommend it to anyone looking for good service, proper restaurant facilities, or reliable wheelchair accessibility. For guests with mobility issues, I would strongly suggest confirming not just wheelchair availability but also the condition of the wheelchair, staff assistance, room location and accessibility before booking.

My overall experience at Treebo Cornerstay, Coimbatore was below average. While the rooms were fairly spacious, the cleanliness and upkeep did not meet the standard I would expect for the price being charged. The towels and bedsheets were visibly dirty and stained, and the kitchen, refrigerator and toilet also required considerably better cleaning. Toilet paper was not provided, which was disappointing for a hotel of this category. Cleanliness and basic amenities are areas that need immediate attention. The breakfast experience was also disappointing. The idlis were half-cooked, while only basic tea and coffee were available. There is definitely room to improve the quality and preparation of the breakfast. Another concern was the parking and access to the property. Too many cars were parked around the porch, making it difficult to access an already narrow and relatively small entrance area. That said, I would like to specifically compliment Ms. Ruby and the young gentlemen at the front desk. They were polite, courteous and genuinely helpful whenever assistance was required. Their attitude and willingness to help were certainly a positive aspect of the stay. The booking process also needs improvement, particularly for reservations made through online booking platforms. The overall process could be made much smoother and more transparent. Overall, the property has potential, particularly with its spacious rooms and courteous staff, but cleanliness, maintenance, breakfast quality, parking/access and the booking process need significant improvement. The standard of cleanliness and service should be brought in line with the price being charged to provide guests with a more satisfactory experience.

text_light: I had a very disappointing experience staying at FabHotel Grand Gunas, RS Puram, Coimbatore. From the moment we arrived, the service was extremely poor. The hotel has steps at the entrance, and we had to carry all our luggage up the stairs ourselves while travelling with our children. Despite seeing us struggling with luggage and kids, none of the staff offered any assistance. The parking experience was also very inconvenient. The staff did not properly assist us with parking or guide us to a suitable parking spot. We also received no proper assistance in getting our luggage to the room. When we entered the room, there was a very strong and unpleasant cigarette/smoking smell. Since we were travelling with children, this was particularly uncomfortable, and we had to request a room change. Unfortunately, the replacement room also had issues. The AC was not functioning properly, and the room door did not have a proper locking system that gave us confidence about our safety at night. Overall, the lack of basic hospitality, assistance, cleanliness, and proper room facilities made this one of the most disappointing hotel stays I have experienced. I honestly did not expect this level of service from a hotel. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the staff service, room maintenance, parking assistance, and basic safety arrangements for future guests.

Key Concerns: - Location & Connectivity: The hotel is located near the back gate of Coimbatore Railway Station (Variety Hall Road). In my experience, bus and cab connectivity from this specific pocket was not very convenient for frequent, cost-effective travel across different parts of the city. If your work involves extensive daily field visits and you depend on public transport or quick app-based cabs, you may find the location less convenient. - Front Desk Communication: During check-in, one front-desk staff member insisted on full advance payment (around ₹50,000), despite my explaining a daily transaction limit on my corporate card. While the issue was resolved once I split the payments, the interaction was rigid and could have been handled with better hospitality. Fortunately, the other reception staff I interacted with throughout my stay were courteous and helpful. - Minor Disturbances: There was occasional noise due to ongoing renovation work, and the calling bell system in the room was not functioning properly during my stay. What Worked Well: - Dining & Hospitality: The breakfast restaurant team was excellent—courteous, attentive, and very welcoming, with good hot breakfast options. The food quality overall was good, and the rooms were spacious with a comfortable, dedicated work desk. - Parking & Checkout: 24/7 vehicle parking was available, and the checkout staff were cooperative in providing separate accommodation and food bills required for corporate reimbursement. Verdict: Overall, the hotel offers comfortable rooms, good food, and helpful service in most areas. It is a solid, practical option for railway travelers or guests using private transport. However, professionals who need convenient daily field travel across Coimbatore may wish to consider the location dynamics before booking.

text_light: A wonderful place in the heart of New Delhi ❤️ My daughter and I had a truly amazing stay. From the moment we arrived, we felt a beautiful energy. All the staff are lovely, incredibly friendly, and always willing to help, at any time. They made us feel very comfortable, cared for, and above all, safe. The hotel is gorgeous, with the charm of a true heritage palace: its lamps, windows, doors, details, and decor make every corner special. And the best part is that it's exactly as it looks in the photos. It's near Main Bazaar, amidst all the hustle and bustle, markets, and characteristic noise of Delhi, but the energy completely changes as soon as you enter the hotel. It's peaceful, cozy, and perfect for relaxing after a day exploring the city. And the breakfast… simply wonderful! 😍 Delicious and plentiful, with typical Indian options as well as more continental choices, such as fruit, omelets, and bread. The chai is spectacular, and the freshly ground coffee is delicious. ☕️ And I want to especially highlight the safety, because for us it was fundamental. Traveling as women, especially alone, makes choosing the right place to stay very important. Here we truly felt at ease, confident, and that we were in a place where we could return after exploring the city and simply relax. We feel very lucky to have found this place. If you are a woman traveling alone, with your daughter, or simply looking for a beautiful, authentic, safe, and peaceful hotel in New Delhi, I highly recommend it. I would happily return without hesitation. 5 stars and totally recommended.

I stayed for two nights at a guesthouse I found after searching around in Majnu Ka Tilla (MNT). MNT itself is like a maze of narrow alleys, but this one is even further down a small lane. I'm sure the guesthouse name is on the main street, but you'll probably miss it and walk right past it. You'll end up going all the way to the end, ask at a currency exchange office, and then walk back a little to find it. It's not that difficult, but at night it can be hard for first-timers to find. There's a Signature Cafe on the 5th floor with a view of the Signature Bridge over the Yamuna River, and the view and atmosphere are quite nice. The room I stayed in didn't have a window, and the TV happened to be broken, which were drawbacks, but the room itself, including the bathroom, was good. They also do laundry up to 5kg for 400rupiah, so you don't have to take it outside, which is nice. There's also a restaurant called Sumo Cafe attached, which I didn't go into. The female staff at the reception desk helped arrange a car from Nizamuddin, but due to the driver's complete lack of English skills, they spent a long time searching for him, becoming exhausted and ultimately unable to meet him. I managed to get by with an Uber, but I was grateful for their help. Also, perhaps by chance, the breakfast at the Signature Cafe, which was practically empty, was delicious. If I ever come back to Delhi, I would definitely like to stay there again.

I can honestly say that because of the staff at the Jaypee Siddarth, my husbands’s recovery was made so much easier. It does take the physiotherapist a few extra minutes to make it upstairs and past security though each day as the hotel does take the safety of its guests seriously. Nina is the most gracious & caring host we have ever stayed with. Her place is renowned over the years as a perfect home stay and having stayed there, we can say that it's the epitome of hospitality. There are a plethora of reasons of staying here & I'm listing a few of them below (not an exhaustive list) - Comfort & Convenience - Her place in Civil Lines is in close proximity to many of Delhi's major landmarks, Metro Stn & ISBT (Kashmere Gate). This made it a star attraction for us & many others. Yet, for those who are looking forward to a peaceful & tranquil stay, it offers that in equal measure too. Oberoi Apartments (erstwhile Curzon's House) is a nice, posh gated society and feels conveniently away from the hustle outside. We loved the verdant surroundings and a special mention for the peacocks & peahens that can be easily sighted inside the society premises. Room & Breakfast: The room was spacious and utilitarian & provided with all the amenities required for a comfortable stay.
