We stayed here for a total of four nights over the 2025 New Year's holiday. It was our first trip to India, as two women, but it was a wonderful accommodation and I would recommend it to Japanese people as well. The area around the accommodation was safe. (There were the occasional stray dogs, cats, and cows.) We never felt unsafe, even at 9 or 10 p.m. There were several restaurants nearby, so we had no trouble finding something to eat. There was also a metro station about a 10-minute walk from the accommodation, making transportation convenient. The room was fully heated, so we didn't feel cold at all, even in the middle of winter. A liter of drinking water was provided in our room every day. Bottled water was also provided, so we used it to wash our face and brush our teeth. For breakfast, we had a choice of multiple menu items. The staff were kind enough to serve us multiple menu items on several occasions. Chai, tea, or coffee was also provided each time, and the chai was especially delicious. The staff were friendly and kind from start to finish, and I felt very at ease throughout my stay. You can also contact them via WhatsApp, so I used that to let them know if I would be checking in late. One thing to note is that if you use a certain amount of hot water, it will turn into water, so be careful about how much you use. I let it out in small trickles. I would definitely stay here again!

Dharampur Haveli has done a wonderful job with its décor. The beautiful heritage setting genuinely reflects the old-world charm, culture and character of Chandni Chowk. The ambience is impressive, and the starters were genuinely very good. Unfortunately, that is where the experience largely ends. The Kathak performance was disappointing. It felt poorly trained and lacked the grace, precision and authenticity one expects from a classical Indian dance form. Perhaps it may appeal more to foreign tourists who are unfamiliar with Kathak, but for anyone who understands or appreciates the art, it was difficult to watch. The restaurant also needs to be much more transparent about its pricing. On Fridays and Saturdays, guests should be clearly informed before making a reservation that only a fixed menu is available at ₹4,500 per person plus taxes, with no à la carte option. This is a significant amount, and guests deserve to know exactly what they are signing up for. More disappointing, however, was the main course. The mutton and chicken dishes were simply not up to the mark. A restaurant that presents itself as a celebration of Purani Dilli’s culinary heritage should be able to showcase these dishes with far greater skill and authenticity. The cooking fell well below what one would expect at this price point. The desserts were an even bigger let-down. The mango kulfi tasted more like coloured ice than genuine kulfi, while the jalebi was thick, undercooked and lacked the crispness and character expected from a proper Old Delhi jalebi. In short, the heritage décor is excellent, but the food and performance do not justify the price. Dharampur Haveli has the setting, the history and the potential to offer a truly memorable Purani Dilli experience. But the kitchen and the entertainment need a serious overhaul. पुरानी दिल्ली की नाक कटवा दी। For a restaurant claiming to represent the culinary and cultural heritage of Purani Dilli, the food simply has to be much, much better.

Whenever I am in Delhi, I try to visit Old Delhi, taking any family and friends along too. And when exploring the Red Fort, Chandni Chowk and the lanes full of wedding finery, silver jewellery, stationery etc the Haveli Dharampura is the oasis in the desert, the calm in the storm. It is so good to slip in through the great wooden doors to a courtyard full of charm and the AC dining room beyond. Good welcome, good food and drink, good ambience. Thank you to everyone at the Haveli for your wonderful service 🙏

We recently stayed at **Hotel Bright** with our family and had a truly wonderful experience. This charming heritage-style hotel offers excellent value for money and is ideal for all kinds of travelers looking for a centrally located stay at a reasonable budget. The rooms were clean, comfortable, and well maintained, with quality bedding that ensured a restful night's sleep. The washrooms were spotless and hygienic, reflecting the hotel's commitment to cleanliness and guest comfort. Being a historic building from the British era, the property does not have a lift, so guests should be prepared to use the stairs. However, the hotel is exceptionally well maintained and upholds standards comparable to many internationally recognized 3-star hotels. The heritage character of the building adds to its unique charm and appeal. One suggestion for future guests: **if possible, request a room with a window when making your reservation, as the hotel has only a limited number of window rooms available.** We found the natural light and ventilation to enhance the overall stay experience. The location is one of Hotel Bright's greatest strengths. Situated in the heart of the city and surrounded by numerous restaurants, cafés, and bars, it offers easy access to dining, shopping, and many of Delhi's major attractions. A heartfelt **thank you to the entire Hotel Bright team** for their warm hospitality and outstanding service. Every member of the staff was friendly, courteous, made us feel welcome throughout our stay. My Honest Stay Experience – House Stay Inn, New Delhi I stayed at House Stay Inn (Chandi Wali Street, approximately 1 km from New Delhi Railway Station) for 4 days and 3 nights. This review is based entirely on my personal experience. Location: The hotel is located inside very narrow lanes off the main road. While it is close to New Delhi Railway Station, reaching the hotel with luggage can be inconvenient. Room Experience: The room was extremely small for two people. There was hardly any space to open suitcases or keep luggage comfortably. Almost everything had to be managed on the bed—it became the bed, dining table, and workspace all at once. Cleanliness: Rating: 2/10 Unfortunately, cleanliness was a major disappointment. When I checked in, the toilet had not even been flushed, which created a very poor first impression. Overall, the room hygiene did not meet basic expectations. Breakfast Experience: The hotel offers complimentary breakfast with tea. During our stay, we had breakfast only once. However, on another day we requested only tea (without breakfast) and were told that tea alone was chargeable. This policy was confusing because tea is included with breakfast, but not if ordered separately. It would be better if the hotel clearly explained this to guests. Food: From what I observed, many hotels in the Chandi Wali Street area do not have their own in-house kitchens. Food appears to be prepared by nearby small eateries and supplied to the hotels. Final Verdict: If your priority is cleanliness, hygiene, and a comfortable stay, I would recommend looking for accommodation in a different area instead of the Chandi Wali Street locality near New Delhi Railway Station. ⭐ Overall Rating: 1.5/10.0 This review reflects only my personal experience during my stay.

A disappointing experience after multiple stays I usually don’t write Google reviews, but after staying at Smyle Inn 3–4 times, I felt it was important to share my experience—not simply out of frustration, but so that future guests know what to expect and the hotel can hopefully improve. Location: The biggest advantage of this hotel is its location, especially if you need to be close to New Delhi Railway Station. However, the approach involves passing through a small lane with a very unpleasant smell from an open urinal, and during the monsoon it can get even worse. That said, this is more of a general Paharganj-area issue rather than something I would specifically blame the hotel for. Rooms: Please check the room category carefully and confirm the actual room size with the hotel before booking. The Classic rooms are extremely small. In my experience, the Comfort/bigger rooms are much better—they are comfortable, clean and considerably more pleasant to stay in. Staff: I would like to specifically mention that the owner has always seemed sensible and nice. However, some of the other staff members, particularly those at the reception, can be quite discourteous when guests raise even minor issues. Their manner of communication can feel unnecessarily rude and irritating. Some basic customer-service and hospitality training would make a big difference. My main concern — blanket/basic comfort: This is the issue that ultimately made me decide not to stay here again. During two of my stays, I faced an issue regarding blankets. I don’t know whether the owner is aware of this policy, but when I requested a blanket outside the winter season, the reception staff simply refused and told me that the hotel provides only a bedsheet during summer and monsoon. I was even told to switch off the fan/AC if I needed to feel warmer. I faced essentially the same issue around two years ago. At that time, my friends were unwell and needed a blanket, and the matter was eventually resolved after we spoke to the owner. Unfortunately, the same situation happened again during my most recent stay last month. I was travelling with a friend who had fever and cold and genuinely needed a blanket, but the reception staff again refused the request. This made me really angry and frustrated and I even gave a big lecture to the receptionist but nothing happened. I had booked the hotel for three days, but the experience became so disappointing that I ended up leaving on the second day. For a hotel presenting itself as a 3-star property on google, I find it difficult to understand why providing a basic comfort item such as a blanket or comforter should depend strictly on the season. Guests have different comfort requirements, and if someone is cold or unwell, a simple request for an additional blanket should not become an argument. I genuinely hope the owner looks into this, particularly the staff’s manner of dealing with guests and the policy of refusing blankets outside winter. These may seem like small things, but for a guest who is unwell or uncomfortable, they matter a lot. After 3–4 stays, this was unfortunately my last one as trust is broken. I hope the hotel takes this feedback constructively and improves these basic aspects of hospitality.

A Very Disappointing Experience at a So-Called 5-Star Hotel Our stay at The Lalit New Delhi was extremely disappointing from beginning to end. For a hotel that presents itself as a 5-star property, the level of service, communication and basic guest care was nowhere near what we expected. Our flight was cancelled due to a technical issue, which meant our arrival at the hotel was going to be significantly delayed. Naturally, I wanted to inform the hotel’s reservation team so that our booking would not be marked as a no-show. I sent several messages but received absolutely no response. I then tried calling the reception desk. On approximately five separate occasions, I was kept on hold for around 10 minutes each time. International calls were costing me around £2 per minute, meaning I was spending a considerable amount of money simply trying to get someone to acknowledge our situation. Every time, I was told that someone from the reservation team would contact me. Nobody ever did. Eventually, we managed to reach the hotel around midnight. The reception experience was equally disappointing. Instead of being welcomed after what had already been a very stressful journey, we were made to feel as though the staff were doing us a favour by checking us in. The attitude was extremely unwelcoming and honestly embarrassing for us. The following morning, things got even worse. We went for breakfast at the 24/7 dining restaurant and were shocked to see around 20 people waiting ahead of us. After approximately 30 minutes, instead of properly managing the situation, guests were redirected to Baluchi on the second floor. Unfortunately, Baluchi was an even bigger disappointment. The service was chaotic and extremely slow. It genuinely felt as though many members of staff were deliberately avoiding eye contact with guests because they did not want to be approached or asked for anything. We had to wait around 20 minutes for even the simplest requests. This is simply not the level of service one expects from a 5-star hotel. But the biggest embarrassment came later. We had specifically booked a half-board package, which clearly meant breakfast plus either lunch or dinner. We chose dinner. After finishing our meal, we were suddenly told by the restaurant staff that we had to pay for the entire dinner. We explained that we were on a half-board package, but rather than checking the booking properly, the matter turned into a long and unnecessary discussion. Eventually, we were taken to the main lobby so that a manager could verify our booking. After all that embarrassment, the manager finally confirmed that we were indeed on the half-board package and apologised. You would think that would be the end of the matter. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. On our final night, we invited some guests for dinner. Because of the previous experience, we had to specifically remind the restaurant staff that we were on a half-board package and that we would personally pay for our guests. After dinner, we paid our bill of approximately ₹10,000, plus another ₹550 in tips. Our guests left, and we returned to our room. Then, at 10:49 PM, our room phone rang. The hotel staff were calling to ask whether we had actually paid our bill. Seriously? After we had already gone through the embarrassment of having our half-board booking questioned previously, after paying the bill, and after leaving the restaurant, someone thought it was appropriate to call our room at 10:49 at night to verify whether we had paid. This was the final straw. From the poor communication before arrival, the unwelcoming reception, the chaotic breakfast arrangements, painfully slow service, staff avoiding guests, the confusion over our half-board booking, and finally a late-night call questioning our payment, almost every aspect of this stay fell far below what anyone should expect from a 5-star hotel. A 5-star hotel is not just about an impressive building or expensive rooms. It is about hospitality, communication, organisation, attention to detail and making guests feel valued.

The listing clearly mentioned that guests could check in up to three hours early, subject to room availability. I arrived about an hour before the standard check-in time, but instead of being properly assisted, I was simply asked to wait. I sat there for around 15–20 minutes, and during that entire time, nobody bothered to offer even a glass of water or properly explain the situation. The biggest issue was that the room was not ready at all. There were several other hotels nearby offering rooms of a similar standard at the same time, so I ultimately had no choice but to cancel my booking and move elsewhere. For a guest who has specifically paid for one of the most expensive rooms and has arrived expecting an early check-in based on the information provided on MakeMyTrip, this kind of treatment felt extremely disrespectful and disappointing. At the very least, the staff should have communicated properly, offered basic hospitality, and given me a clear idea of how long I would have to wait. I was also not impressed with the receptionist’s attitude or behavior. Overall, the experience was far below what I expected from a hotel charging this much. 1 star from me. A mid-range hotel is impossible to find in Connaught Place; there's nothing in between the luxury hotels and the guest houses. Ram's Inn is a guest house, comfortable enough for a solo traveller, but if you're looking for bright white sheets and towels, spotless walls, dustless fans, 24-hour reception, daily housekeeping, step-free access with lifts, instant hot water, and reliable wifi then you should shell out for one of the nearby full-service hotels instead. Ram's Inn does a good job with the facilities that it has available, and if you have business around Connaught Place its location can't be beat. The staff on the ground floor are always present, available and responsive, and check-in is efficient. My tariff did not include breakfast, but Saravana Bhavan opens at 8am just a few minutes' walk around the corner and is quick and uncrowded in the mornings. In my second-floor walk-up room the white sheets and towels seemed tinged grey, and on the second of my two evenings the wifi stopped. And when I walked downstairs at 6.40am to go to the Hanuman Mandir at sunrise I found myself locked inside, with no staff visible, till 7.51am. On the other hand, I paid a fraction of what I would have paid for a full-service hotel. All in all, Ram’s Inn is value for money for a solo traveller but whether it will satisfy you will depend on your price-to-service trade-off. I'm OK with it, but I wouldn’t bring my family here.

My stay at Hotel Nirmal Mahal, Delhi, was extremely disappointing and honestly much worse than what I expected from the pictures shown online. The actual hotel does not look the way it is presented in the photos, so please do not rely completely on the pictures while making a booking. The cleanliness was one of the biggest problems. The rooms were dirty and poorly maintained, and the bathrooms were in an extremely unhygienic condition. The overall cleanliness was so poor that it made us uncomfortable staying there. The hotel seriously needs better housekeeping and regular maintenance. The lift was not working during our stay, which was a major inconvenience. Imagine having to climb 3–4 floors using the stairs, especially for elderly people or anyone carrying luggage. This is something that should be properly maintained for the safety and convenience of guests. There were also frequent power cuts. When we complained about this, the staff casually told us that it happens every day and is “normal” and that we should adjust. This was extremely frustrating. Guests should not be expected to simply accept such basic issues after paying for a hotel room. The behaviour of the staff was another major disappointment. Some staff members were extremely rude and disrespectful. They did not properly listen to our concerns, and instead of helping us, they spoke rudely and behaved as if our complaints did not matter. Good hospitality requires basic courtesy and a willingness to listen to guests. The surroundings were also very unpleasant. There was a lot of garbage and dirt outside the hotel, which caused a very bad smell around the area. The location is also quite inconvenient because the hotel is situated deep inside the lane, making it difficult for autos and e-rickshaws to reach directly. When some drivers do come, they often ask for an additional charge. Overall, the entire experience was extremely unpleasant. The hotel needs major improvement in cleanliness, bathroom hygiene, housekeeping, maintenance, electricity, lift service, staff behaviour, and the surrounding area. Most importantly, the hotel shown in the online pictures does not match the actual condition we experienced. I would strongly recommend that potential guests carefully check recent reviews and photos before booking. Unfortunately, I would not recommend Hotel Nirmal Mahal for a comfortable or hygienic stay.

text_light: An absolutely unforgettable birthday dinner at C2C, Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon, Goa. From the moment I arrived, everything was exceptional — the service, the attention to detail and all the thoughtful little surprises throughout the evening. A very special thank you to Rupesh Gupta and Amit Kesri for making me and my friends feel so warmly welcomed and beautifully looked after. And my deepest compliments to Chef Edridge — the menu was truly exquisite. Every course felt carefully considered, elegant and full of flavour. The burrata with berry compote and basil oil was simply unreal — such an unexpected and delicious combination. The signature mushroom cappuccino with golden leaf was another highlight and had everyone at the table talking. The presentation of the refreshing lemon and mint sorbet was a wonderful surprise and created such a beautiful moment for all of us. The fish was cooked to perfection, delicate and absolutely delicious. And then came the finale — the matcha cheesecake. As the birthday girl, even I wasn’t expecting the way it would be presented! It surprised not only me but all my guests and was the perfect ending to an already incredible dinner. This wasn’t simply a birthday dinner — it was a whole experience. Beautiful food, refined flavours, creativity, warmth and genuine hospitality. Even writing this review and remembering the menu is making my mouth water all over again! 😊 A huge thank you to Cullen and the entire C2C team, and to everyone behind the scenes who contributed to making my birthday so special. You gave me and my guests an evening we will remember for a very long time. My birthday could not have been more perfect. Thank you from the bottom of my heart! ❤️

hotel_name: Taj Cidade De Goa Horizon, Goa
text_light: ⭐️ Absolutely Outstanding – The Star of Our Goa Trip! Simply exceptional! Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon was the absolute highlight of our 6-day Goa trip—a truly stunning, luxurious, almost seven-star experience. Our sea-view room was amazing. The huge floor-to-ceiling glass window with an incredible sea view was simply breathtaking. The bathtub was a huge hit with the kids, and every detail of the room felt premium and beautifully maintained. The massive lobby, stunning architecture, spectacular sea views and beautiful dining areas were all top-class. Dining with the sea view, whether indoors or outdoors, was an experience in itself. Breakfast, food quality, cleanliness and service—all excellent. The staff deserve a special mention—polite, well-mannered, decent, warm and genuinely lovely. The property has two fantastic pools, including an infinity pool, with amazing views. We also had access to the pool and private beach of the Heritage property, with a complimentary buggy service whenever we wanted to go to the beach. During our Ganesh Chaturthi stay, the hotel also surprised us with an excellent complimentary high tea, which was so generous and filling that we hardly needed anything afterward! What a property, what a view, what a room! Absolutely amazing. Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon was undoubtedly the STAR of our Goa trip. ❤️

Rest of the issues like sea view and all are fine to some extent. But toilet is a core issue. I can only fully recommend this hotel to others if they fix that. I have given 5 stars as the staff are really trying their best. But infrastructure is something that they cannot do anything about. Hopefully, the management can fix it by next visit.

We had a wonderful stay at this beautiful seaside resort in the Dona Paula area. Its location is excellent close to the Dona Paula Viewpoint in Panjim and conveniently accessible to many of the popular cafes and restaurants nearby. The resort also has ample parking space, which makes it very convenient if you're traveling by car. One of the highlights of our stay was the spacious rooms. We chose a sea-view room, and waking up to the view of the ocean every morning was truly worth it. The property itself is peaceful, well maintained, and offers a relaxing atmosphere. The breakfast spread was another standout. There were plenty of vegetarian options but the taste wasn’t all that great but enjoying breakfast by the pool with uninterrupted sea views and the sound of the waves made for a very memorable experience. There were just a couple of minor drawbacks. The hot water supply was a bit inconsistent at times during the day. Also, if you book the sea-view rooms, be aware that reaching them involves a fair amount of walking, and the resort does not provide buggy or shuttle services. This may not be the most convenient option for senior citizens or guests with limited mobility. During the monsoon, you're also likely to get wet while walking to and from the rooms. One small observation was that the pathway leading to the sea-view rooms felt a little secluded and somewhat disconnected from the main part of the property, with a few small structures along the way. It wasn't a major concern by any means, but it's something worth knowing before booking those rooms. Overall, these were relatively minor inconveniences compared to the overall experience. The stunning location, spacious rooms, peaceful ambience, excellent breakfast, and beautiful sea views made for a very enjoyable stay. I would happily recommend this property to anyone looking for a relaxing getaway in Goa.

Extremely Disappointing Experience at Regenta Panaji, Goa My stay at Regenta Panaji was one of the most disappointing hotel experiences I have had. I chose this hotel expecting professional hospitality, comfortable accommodation, and quality service, but unfortunately, it failed to meet even basic expectations. The biggest issue was the extremely poor customer service. The staff appeared indifferent and unresponsive to guest concerns. Requests took far too long to be addressed, and in some cases, they were simply ignored. There was a noticeable lack of coordination among the hotel team, making even simple interactions frustrating. The housekeeping standards were also below average. The room was not maintained to the level expected from a reputed hotel. Cleanliness could have been much better, and the overall upkeep gave the impression that guest comfort was not a priority. The check-in and check-out process was unnecessarily slow and disorganized. Instead of a smooth arrival experience, I had to spend an unreasonable amount of time waiting. Such delays are unacceptable, especially for business and family travelers. The food quality was another major disappointment. The menu was limited, the taste was average, and the service in the restaurant was slow. Considering the prices charged, the value for money was extremely poor. The hotel facilities also did not match the expectations created through its advertisements. Maintenance seemed inadequate, and several areas required better attention. The overall atmosphere lacked the warmth and professionalism expected from a hospitality brand. What disappointed me the most was the lack of genuine concern for guest satisfaction. Rather than resolving issues promptly, the staff seemed more interested in offering excuses than solutions. Good hospitality is about making guests feel welcome and valued, and unfortunately, that was completely missing during my stay. Overall, I cannot recommend Regenta Panaji based on my experience. There are several better hotels in Goa that provide superior service, cleaner rooms, better food, and far greater value for money. Unless significant improvements are made in customer service, housekeeping, maintenance, and management, I would not consider staying here again.

There were a few mosquitoes in the room, and the cupboard had a damp, humid smell with an unpleasant wooden odour. The service was quite slow, and I was surprised that even drinking water bottles were chargeable with no complimentary bottles provided. There were also a few maintenance issues. The corridor lights were not switched on at night, making it inconvenient to move around, and the UPS backup failed for a few minutes during a power interruption. Overall, the hotel has potential, but it needs significant improvements in room maintenance, basic amenities, housekeeping, and service standards to provide a better guest experience for the price charged. 😑

There is an intercom on the table to communicate with the reception and can order eatables from the Menu present. A large window occupies one side of the room, with double curtains, one sheer or lace curtain to allow light through if you want and it makes the room bright. The other is a linen like heavy curtain which blocks the light if needed. Lights in the room are wonderful, one switch near the bed for less lights, and another for more lights which makes the room brighter, according to your need. There is quite a big TV in the room for those who like to view. I was not interested in watching so I will not be able to tell whuch channels are available. A full length cupboard is there at the enterance for hanging clothes and also shelfs for folding. A rack, in the room I was, was on the left of the cupboard on which to place bags. A half length mirror is above the rack. Bathroom was clean and compact, and tiled. With basin and a tub, for those who would like a tub bath, with both hot and cold water, and a curtain to prevent splashing outside the tub, so the bathroom remains dry, ( I think, especially important when older people are there). The staff are hospitable, and helpful. There is a dining room, which we unfortunately did not use. We ordered a club sandwhich as we were in a hurry, it was tasty and came with fries.

I've had a very very mixed experience here. The good things first. This is one of the best and most well behaved and cultured staff I've seen, on par with 5 star hotel standards. Now to the most annoying part. Some rooms like mine have a connecting door to the next room. And because of this everytime someone checks in into your neighbouring room they think the door leads to an extension of their room and try to force open it. It's a blatant invasion of your privacy. I can't blame the guests for that nor the staff, it's a building flaw that needs to be fixed. I stayed here for 10 days and 4 different people have checked into that neighbouring room at various hours and they all tried to force open that door, sometimes at midnight when I was asleep. It was a very very unsafe feeling. And because of the door not being sealed, every single noise from the neighbouring room causes a huge disturbance in my room every single time. If they cannot fix this, no matter how well mannered the staff might be, the guests are going to have a bad experience.

The hotel is perfectly located, with a peaceful water stream on one side and the colorful streets of Fontainhas on the other, making it an ideal base for exploring the neighborhood on foot. The staff are extremely helpful, friendly, and always ready to assist, making the stay even more enjoyable. The hotel also has its own kitchen and restaurant, serving tasty food at very reasonable prices. If you stay here, don't miss the Curd Rice—it's absolutely delicious and one of the best I had during my visit! Overall, Hotel Ria offers great value for money, a convenient location, clean rooms, and warm hospitality. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable stay while exploring the beautiful heritage streets of Fontainhas, Panjim.

We had a wonderful stay at O'Pierre Hotel! Right from the booking process, the experience was smooth. I called twice hoping for a better discount. Although I didn't get the discount I expected, the customer care lady (sorry, I don't know her name) surprised me by suggesting I book through TripAdvisor to get a lower price for the same room. That level of honesty is rare and truly appreciated. The rooms were spacious, beautiful, clean, and well-maintained with excellent AC. The only small suggestion is to replace bed sheets with visible stains or marks. The staff went above and beyond throughout our stay. They allowed us to extend one room until 5 PM for just half a day's charge since we were traveling with kids and had a 6 PM bus. Even when we checked out about 1.5 hours late, they handled it very politely and understandingly. One of our children got hurt, and the staff immediately provided a band-aid and calmly guided us on basic first aid, which was very thoughtful. Another staff member honestly advised us to walk to Deltin Jaqk instead of taking a cab, saving us unnecessary expense. They even allowed a lady who came to do dreadlocks for my wife and sister, and later suggested she could have gone to our room for the kids' comfort, despite their usual visitor policy. A special thanks to the watchman, who stepped out in the rain to help our Goa Miles cab reach the hotel and assisted with our luggage. I couldn't tip him, but he truly deserves appreciation from the hotel. Breakfast had limited options, but everything was delicious, especially the puri bhaji! Water bottles were always provided promptly without any unnecessary charges. Overall, every staff member was polite, caring, and genuinely focused on guest comfort. Small gestures like these made our stay memorable. Highly recommended!

The ambiance of this hotel exceeded our expectations. At a very reasonable tariff, it offers the comfort and luxury typically associated with much more expensive star-rated hotels. The rooms are cozy, well-designed, and comfortable. The lighting throughout the property is excellent and adds to the overall pleasant atmosphere. The first-floor lobby creates a sense of elegance and gives the impression of a premium stay. The cafeteria also has a modern and relaxing vibe. One of the highlights was the spacious, well-maintained, and exceptionally clean washrooms. The interiors, fittings, and overall facilities in the washrooms are impressive. Considering its affordable pricing, this hotel offers outstanding value for money. While the breakfast spread is somewhat limited, it is perfectly reasonable given the room rates and overall quality of the stay. Overall, this is an excellent choice for travelers seeking comfort, cleanliness, and a premium experience at a budget-friendly price. The best part is that the owners personally manage the hotel and interact with guests themselves, leaving little room for any mismanagement and ensuring a warm, attentive experience.

Located just beyond Miramar in a quiet, well-planned residential neighborhood, this 26-key property sits about 400 meters off the main road. The building is tucked right into a residential area with virtually no open space surrounding or within the premises. ​The Room & Facilities I stayed for two nights in a clean and spacious room, though it didn't offer much of a view. While basic room essentials were provided, standard conveniences like an iron, hairdryer, and full-length mirror were surprisingly absent. For leisure, there is a pool table and a carrom board placed outdoors near the dining area. ​Dining The single on-site restaurant handles the breakfast buffet, which was fairly average with limited variety—they didn't even have a toaster available. For lunch or dinner, especially if you prefer pure vegetarian food, ordering via food delivery apps like Zomato is a much better option. ​Location & Final Verdict There is very little within walking distance; even the beach is roughly 500 meters away. Overall, this hotel is fine if you strictly need a clean, quiet place to sleep at night, but it lacks the atmosphere, amenities, and location suited for family trips.

If you are looking for a place in the Dona Paula area of Goa for a reasonable price, this small hotel a good option. I would consider this place again if returning to Dona Paula. My first impression of my room was that it was a little (not a lot) more down-market than the pictures I had seen online suggested; but it was fine overall. The room seemed clean, the property seemed safe, and overall, I found it to be decent value. My room, facing the back of the property, was quiet - although there was not much of a view. The property faces a busy street, so I suspect a room facing the front of the property might have noise issues. When I checked in, the front desk/table had a big sign about all the fees they charged (e.g., for damaged property). And when I entered the room, that (a similar sheet of info centered prominently on the bed) was by far the most prominent piece of info in the room. That didn't create the best sense of welcome - but I had no issues with additional fees, etc. My point here would be: don't let that odd form of welcome put you off. The entrance to the hotel is at the back of the hotel - and is accessed from a side street that runs along the left side (as you face the hotel) of the property. The fellow working at the front desk/table the evening I arrived was not particularly friendly - nor was he unfriendly. But the woman who worked there in the daytime, the security guard, and the cleaning lady all seemed very nice. The room has a built-in water filtration system. I mostly stuck to bottled water during my stay but I did use the filtered water once of twice and had no issues. Bathroom appliances all worked fine. WiFi worked fine. There are a couple small supermarkets and restaurant options within short walking distance, including the Burger Factory on the ground floor of the hotel building. The room had helpful info on nearby spots. GoaMiles (the local version of Uber; download that app and pre-load it with some [refundable] credits, as Uber does not work in Goa) worked fine for pick up and drop off at the hotel. My waits for pickup varied between two and seven minutes. One cab driver I used did not know where Villa Donna was - but he did know where Burger Factory was - so that may be a good landmark to mention to a cab driver. Just be aware there are a couple Burger Factory locations - you want the one in Dona Paula. If I were to return to Goa, I would probably try staying at one of the beach towns far to the north or south of the Dona Paula area. The developed Dona Paula area, with its casino boats, didn't particularly appeal to me. But if I were returning to the Dona Paula area, I would be happy to stay at Villa Donna again.

At the start, one must say, Manvin's has a very kind and empathetic landlady who's available in the mornings to sort out issues guests may've. Manvin's also enjoys great views, perhaps the best in Panjim for a hotel in this price range. My disappointment stems from the sparkling reviews and amazing pictures and videos on Google Maps, several of which have been posted by guests and don't belong to the hotel. I got the impression that it's a big hotel with attendant facilities like a gym, restaurant and bar. Manvin's is more of a bed&breakfast or a budget guesthouse, located on the 5th and 6th, perhaps also 7th floors of an aging building in a fine location in the very atmospheric Fontainhas in the heart of Panjim. Accessed by a decrepit lift, it certainly has a higher fire hazard than other hotels in the area. Safety-minded guests should scope out the two staircases leading down to ground level. The rooms are spacious, with river and garden views though austere and simple. The 6th floor rooms are a lot hotter during the warm months, and non-aircon rooms on that floor are inadvisable, despite the superior views. The breakfast area has really fine views of the rooftops and colourful buildings of Fontainhas, the blindingly white 1541 Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, and the beautiful bridge over the River Mandovi in the distance. The morning breakfast, though frugal, can be surprisingly delicious. The hotel also arranges an airport pickup or drop, at an extra cost, if informed in advance. This was a real advantage as I'd an early morning flight, and cab services in Goa at that hour can be very unreliable. All in all, I'd say, this could be a lovely place to stay during the mild-weather months from October to February. Not so lovely during the hot and humid months.

Extremely Disappointing Experience at Treebo Sunheads Miramar Room 109 I had booked a room on 20 September 2027, with check-in at approximately 2:30 AM on 21 September 2027 and check-out at 4:00 AM. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing from the moment we entered the room. The room had a very strong and unbearable smell of fresh paint. Since we checked in at around 2:30 AM, we were already exhausted, but the smell was so strong that we experienced considerable discomfort and cold symptoms. I immediately went to the reception and requested a room change. I spoke with Sameer Jena, who told me that he was the manager. However, I was not provided with any proper solution. I also approached a housekeeping staff member, who said that he could not help. As an attempt to reduce the smell, I requested some cut onions, hoping they might help reduce the smell. Unfortunately, this did not make any difference. Since the smell remained unbearable, I went back to reception and again requested either a room change or some other solution. I was told that they could spray an air freshener. Considering that the room already had an extremely strong paint smell, I felt that spraying an air freshener would only make the situation worse. I was then told that all the rooms were occupied. When I asked about a refund because the room was not in a suitable condition for us to stay in, I was told that “there is no word called refund in Treebo Sunheads Miramar.” I found this response extremely disappointing and unprofessional. What made the situation even more frustrating was that, only after I asked about a refund, Sameer Jena mentioned that there was another room available, but apparently that room also had a paint smell. If an alternative room was available, I believe it should have been offered when I first raised the issue rather than only after I asked about a refund. Throughout the conversation, Sameer Jena was rude, raised his voice, and behaved in an unprofessional manner. Due to the way the situation was handled, we eventually left the room at around 4:00 AM. We left the room open and took the keys with us because I wanted to report the matter to someone else in management, as I did not feel that my concerns were being handled appropriately. The following morning, when I returned the keys, the staff were not even willing to properly listen to what had happened during the night. This was extremely disappointing and gave me the impression that the management was not taking the complaint seriously. A hotel should provide guests with a clean, comfortable, and suitable room, and complaints should be handled with patience, courtesy, and professionalism. Unfortunately, none of this was reflected in our experience. If the management expects to provide hospitality, I strongly recommend proper training for the staff in guest service, communication, complaint handling, and professional behaviour. I am extremely disappointed with this experience and would absolutely NOT recommend Treebo Sunheads Miramar to anyone. I would strongly discourage anyone from choosing this hotel by writing this review, based on the experience we had. The condition of the room, the way our complaint was handled, and the unprofessional behaviour we experienced were completely unacceptable. This is certainly not the level of hospitality a guest should expect. Overall experience: Extremely disappointing. Overall rating: 0/5.

A Beautiful Heritage Stay in the Heart of Fontainhas I had a wonderful stay at Panjim Inn, located in the beautiful heritage quarter of Fontainhas. The property itself is a stunning heritage building and one of the iconic structures along the heritage streets of Fontainhas. It was a unique experience to stay in a building that is so popular as a backdrop for photographs. The interiors are beautifully maintained and the rooms are comfortable and equipped with all the necessary amenities for a pleasant stay. The food was another highlight of my experience, the breakfast had a great variety of options, and the in-house restaurant was also a convenient choice for enjoying a good meal. Overall, I truly enjoyed my stay at Panjim Inn. If you want to experience the charm, character and heritage of Fontainhas while staying in a beautiful heritage property, this is definitely a great place to consider.

Tucked into the heart of Fontainhas, Panjim Inn feels less like checking in and more like being welcomed home. Every corner carries a story, every piece of art a memory, every conversation the warmth of people who genuinely love where they are and what they've created. There is a quiet romance to this place. Mornings drift in with soft light through old Portuguese windows, afternoons unfold unhurriedly, and by evening you're no longer a visitor but part of the rhythm of the house. What makes Panjim Inn special isn't just its beautiful heritage or its thoughtful curation. It's the people. Their generosity, warmth and effortless hospitality remind you that luxury isn't always found in extravagance. Sometimes it's found in being known, lingering over conversations, or feeling completely at home in a city you've only just met. I came to Goa looking for beauty. I left reminded that beauty is rarely just a place. More often, it's the people who invite you in and make you feel like family.

Hotel Liberty is a budget-friendly accommodation located in the heart of Panjim, making it a convenient option for travellers who prioritize location over luxury. Situated close to major attractions like the Church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception and the lively Panjim market area, the hotel offers easy access to sightseeing spots, local restaurants, and casinos, making it suitable for short stays and quick trips. The hotel provides basic amenities such as air-conditioned rooms, room service, and a small lounge area. Some rooms are equipped with essential facilities like a refrigerator and hot water, catering to minimal travel needs. The staff is occasionally described as helpful and accommodating, especially when assisting with local travel or room arrangements. However, guest reviews suggest that the property falls short in terms of maintenance and cleanliness. Many visitors have reported issues such as poorly maintained rooms, lack of hygiene, and the presence of insects, which can affect the overall comfort of the stay. Ratings across platforms generally remain below average, with cleanliness and room quality being the most common concerns. Despite these drawbacks, some travellers still consider it an acceptable option for a low-budget stay, especially if the plan is to spend most of the time exploring Goa rather than staying indoors. The hotel may suit solo travellers or groups looking for an economical place to rest, but it is generally not recommended for families or those seeking a comfortable and premium experience. Overall, Hotel Liberty is best viewed as a basic, no-frills stay in a prime location. While it offers affordability and accessibility, potential guests should weigh these advantages against the reported issues with upkeep and hygiene before making a booking decision.

My Goa Home Away From Home Vivenda Rebelo Homestay is one of those rare places that doesn’t feel like a hotel at all — it feels like a home. Set in a beautiful heritage home, the place has a warmth and character that is difficult to find in regular accommodation. It is cozy, peaceful, spotlessly clean and extremely well maintained. The washroom deserves a special mention — exceedingly clean, which is something I really appreciate. The location is excellent as well. A lot of well-known eateries are within a 15–20 minute walk, while there are two fine-dining restaurants barely a minute away. So you get the peace and charm of a heritage home without being away from great food. But what makes the stay truly special is Deric, the owner. He is humble, warm and genuinely customer-centric. There is no need to call him for anything — just WhatsApp him and he is always quick to respond and happy to help. You get the feeling that he genuinely cares about his guests and their experience. One of my favourite moments was sitting out on the terrace, listening to the sound of the Goan monsoon rain and sipping a chilled beer. It was one of those simple, perfect moments that you remember long after the holiday is over. The whole place has a wonderfully homely feel. You don't feel like a tourist staying in a property; you feel like you are staying in someone's lovely Goan home. I can say this with complete certainty: Vivenda Rebelo is now my permanent home in Goa for all my future visits. In fact, this is the kind of place that could actually make me come back to Goa just to stay here again. Highly recommended for anyone looking for warmth, cleanliness, character and genuine Goan hospitality rather than just another hotel room.

Vivenda Rebelo is a delightful homestay that beautifully captures the old-world charm of Goa. With its heritage look and character, the property has a warm, inviting atmosphere that makes you feel at home the moment you arrive. The rooms are cozy, comfortable and thoughtfully maintained, making it an ideal choice for a relaxed stay in Panjim. Another big plus is the ample parking available on the road, which makes arriving and settling in remarkably convenient. The homestay also has an easy approach and convenient accessibility, making it a practical base for exploring Panjim and the surrounding areas. It’s in the heart of Panjim, and at the same time is surrounded by greenery all around. What truly adds to the experience, though, is the hospitality. The host, Deric is warm, friendly and very approachable, always ready to help and make guests feel comfortable without being intrusive. That personal touch gives Vivenda Rebelo the welcoming charm that one hopes for in a homestay. Overall, Vivenda Rebelo is a lovely blend of heritage charm, comfort, convenience and genuine Goan hospitality. A cozy little stay with plenty of character: highly recommended for anyone looking for an authentic and peaceful experience in Panjim!

The accommodations are charming and well-maintained, providing a comfortable atmosphere to unwind. Our host, Deric, was incredibly knowledgeable and helpful. He provided us with valuable insights about nearby activities, such as scenic boat rides along the Mandovi River and relaxing days at Miramar Beach. He also guided us to must-visit churches like the Basilica of Bom Jesus and the picturesque Latin Quarter of Fontainhas. Deric even suggested some fantastic food trails, allowing us to savor the rich flavors of Goan cuisine. Overall, the combination of the beautiful location and Deric’s hospitality made for an unforgettable stay!

Every year, without fail, my companion, Sarmila, and I find ourselves returning to the serene embrace of Vivenda Rebelo during our annual pilgrimage to the International Film Festival in Goa. What initially drew us was the allure of the festival, but over the years, our priorities have shifted. Now, our sojourn at Vivenda Rebelo is less about the cinematic extravaganza and more about seeking refuge in the tranquil and exotic ambience of this homestay. Nestled amidst tree-rich approach roads that wind their way through unobtrusive structures, the mornings at Vivenda Rebelo are a symphony of bird songs. The avian visitors transform the atmosphere into a natural haven, undisturbed by the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Deric Rebelo, the genial owner of this homestay, goes beyond the role of a mere host – he is a friend who anticipates our needs and ensures our comfort without us having to utter a word. From the vantage point of our balcony, we immerse ourselves in the soothing melody of birdsong, appreciating the harmony between nature and the quaint surroundings. Vivenda Rebelo provides a sanctuary that is both proximate to the town and yet removed from its clamour. It's not just a place to stay; it's a haven where one can unwind, delve into a good book, or simply revel in the silence punctuated by the chorus of birds. In my lifetime, I've encountered various accommodations, but none compare to the unique charm of Vivenda Rebelo, especially for a brief respite from the rigours of daily life.

I booked through the AMEX portal (the Hotel Collection.) due to the offering of a free upgrade. When we got to the front desk upon arrival, we asked if we could get a sea facing twin bed room. They said they were completely sold out on our first night due to a conference being held at the resort. However, they said that the upgrade we wanted might be possible if we call the next day in the morning (they were fully booked due to a conference that was ending the next morning). I called the next day and it’s like they completely forgot what we were told. They said that it is not possible to upgrade us and that we were already upgraded (our view was literally of concrete and the pool so obviously a stingy upgrade that was basically not an upgrade at all). On the Hyatt app, I was able to see plenty of room availability. And THEN they had the audacity to say that we could pay for an upgrade? So you have the room available, I booked through the AMEX portal specifically for the upgrade, I was told that such an upgrade is possible if we ask the next day, and then when I ask they tell me I have to pay? Well then what’s the point of using the AMEX portal when you clearly have plenty of rooms available? While this was booked by my father, I personally generally only stay at Hyatts when possible. And this is by far the most stingy experience I have ever had. I request upgrades ALL THE TIME. On top of that, the room is showing obvious signs of wear and tear + the breakfast has the least selection I have ever seen at a hotel since my arrival in India. I understand that if you are sold out, upgrades aren’t possible. But when you are NOT sold out and previously promised a guest to try and accommodate their request the next day, AND THEN you tell them that they have to pay despite them booking the hotel through the “Hotel Collection” via the AMEX portal which promises upgrades. Well trust me, I am never staying here again. Staff is also poorly trained and random areas of the hotel look run down. If you look over the edge of the short sea wall, the area is littered with trash. Room service takes forever even at less popular times of day (3/4 PM). The phone in our room is broken. AND it takes forever to reach the front desk. It will ring for too long until someone responds. And it is impossible to reach in room dining to ask any questions regarding menu items. Once rom service called ME after submitting an order to ask if I wanted to order anything else. Obviously they’d offer service to us when they see an opportunity to squeeze more money out of guests! When I asked if the garden salad could come with chicken like the chicken Caesar salad, they said no. I mean come on you can’t just pick up the chicken you put in the chicken Caesar salad and throw it on the garden salad? Like it’s a very basic request. So much of the staff here just seems so confused when we make small requests and the response to any requests that may require some creativity causes them to stutter and tell us very ineloquently that the request isn’t possible. I Some of the staff seems to struggle with English. Which was fine because my father knows Hindi. But I do not speak Hindi, so if I were to come here without him it would be slightly challenging. Also, rooms don’t come with a coffee machine which feels odd for a hotel of this caliber but not a dealbreaker for me. am just throughly disappointed by this hotel. If you feel like much of my issues can be attributed to communication errors, please work on that. Edit: they were able to provide an upgrade later in the day. The manager said it wasn’t possible earlier due to the upgraded room having not yet been cleaned. However, that was not at all what the other staff told us. I called several times and they all gave us different reasons and repossess. Additionally, our original room was missing a chair for the table which is a really weird thing to overlook.

Honestly, one of the best parts of our Goa trip was the hospitality we received here. ❤️ I had initially booked this resort for just one night and was planning to move to a beachfront resort afterwards. But the service was SO good that I ended up extending our stay here instead — and actually extended our North Goa trip by another day too! A very special mention to Manya, Rishu, Binpna and Aman. Every single one of them was so warm, helpful and genuinely considerate throughout our stay. Since it was just me and my sister travelling, having people around who were always ready to help made us feel incredibly comfortable and looked after. They also helped us with the rental thing. Rather than leaving us to figure everything out ourselves, they gave us a reliable contact number and helped arrange everything according to our convenience. It made getting around Goa so much easier for us. And then there was one particular incident that really showed us how genuinely helpful they were. Our phone and power bank accidentally got wet, so suddenly neither of us could charge our phones and we were completely stuck. The staff actually went out of their way and ordered a power bank using their own phone for us and we paid them back later. It might sound like a small thing, but when you’re travelling and suddenly have no way to charge your phone, that kind of help means soo much. What I loved most was that none of this ever felt like they were simply “doing their job”. They were genuinely attentive and made sure we were comfortable and sorted throughout our stay. The property is lovely, but honestly, the people are what made us want to stay longer. Thank you to the entire team and especially to Manya, Rishu, Binpna and Aman for going out the way to help us out and for making our stay so comfortable and memorable. 10/10 for the hospitality, kindness and service. Would happily stay here again! ❤️

The owner (Ram) of this property is a big-time fraud. While taking payments, he promised many things, but after receiving the money, he showed his real face. I met him on Airbnb, where he had posted flat pictures showing the front view of a white bungalow but the reality was completely different. The building was completely different building & is old, dirty, and unsafe. There is no security. When I saw it, I immediately realized I had been scammed! Right in front of the entrance, they had left a dirty commode. When we entered the flat, there was fungus everywhere — behind the bed, in the hall, on the doors, wardrobes, and walls. The entire flat was stinking of fungus. The bedsheets were torn, and the pillows, mattresses, and curtains were full of fungus. Our skin turned red due to infections. Because of this, they shifted us to a 1RK for 5 days, which had no basic facilities. Ram (the owner) trapped us, as he has trapped many others, by saying “the beach is less than 100 meters away from my building.” But that’s a lie the beach is more than half a kilometer away (see attached screenshot). He had promised daily room cleaning in writing since I have OCD and we cook at home everyday. But every single day, he created fights, saying, “Kal hi to saaf karwaya tha, aaj kyun bheju?” I begged him many times, explaining my OCD, but he continued to harass us with his evil behavior. In the washroom, sewage water from another bathroom was leaking and flowing into ours. While using the toilet, sewage water was literally falling on my head! The owner arranged only a temporary fix. The kitchen door was broken, and every night some animal came in, pulling garbage bags and spreading trash all over. When we complained, the owner casually said, “What to do?” He had also promised that the washroom would be cleaned twice a week, but even that didn’t happen properly. The caretaker came without cleaning materials and asked us how to clean! They had no training at all. We even gave them our personal cleaning supplies, and many times my husband cleaned the washroom himself because the caretaker was completely clueless. Accessing the washing machine was another struggle. They kept working washing machine in one of a room’s attached balcony, if any guest is there we used to climb to the balcony with the help of chair (see attached picture). We had already paid in advance, so we had no choice but to stay. For every small or big issue, we had to chase the owner multiple times. During our one-month stay, we saw many guests come and leave early because of the same false promises and terrible service. So, it’s not just our experience — many people have suffered because of this owner. Ram has ruined many people’s vacations, time, and money. He is a shameless person, and our stay was a nightmare. Later, when I checked other customer reviews, I was shocked to see that many others had been scammed by this same person. The caretaker blames the owner, and the owner blames the caretaker — together, they made our lives miserable. All we expected were basic facilities a clean room, fresh bed, mattress, and towel without fungus but instead, this man made our 30 days a living hell!

Supportive staff, but an incredibly disappointing, aging property How can this property justify a 4-star rating? This is my 9th time visiting Goa, and it has been a total disappointment. Having just completed my first day, I am dreading my next 3 nights. The Bad: Room Issues: We paid for early check-in so we could sleep, but the AC was incredibly noisy and took 1.5 hours to fix. The curtains were dirty, the washroom smelled terrible, and the mattress was entirely sunken in and worn out. Amenities: The main pool was under maintenance. We were directed to a small private pool instead, which was poorly maintained and dirty. Mosquitoes: A severe mosquito infestation at both properties. I killed over 8 mosquitoes in the washroom alone on the first day. Service: The hotel felt noticeably understaffed. The Good: Staff: When we complained about the room, the staff was very supportive and helped us relocate to another property in Candolim. However, waiting for room availability wasted half of our day. Ultimately, the second property was just as old and poorly maintained as the first. Both urgently need serious renovations. If you are expecting a true 4-star experience, look elsewhere. This is a 2 or 3-star property at best.

A Mixed 4-Star Experience with Great Staff Gestures and Excellent Food Rating: 3.5 / 5 The Good: * Prime Location: The hotel has an excellent location right on the main road. It is highly convenient, with major convenience stores, supermarkets, and famous restaurants just a short walk away. * Spacious Rooms: While the exterior architecture and property appearance look a bit outdated from the outside, the rooms inside are a pleasant surprise. They are very well-spaced and come with attached balconies. * Outstanding Culinary Staff: The breakfast buffet was a bit repetitive day-to-day, but the food quality itself was very good. A special shoutout to Chef Sapan and server Mahesh. They went entirely out of their way to improve our dining experience. When we asked for non-vegetarian options, they prepared world-class fish and grilled chicken specifically for us. * Service Recovery: We initially stayed on the top floor and were heavily disturbed by constant, loud noises coming from the housekeeping team. Despite multiple complaints, the noise issue couldn't be resolved in that room. However, the management made a very nice gesture to amend the situation by upgrading us to a luxurious room, which we greatly appreciated. The Bad: * Disappointing Rooftop Pool: The rooftop swimming pool was a major letdown. It was not well-maintained, and there was not even a single umbrella available for shade. Being open on the rooftop without any sun shelter made it a very disappointing amenity to use. Verdict: As a 4-star property, Lemon Tree Candolim does a good job overall, but there is clear room for improvement. They need to focus on property maintenance—especially the pool area and noise management—to truly maintain the 4-star standard they stand for.

text_light: Had a mixed but overall decent experience at Stone Wood Beach Resort, Vagator. The biggest highlight is the location and the great view of the beach. It’s a nice place if you want to stay close to the beach and enjoy the surroundings. Initially, the room we were given had an issue with the ceiling, with some powder falling from above. We informed the staff and were given another room, which was clean, comfortable and much better. The restaurant serves really tasty food, but the service needs some improvement. The waiters are not always available to take orders, and we had to wait quite a long time on multiple occasions. The swimming pool is also quite small and doesn’t have much depth, so it’s more suitable for a quick dip than actually swimming. One important thing to keep in mind before booking: if you’re looking for a peaceful stay or planning a relaxing family vacation, this may not be the ideal place. There are several pubs around the resort and loud music can continue until around 4 AM. This was a problem for us, although to be fair, the reception staff did inform us about the noise during check-in. Overall, the beach view and location are great, the food is good, and the staff did address our room issue. However, the surrounding nightlife and noise are definitely something to consider before booking.

Hotel Viva Baga is a nice place to stay if you want to enjoy Goa's famous nightlife, as it is just a 5-minute walk from Tito's Lane, putting you right next to top parties, pubs, and a vibrant shopping market. Baga Beach is also within a reasonable 15-minute walk from the property. The hotel provides on-site parking, though it is limited, so finding a spot during peak season can be a challenge. However, if you are visiting during the off-season from March to October, the hotel provides special on-site discounts. If you plan to travel during these months, I highly recommend opting for an on-site walk-in booking instead of an online booking to grab these special discounted rates. These discounts depend heavily on room demand, so they are not always guaranteed, but they are mostly available during the quieter off-season months. Safety at the hotel is well-handled with CCTV cameras installed across the premises. For amenities, they provide free water, but it is a self-service system where you have to fetch it from the reception yourself, and note that there is no room service available for ordering food.The rooms were okay overall. We booked two triple-bed rooms, which featured nice balconies with a pleasant roadside view. One of our rooms was a little stinky at first, but the staff cleaned it again immediately after we notified them. Regular facilities like clean towels and soap were provided, the ACs worked well, and the bathrooms had running hot and cold water. Lastly, keep in mind that the hotel enforces a strict checkout policy at 10:00 AM. If you need a late checkout, you can extend your stay by paying ₹100 per person per hour, subject to room availability. It is a decent budget option for party lovers and groups.

Alila Diwa Goa can be termed one with a great natural setting hotel. This hotel and its higher category rooms are very good. This place boosts of some trees which are more than 50+ years old. their food restaurant is good. If you are like me, who is a lazy tourist and don't want to venture out too much then its the place to be. The Sunday brunch is quite exquisite with a live counter of poultry and sea food available. The rooms are great with a huge balcony overseeing the swimming pool (there are 2 of them). The bathroom is stylish and got modern aesthatics. The bed is really quite comfortable and provides a deep slumber. Some drawbacks, the beach is not close and the hotel provides a van to transfer guests to and fro hotel from 8AM to 7PM. The beach itself is not great in any sense and so one can avoid it. There seems to be some good outside restaurant, called Mikes place or something which seems to be quite famous but I did not visit that. Finally, the managers here are quite high nosed ones and getting one of them to have attention is difficult, especially when you are troubled and need assistance. its in South Goa so never take flight to MOPA. Go for Dabolim only.

We repeatedly requested a room change and explained that we had a one-year-old baby who was crawling on the floor, so keeping him in a constantly damp room for three days was simply not acceptable for us. We asked for another room or even an upgrade, but were told that every room had the same problem. At that point, we requested a refund because we did not want this issue to ruin our baby’s first birthday. Even that request was denied. With no reasonable alternative offered, we were left with no choice but to stay. The service was another major disappointment. Simple food orders took an extremely long time, whether ordered to the room or from the restaurant. Waiting for hours for basic dishes is unacceptable, particularly when travelling with a one-year-old child. I have visited Goa seven times and have stayed in hotels ranging from 2-star to 5-star properties, but I have never experienced this combination of poor room conditions, slow service, and such an unhelpful response to a genuine guest complaint. There was also an issue with hotel benefits/discounts. The rules and benefits communicated at check-in were presented differently when we actually tried to redeem them. Changing the rules at the time of redemption is extremely frustrating and leaves guests feeling misled. What disappointed us most was not just the room or the service—it was how our concerns were handled. We were travelling for our child’s first birthday, and instead of receiving basic assistance when we raised a genuine concern, we felt that our complaints were simply dismissed. For a property carrying the Marriott name, this experience was nowhere close to what we expected. This was one of the most disappointing hotel experiences we have had in Goa. We will not be returning to this property, and based on our experience, I would not recommend it to families travelling with young children. I sincerely hope the management takes this feedback seriously and reviews the condition of the rooms, guest complaint handling, service standards, and communication of hotel benefits.

I am writing to formally place on record my deep dissatisfaction regarding our recent stay at Club Mahindra Assonora. What was intended to be a pleasant, relaxing family holiday proved to be a frustrating ordeal, falling markedly below the service benchmarks associated with the Club Mahindra brand. Disorganized Arrival and Check-In : The arrival process was chaotic and unnecessarily delayed. Despite holding a valid, prepaid reservation via Agoda which your front desk team acknowledged having received via email staff struggled to locate and confirm our booking in a reasonable timeframe, causing an unwelcome and disruptive start to our stay. Lapses in Housekeeping, Basic Amenities, and Room Service Throughout our stay, routine requests required persistent follow-ups with little accountability: Unreasonable Delay for Infant Meals: While dining poolside, we requested baby food for our 10-month-old infant. It required several reminders and an unacceptably long delay of 30 to 40 minutes to provide basic nourishment for a baby. Lack of Prompt Guest Assistance: My footwear was inadvertently misplaced or taken by another guest near the pool. Given the extreme afternoon heat, the pool deck was scalding. Despite requesting a replacement pair of basic slippers, staff failed to assist over a 20-to-30-minute period, forcing me to walk barefoot across the hot deck to the room. Substandard Toiletries: Rather than providing standard body wash, the shower area was stocked with hand wash bottles. When questioned, housekeeping personnel casually stated that identical cleansing fluid is used interchangeably for hand wash and body wash—a severe compromise on standard hospitality hygiene protocols. External Delivery Mismanagement: I arranged for essential supplies to be delivered to the main security gate and checked if housekeeping could transfer the package to our room. Rather than communicating policies clearly, staff gave vague assurances ("let me check and update you"). After waiting half an hour with zero follow-up, I had to walk to the main perimeter gate myself to retrieve the parcel. Protracted Baggage Delays at Departure: During departure, housekeeping instructed us to leave our baggage in the room while we cleared billing at reception. Despite finalizing billing immediately, we were forced to wait nearly 30 minutes at the front desk for our luggage to be transferred via buggy. Unprofessional Front-Desk Conduct: The most concerning aspect was the dismissive conduct of the front-desk staff during checkout. When asked how our stay had been, I clearly highlighted these operational failures. Instead of registering the feedback or offering a standard apology, the representative immediately launched into a pitch for a Club Mahindra vacation membership. When I noted that our luggage was still delayed and ask the staff why when should get your search membership after search horrible service? The staff member retorted abrasively, "It's my work to ask you for the membership." It is alarming that desk personnel prioritize membership quotas over fundamental guest satisfaction and basic professional etiquette. Overall, Club Mahindra Assonora demonstrated acute operational mismanagement, inadequate staff training, and an absence of guest-centric hospitality.

We stayed at Taj Exotica for two days, and once again Taj reminded me why I keep going back to them. I’ve stayed at Taj properties quite a few times, and what I really love is how consistent their service is. No matter which Taj you walk into, there is a certain standard of hospitality you can expect. They almost never say no to a request, even when you know you might be asking for a little too much! 😄 They somehow find a way to make it happen, and more importantly, they do it with a smile. Taj Exotica itself is exceptional. The property is beautiful and extremely well maintained, the pool is easily one of the best I’ve seen, and having direct access to the beach makes it even better. The buggy service deserves a special mention too. You could probably ask them to pick you up and drop you off a million times a day and they would still arrive with a smile. What really stands out, though, is the staff. They genuinely seem to care about whether you’re comfortable. It never feels like they’re just putting up with your requests because it’s their job. The only thing I felt could be better was the food. We weren’t particularly impressed with it, but even there they surprised us. When we mentioned it, they actually told us we were welcome to order food from outside. I honestly wasn’t expecting that kind of flexibility from a five-star resort, and I really appreciated it. We had originally wanted to be here for our daughter’s first birthday, but unfortunately we couldn’t get the dates we needed. So after two days at Taj, we moved to another five-star property in South Goa for her birthday. And that was probably the best reminder of just how good Taj is. The other property had a huge room and a beautiful golf course, and honestly, that’s where the five-star experience ended. Everything else felt more like a three-star experience to me. It actually had me wondering how both properties could carry the same five-star rating. That stay made me realise that five stars on paper and a five-star experience are two very different things. Taj gets the experience right. Not just the rooms or the facilities, but the hospitality, the attention to detail, and the way the staff make you feel throughout your stay. After this trip, I think I’ve made up my mind. If there’s a Taj wherever I’m travelling, I probably won’t be looking too hard for another option. Thank you to the entire team at Taj Exotica for another wonderful Taj experience. ❤️

I visited Taj Exotica in July for my birthday dinner, and unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing. I honestly never expected this from a 5-star Taj property. I started calling Sala Da Pranzo in the afternoon—three times, but nobody answered. I then called reception, and they answered professionally within three rings. I asked them to connect me to the restaurant, but even after being transferred, nobody answered after several attempts. I called reception again and finally got connected to Miguel Arcanjo, where I managed to book a table. Later, I called Sala Da Pranzo again to ask about the menu. After 5–6 unanswered calls, someone finally picked up. The way this person spoke to me was extremely rude and unprofessional. His tone and attitude made me feel as though I was disturbing him simply by calling for information. Instead of politely answering a basic question about the menu, he spoke with obvious irritation and seemed eager to end the call. I received almost no useful information from him. For a property of this standard, this was completely unacceptable. The property itself is absolutely stunning—probably one of the most beautiful properties I have seen in Goa. Unfortunately, the service at Miguel Arcanjo was nowhere close to the standard expected from a 5-star hotel. There were only 2–3 tables, yet the staff were not attentive at all. We repeatedly had to call or search for someone for basic service. Even when the restaurant was almost empty, the staff were standing together chatting instead of attending to guests. When we asked for the bill, almost everyone had disappeared, and we waited around 20 minutes for the bill from one staff member who seemed relatively new. Coming to the food, the Prawn Tempura was good, although larger prawns would have been more appropriate for the price. The Chilli Mutton from the Monsoon Festival menu was average, the lobster was excellent, but the risotto was very disappointing. Overall, the food was mixed, but the service was the biggest disappointment. For the amount we spent, I genuinely don't feel the experience was worth it. Goa has many places offering much better food and service at the same or even lower price. Beautiful property, but as a non-residential guest, my experience was far below what I expected from Taj. Unfortunately, I would not recommend it for a special occasion based on this experience.

text_light: A Serene Beachfront Escape in the Heart of Morjim We recently stayed at Montego Bay Beach Village in a Log Cabin, and it was a wonderful experience. We tried the Prawns, Kingfish, and Pomfret, along with chicken and veg dishes—all were delicious. Convenience: The location is unbeatable. Having a two-wheeler rental and taxi stand right at the main gate made exploring so much easier. No need to hunt for a scooter! Amenities: The room had everything we needed (AC, hot water, fridge, etc.), and the swimming pool was a great spot to cool off.
