text_light: My 5th visit to Montego Bay Beach Resort was shockingly bad and honestly quite disturbing. The experience started on a poor note itself, reception staff were cold and unwelcoming, and the breakfast was below average. For ₹10,000 per night, this level of service is unacceptable. Some kind of tournament was going because of which the resort was very crowded and benches were always occupied! But the real issue is something far more serious. There is an aggressive taxi mafia operating right outside the resort. When I asked at reception for a cab to travel 15–16 km (Fat fish Calangute), I was quoted ₹1,200. The same ride on Goa Miles was around ₹500. When I checked with the group sitting at the resort gate, they quoted the exact same inflated fare. It felt like guests are being forced into overpaying. Because of this, I avoided travelling and limited my plans. The situation escalated on the day of departure. I had booked an external cab, but as soon as it arrived, a group of these taxi operators (goons) surrounded the vehicle, started shouting, abusing, and threatening the driver. They were forcing my cab driver to leave. This happened in front of my child. What’s worse? The resort staff did absolutely nothing. No support, no intervention, nothing. When I asked for help or even a police contact, they said they didn’t have it. Calling 100 was useless. Finally, a person from the resort (possibly the manager) showed up, but instead of helping, he told my driver that “these cabs are not allowed here.” That statement said everything. It clearly feels like the resort is either complicit or simply doesn’t care about guest safety while this harassment happens at their own entrance. I somehow managed to leave, but the entire experience was intimidating and deeply unsettling. Maybe few negative review won’t matter but as a guest who once trusted this place, I felt it was important to share the experience so that others can make an informed decision and avoid going through what I did.

text_light: ​If you are looking for that classic, laid-back North Goa vibe where the ocean is your backyard, Montego Bay Beach Resort in Morjim is a solid contender. I recently stayed here as a guest for a destination wedding, and the setting provided a truly magical backdrop for the celebrations. ​Unbeatable Location: The resort is incredibly easy to find and offers seamless access to the shoreline. If your idea of a vacation is rolling out of bed and being on the sand in sixty seconds, this is the place. ​Perfect for Weddings: As a destination wedding venue, it’s fantastic. The transition from the ceremony to the party is effortless, and the "toes-in-the-sand" experience is exactly what you want for a Goa wedding. I would highly recommend it for events. ​Exceptional Service (Special Shoutout to Joel!): The staff here are the real stars. They are super friendly and attentive. I want to give a special mention to Joel from the restaurant staff—he was outstanding and made sure we were well taken care of throughout the wedding festivities. ​Beach-View Dining: The restaurant overlooks the Arabian Sea. It’s the perfect spot for a sunset drink or a breezy morning coffee while watching the waves. ​The Trade-offs. ​Room Condition: The rooms are impressively spacious—plenty of room to spread out—but they are definitely starting to show their age. You might notice some wear and tear in the fixtures and decor that a refresh would easily fix. ​Parking Woes: If you’re driving down or renting a car, be prepared. The parking space is quite limited, which can be a bit of a headache during peak ceremony times when many guests arrive at once. ​The Food: While the view from the restaurant is 10/10, the daily kitchen offerings are currently a bit hit-or-miss. The menu needs some improvement in terms of flavor and variety to truly match the premium feel of the location. ​

My stay at Dhanrains Moonlight Retreat Cottages was a genuinely pleasant and relaxing experience. If you are looking for a place where you can step away from the noise and rush of everyday life and simply enjoy some peace and quiet, this retreat is definitely worth considering. The surroundings have a lovely natural feel, making the property a nice choice for anyone who wants to spend some quality time away from crowded and busy places. The cottages provide a comfortable setting where you can relax, unwind, and enjoy the slower pace of a retreat. The cottages themselves are comfortable and inviting. They have the kind of cozy atmosphere that makes you feel at ease after a day of travelling or exploring the area. The overall environment is suitable for couples, families, or even small groups of friends who want to spend some time together in a relaxed setting. Another thing I appreciated was the hospitality and overall experience. The staff were pleasant and helpful, and the stay felt welcoming rather than overly formal. Good hospitality can make a big difference during a holiday, and the friendly atmosphere here certainly added to my experience. The property is also a good option for people who enjoy being close to nature. Instead of feeling like you are staying in a typical commercial hotel, there is more of a retreat-like feeling, which is exactly what I was looking for. Mornings and evenings were especially enjoyable because of the peaceful surroundings. I also liked the fact that the place offers an opportunity to slow down and disconnect for a while. Sometimes the best part of a trip is not a packed itinerary but simply having a comfortable place to sit, relax, talk with your companions, and enjoy the surroundings. Dhanrains Moonlight Retreat Cottages creates that kind of atmosphere. Overall, I would describe my experience as comfortable, peaceful, and refreshing. It is a place I would consider returning to, especially when I want a quiet break and a more relaxed holiday experience. Whether you are travelling as a couple, with family, or with friends, the property offers a pleasant setting for spending some quality time together. Overall, Dhanrains Moonlight Retreat Cottages is a lovely choice for anyone seeking peace, comfort, natural surroundings, and a relaxing getaway. I had a very enjoyable stay and would happily recommend it to others looking for a quiet retreat.

All our wishes and requests were fulfilled almost immediately. The owner is a truly warm person. And of course, the soul of the hotel is its general manager, Kali! An amazing person who is always there and always ready to help. By the end of our stay, we practically became family 😅 For me, this attitude is what defines it. The second reason is the location. It's a 2-minute walk from the sea. And that's perfect, because all the noise from the party scene and the music that starts in the evenings is hidden from the hotel, allowing you to relax peacefully. The third reason is the hotel itself. It's clean and tidy. The rooms on the second floor are amazing! Freshly painted white walls (a rarity in India 😅), fresh wooden furniture, lots of light from the large panoramic window, light curtains, and clean, good-quality bed linens and towels (also a treasured rarity in India). A decent shower. A kettle in the room. A refrigerator on each floor. Free water is available at reception! This is my first time in India and Goa. And I'm so glad that my acquaintance with this state began with Ramdev. I definitely recommend it!

Worst Stay of My Life. Sinq Beach Morjim — one of the worst hotel experiences I have ever had. I have stayed at many hotels, but my experience at Sinq Beach Morjim was genuinely shocking and deeply disappointing. This was not just a bad stay — the overall condition of the property made me extremely uncomfortable and, at times, genuinely concerned about hygiene and safety. The entire place had a negative, eerie atmosphere. Personally, I felt so uncomfortable there that the property actually gave me a “haunted” feeling. That may sound dramatic, but that was honestly how the place felt during my stay. And then came the actual problems:. Approach road: Absolutely terrible and inconvenient. The first impression itself was disappointing. Hygiene & maintenance: The condition of the room and fittings was nowhere close to what one would expect from a decent hotel. Shower head: Heavily rusted and visibly unhygienic. Fungus / dampness: Visible fungal growth and damp-looking patches in multiple areas. Walls & ceiling: Cracks, stains and signs of poor maintenance were clearly visible. Electric kettle: This was particularly disgusting — the kettle had foul-smelling liquid/residue inside it. I wouldn't even consider using it. Room fixtures/furniture: Several things looked old, damaged, poorly maintained and simply neglected. Food: Ridiculously disappointing. Definitely not what I expected from a hotel charging guests for a stay and meals. Staff conduct: During my stay, I personally observed staff members drinking alcohol in another room, which added to my discomfort and concerns about the overall professionalism of the property. Sense of safety: I simply did not feel safe or comfortable staying here. The attached photographs speak for themselves — rusty fixtures, visible deterioration, cracks, dampness/fungal-looking patches, damaged fittings and an overall lack of proper upkeep. What bothered me most is that these aren't minor cosmetic issues. Basic cleanliness, hygiene, maintenance and guest comfort should be non-negotiable in any hotel. My honest recommendation: AVOID THIS PLACE. If you are planning a Goa trip and looking for a comfortable, clean and safe place to stay, I would strongly suggest looking elsewhere rather than taking a chance with Sinq Beach Morjim. This review is based on my personal experience during my stay, and I am sharing it because I would not want another traveller to spend their hard-earned money and end up having the kind of experience I had. One of the worst hotel stays I have experienced in my lifetime.

Disappointing Experience for a Large Group — Poor Maintenance & Lack of Vibe ​We visited SinQ in July as a group of 20 people, drawn in by the high online recommendations and strong reviews. Unfortunately, our experience was very disappointing. For a venue with so much hype, the place felt completely dead with no music or atmosphere to speak of. ​The cleanliness standards were sub-par, and the food was average at best. What made it more frustrating was the total lack of maintenance on their key features—the property highlights a unique setup with a pool/jacuzzi area, but the jacuzzi was non-functional and unhygienic. ​The only saving grace of the entire visit was the direct access to Morjim Beach. At this point, I’m not sure whether I stayed at a hotel or participated in an escape-room challenge. I booked this room based on its ratings, but honestly, it was nowhere near worth the rating or the money we paid. I stayed at IK London Hotel near AIG, Somajiguda, Hyderabad. First, I would like to appreciate the gentleman at the reception. He was extremely polite, gentle, and well-mannered, and his professionalism was commendable. However, the room cleanliness needs significant improvement. Although the room appeared to be cleaned, there were many small cockroaches on the towels, bed, chair, and even in the bathroom. This was very disappointing and unacceptable. The most upsetting experience was at the hotel restaurant during lunch on 21st July. I asked the waiter, Ramesh, about the available vegetable dishes. He informed me that paneer was available, but I specifically ordered only Jeera Aloo, buttermilk, and papad. He handed me the menu, and at no point did I order Mix Veg. Later, another staff member came to reconfirm my order and mentioned that I had ordered Mix Veg along with Jeera Aloo, buttermilk, and papad. I immediately clarified that I had never ordered Mix Veg. I was dining alone and could not possibly finish two full vegetable dishes. Instead of correcting the mistake, Ramesh insisted that I had ordered both dishes and said that since they had already prepared them, I had to accept both. His behavior was rude, unprofessional, and disrespectful. I had to approach the reception to report the incident. We chose this hotel because one of the doctors at AIG Hospital recommended it. My husband had undergone surgery and was in the ICU, and I came to the restaurant hoping to have a peaceful lunch during a very stressful time. Being treated so disrespectfully by a staff member was deeply upsetting. While the rest of the staff were courteous, one employee's behavior can significantly affect a guest's overall experience. Hospitality is not just about providing accommodation and food—it is about treating guests with respect. We had planned to stay here for four more days, but after this experience, we have decided not to continue our stay. Even if it means walking a little farther to reach AIG Hospital, I would rather choose a place where guests are treated with dignity and respect.

Before booking, please understand that this is an inn, not a hotel. An inn offers basic facilities and limited services, while a hotel usually provides more comfort and full-service hospitality. If you keep this difference in mind, your expectations will be realistic. We booked a three-person occupancy room because the two-person option felt too small. They initially quoted ₹2000+ for an AC room, but we negotiated and settled at a better price. Make sure you finalize everything on the spot and take a confirmation slip. Do not leave anything verbal. The room was okay. Bathroom and geyser were working fine. There was no balcony. There were windows but they could not be opened, and there was no view as another building was right outside. WiFi was very good. Housekeeping was done whenever we requested bedsheet changes or cleaning. The dustbin was kept outside, and whenever we informed them, they cleared it. So service was manageable. Food options are easily available nearby. The biggest advantage is that it is just a two-minute walking distance from Yashoda Hospitals, which makes it very convenient for patients and attendants. Right in front of this inn, there is a big hotel where we inquired for one day and the tariff was around ₹6000. So you can compare and decide what suits your budget and comfort level. I do not know about other occupancy types or rooms. I am only sharing my experience with the room we stayed in. I heard that the top floor rooms have a common balcony, but we did not stay there. This place is fine if you understand what an inn offers. Suitable for couples and people who are okay with non-veg surroundings. Elderly guests might find it a bit suffocating. Not recommended for long stays. We stayed for 7 days, and that was enough. Hope this helps future visitors decide better.

Whether you’re traveling for work, shopping, or sightseeing, this location adds great value to your stay. The room pricing is also very reasonable. A **Non-AC room costs ₹1500**, and an **AC room is ₹1700**, which is quite fair considering the location and the amenities provided. The rooms are clean, well-maintained, and spacious enough for both solo travelers and couples. The beds are comfortable, and the bathrooms are kept hygienic with regular cleaning. The staff here is polite, responsive, and always ready to assist with any requests, making the stay even more pleasant. Check-in and check-out were smooth, and the overall property feels safe and secure. The surrounding area has plenty of eateries, grocery stores, and transport options, which is a big plus for outstation guests. If you’re looking for a reliable and budget-friendly place near Punjagutta, Sai Manikanta Residency is a great choice. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone planning to stay in this part of Hyderabad.

I recently had the pleasure of staying with my family at Neem Tree Apartments at Kapadia Lane, near Irrum Manzil Metro Station, and overall, it was a delightful experience. The rooms were beautifully designed, offering a cozy and inviting ambiance that made my stay truly enjoyable. All the amenities provided were top-notch, contributing to a comfortable and convenient stay. If you plan accordingly and buy a few groceries, you can save a lot on restaurant bills as there is a refrigerator, all necessary utensils, etc. to make you feel like you're at home. While it didn't significantly impact my stay, I believe it's important to mention for the sake of transparency. Despite these minor drawbacks, my overall experience at Neem Tree was positive. A Comfortable Stay with Some Areas to Improve — Overall ⭐⭐⭐½/5 1. Stay — ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 The stay at Taj Deccan was tranquil, cozy and quite serene. The room had all the amenities I needed, and I had no complaints on that front. My room overlooked the garden at the back, which made the experience even more pleasant and relaxing. Overall, a very comfortable and peaceful stay. 2. Food & Other Experiences — ⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4/5 The food selection was good, with plenty of options available. A little more consistency with seasoning would help, as a few dishes needed some salt. A special mention for the hummus—it was really tasty and definitely stood out. One thing to note regarding the breakfast buffet: make sure you reach well before 10:30 AM. I reached at around 10:20 AM and, when the 10:30 AM bell rang, the buffet was cleared. This was a little unexpected, particularly since I had reached before the stated closing time, and I couldn't get several items I wanted. Fortunately, I managed to get the aloo paratha. There was also a communication issue with the breakfast service. At one point, we requested a few items from the serving staff and were told they would be brought to us. However, after waiting for around 20 minutes, when we followed up, we were told that service had already stopped at 11:00 AM. Clear communication about the service cut-off would have avoided the confusion. One more point worth mentioning is the valet parking experience. I have owned my car for around three years and have never experienced a battery drain. However, after the overnight valet parking, the battery was completely drained. I had to call RSA, and the technician jump-started the car and checked the battery, confirming that the battery itself was fine. He mentioned that a button may have been left switched on overnight, which could have caused the battery to drain. Given this experience, I would suggest guests consider parking their cars themselves, if possible, and ensure the car is properly switched off and secured before leaving it overnight. Overall, the stay was pleasant, particularly because of the peaceful ambience and garden-facing room. However, the breakfast-service communication and valet-parking experience brought down the overall experience for me. Overall experience: ⭐⭐⭐½/5

text_light: Very Disappointing Experience with Our Corporate Event I am sharing this review based on my personal experience with Deccan Sarai, Hyderabad, during our corporate event on 19th September 2026. We had booked the entire sixth floor — Cilantro Hall, Mint Hall and the passage area — well in advance and made the required advance payment based on the understanding that the space would be exclusively available for our event. During the planning, I was in regular contact with Lakshmi (Banquet Sales Manager) Hotel Deccan Serai , who was very responsive and repeatedly assured me that everything would be taken care of. I had also informed her in advance that I would visit the hotel on the evening of 18th September to check the arrangements, and she assured me that she would be available. However, when I reached the hotel, Lakshmi was not available. More importantly, we discovered that Mint Hall had been converted into the hotel's restaurant area, while the passage area was being used for a buffet for other hotel guests. This was completely different from what had been discussed and paid for. What was most disappointing was the lack of accountability. There was no clear point of contact who could explain the situation or provide an immediate solution. I repeatedly tried contacting Lakshmi, but could not reach her. We spent almost three hours trying to find someone who could take ownership of the issue, and eventually we were told that she was unavailable for a few days and that others did not have proper information about our arrangements. AV Coordination Was Also a Major Concern The AV arrangements were equally disappointing. Vikas, who was provided as the AV contact, was not available on time, and the AV setup was delayed by at least an hour. The technician available at the venue was not adequately prepared, and we were initially told that certain microphones, cables and other AV requirements were not available, despite these requirements having been discussed beforehand. This also affected our videography. We had arranged two professional videographers, but the required audio access/cable was not provided to them. As a result, the final videos had poor audio quality, which was extremely disappointing after investing in professional event coverage. The bigger concern throughout was that there was no accountable person available to quickly resolve these issues. I would, however, like to appreciate Chandrakant from the housekeeping team, who genuinely tried to help us on the event day and supported us wherever possible. Unexpected issues can happen during any event. However, for a corporate event planned months in advance, clients expect proper communication, coordination and a responsible point of contact. In our case, the main concerns were: Booked space not being provided as committed No advance communication about the changes No backup when the primary contact was unavailable No one taking ownership of the situation for several hours Significant delay in AV setup Poor coordination of AV requirements Videographers not receiving the required audio access, affecting the final videos We travelled from Mumbai and planned the event based on the commitments made by the hotel. The experience created unnecessary stress just hours before a major corporate event. Based on this experience, I would not recommend Deccan Sarai for corporate events . I sincerely hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves its communication, internal coordination, AV management and accountability for future corporate clients.

A Refined and Memorable Stay at Deccan Serai, Hyderabad. My visit to Hyderabad was made particularly enjoyable by my three-night stay at Deccan Serai Hotel. From Friday through Monday, the hotel provided a level of comfort, hospitality and attentive service that genuinely enhanced my overall experience of the city. What impressed me most was the quality of the service. The staff were consistently courteous, gracious and exceptionally responsive. Every request was attended to with efficiency and, more importantly, with a warmth that made the interaction feel personal rather than merely procedural. There is a certain understated elegance to hospitality when a guest feels looked after without ever feeling overwhelmed by attention, and Deccan Serai manages to achieve that rather well. The hotel itself offers a comfortable and welcoming ambience, with well-maintained spaces and rooms that provide a pleasant retreat after a day spent exploring or working in Hyderabad. Everything felt orderly, clean and thoughtfully managed, allowing me to simply relax and enjoy my stay. I particularly appreciated the consistency of the experience. Over the course of three nights, the courtesy and responsiveness of the team remained exemplary. It is often the finer details—the prompt response to a request, the genuine smile, the willingness to go the extra mile—that distinguish a good hotel from a truly memorable one. Deccan Serai certainly understands the importance of these details. There are, of course, many hotels one can choose from in Hyderabad, but what makes a stay memorable is rarely just the room or the facilities. It is the feeling one carries away at the end of it. In my case, I left Deccan Serai with a very positive impression of the hotel and, particularly, of its people. A gracious, comfortable and thoroughly enjoyable stay. I would be very happy to return to Deccan Serai on my next visit to Hyderabad and would have no hesitation in recommending it to others looking for refined hospitality, attentive service and a genuinely pleasant stay.

text_light: I had a disastrous stay at Skyla Hitech and would strongly advise everyone to avoid this property. For the high prices charged, the experience falls drastically short. Rooms & Odor: The rooms are completely mediocre and not worth the rate. Worse, the entire floor and the rooms carry a persistent, sickening drainage smell that makes staying here unbearable. Housekeeping Harassment: The staff has zero respect for guest privacy or rest. They will ring the doorbell continuously until you get out of bed to answer. Even if you are asleep, they refuse to move on or come back later; they force you to physically open the door just to tell them to return later. Impractical Laundry Service: Ironing and laundry are outsourced rather than managed in-house. Even for basic pressing, they demand an absurd 24-hour turnaround time. Subpar Food & Hygiene: The breakfast buffet is terrible—tasteless, greasy, and poorly prepared. To make matters worse, the kitchen staff cuts the fresh fruit with knives used for cooked/savory food, making the fruit taste like the rest of the buffet items. Overall, an utterly mismanaged property with poor hygiene and disruptive staff. Look elsewhere.

The location of the property is excellent, centrally located near Statue Circle, and being a well-known brand, we expected a certain standard of service. We stayed here from 17th to 19th September and, while the stay itself was comfortable, two incidents left us extremely disappointed. On the evening of 18th September, we ordered two cups of tea and were charged ₹177, which was quite reasonable. The very next day, we ordered the same two cups of tea and were charged ₹370. When we questioned the difference, no one was able to give us a satisfactory explanation. What was even more surprising was the quantity—the tea served was not even half a cup. In all my years of staying at hotels, I have never experienced something like this. However, the more serious concern was regarding my sunglasses. I had kept them in the room, and the room was cleaned by housekeeping that same day. That was the last time I saw them. I immediately informed the reception and asked if the sunglasses had been found. After searching everywhere myself and waiting for two days, I personally returned to the hotel and requested them to check again. I was simply told that nothing had been deposited with Lost & Found. What disappointed me most was the way the matter was handled. I expected the hotel to at least check with the housekeeping staff member who had cleaned our room and make a genuine effort to trace the missing item. Instead, there seemed to be no proper follow-up or explanation. A comfortable stay can easily be overshadowed by experiences like these. For a reputed property, guests expect not only good rooms and location, but also consistency in billing, accountability and a more responsive approach when a guest reports a missing personal belonging. If someone from the hotel manage this Google account I hope they still can give it a try to find those sunglasses.

A Memorable 2-Night Stay at Hotel Diggi Palace, Jaipur We had a wonderful 2-night stay at Hotel Diggi Palace, Jaipur, and it was truly a memorable experience. The ambience and heritage charm of the palace were simply outstanding, with beautiful architecture, lush greenery, peaceful courtyards, and a luxurious feel throughout the property. One of the highlights was seeing beautiful peacocks and monkeys around the palace, which added to the unique experience of staying in such a natural and heritage-rich environment. 🦚🌿 The rooms were luxurious and comfortable, and the swimming pool was a great place to relax. We also enjoyed delicious meals, and the live music during dinner created a wonderful atmosphere. The candlelight dinner was especially memorable. 🕯️🎶 The staff were very supportive, polite, and welcoming throughout our stay. Their hospitality made our experience even better. Overall, Hotel Diggi Palace is a perfect blend of heritage, nature, luxury, great food, and warm hospitality. We thoroughly enjoyed our 2 nights and would happily recommend it to anyone visiting Jaipur. 5/5 — A truly beautiful and unforgettable stay! ❤️

0/5 if I could — Extremely Disappointing Family Stay I stayed at Varanasi by Jai Club with my family from 5 September 2026 to 7 September 2026, and the experience was extremely disappointing. The room condition was pathetic. Basic daily-use items that one would normally expect in a hotel room were not available. To make matters worse, the flush was broken, which is a basic facility that should have been checked before handing over the room to a guest. Breakfast was included in my Booking.com reservation, but there were only two options available, and unfortunately, the quality and taste of both were very disappointing. For a family stay, this was nowhere near the standard I expected. The payment experience was another major issue. I had made the reservation through Booking.com and requested a payment link. The staff/management appeared unfamiliar with the process of generating or handling an online payment link. For a hotel operating in the modern hospitality industry, this was surprisingly inconvenient. There was also a clear discrepancy in the billing. The invoice provided to me showed ₹9,086, while I was charged ₹9,250. I had not applied any Booking.com discount coupon, so I expected a clear explanation for the difference. Unfortunately, the matter was not handled professionally. What disappointed me most was the attitude of the management. When I tried to explain my concerns, they did not properly listen or address the issues. At one point, the management person left the counter instead of discussing the matter with me, while I was being pressured to make the full payment. I was travelling with my family, so I expected basic cleanliness, working facilities, decent food, transparent billing, and professional customer service. Unfortunately, my experience fell short in all of these areas. My rating: 0/5 if the platform allowed it. If negative ratings were available, I would rate this property -5. This did not feel like a proper hotel; it felt like a poorly managed dharamshala, and in some respects, even worse. Based strictly on my experience during 5–7 September 2026, I would not recommend Baramasi by Jai Club, particularly to families. I hope the management takes these issues seriously and improves the basic standards of housekeeping, maintenance, food, billing transparency, and guest handling.

We had to ask repeatedly for hot water, sometimes waiting for fifteen minutes, and there were even times when we had none at all. For a hotel of this caliber, this is a major issue. Other basic amenities were also lacking: no toilet paper upon arrival, no soap, and inadequate housekeeping in the room. Finally, the hotel tried to charge us for a bottle of water we had at breakfast (five times the price of a bottle, 104 rupees) even though we had never been told it was extra. We had to complain to reception to get this absurdity resolved. Overall, the experience was completely different from the price paid or what was advertised on Booking.com. hotel_name: Chitra Katha - A Story Per Stay
text_light: Absolutely loved our 3-day stay here! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ This hotel offers excellent value for money and was one of the most economical stays we’ve experienced without compromising on comfort or quality. The property was spotlessly clean, centrally located, and made exploring the city incredibly convenient. The rooftop restaurant was another highlight, offering beautiful views and a lovely atmosphere. What truly made our stay special was the personalized hospitality from Anshu. He took the time to share the history of the city and prepared a customized itinerary along with a detailed map, including recommended food spots. This thoughtful guidance helped us explore the city efficiently and discover some amazing local experiences. The staff were always polite, helpful, and welcoming. As female travelers, we felt completely safe throughout our stay, making it an excellent choice for solo female travelers as well. The food was outstanding. The Laal Maas prepared by Anshu was absolutely delicious, and the Chicken Stew is a must-try for anyone visiting the hotel. Also, don’t skip the breakfast package—the breakfast combos are fresh, tasty, and great value for money. A special thanks to Ballu Bhaiya, our auto driver, who made sightseeing effortless. His service was economical, reliable, and perfectly aligned with the customized itinerary prepared by Anshu. He was patient, punctual, polite, and always mindful of our comfort and safety, making our travel experience smooth and stress-free. Highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a clean, safe, economical, and memorable stay with exceptional hospitality. We would happily stay here again!

I chose this hotel after checking its ratings on Agoda, but unfortunately, the actual experience was completely different from what I expected. The ratings did not reflect my experience at all. 1. Cleanliness: The rooms were dirty when we arrived for check-in. The almirah was even worse—you could easily see dust just by running your finger over it. The windows were extremely dirty and were not cleaned even after we complained. As for the “view,” there was garbage all over the area outside the window. The floor in front of the rooms was also very dirty. I have attached pictures for reference. 2. Broken doors and locks: The knobs/locks of both the main door and bathroom door were broken. We had to struggle just to lock the main door, and the bathroom door could not be locked at all, no matter how much we tried. 3. Basic room service: I asked for a jug and glasses for drinking water. I was told that they only provide water in bottles, and they provided only one glass for the entire room. Later, when I asked the receptionist for water, I was told that the room service staff was away and that if it was urgent, I should come downstairs and collect it from the counter. 4. Receptionist behaviour: The receptionist was extremely rude and did not know how to speak to or deal with customers professionally. The way he responded to our requests was very disappointing. 5. No working kitchen: One of the biggest problems was that the hotel's kitchen was not operational. This was not clearly mentioned anywhere before booking. We had a lot of difficulty getting food and even tea. When I asked the receptionist about it, he simply said that they did not have enough staff, so the kitchen was closed, and told us to order food through Zomato or Swiggy. 6. Room type was not provided as booked: I specifically booked a Deluxe Room with two separate beds, but we were given a room with a single double bed. When I raised the issue, I was told that no twin-bed room was available at that time. However, the hotel had confirmed through messages that all the requested conditions would be fulfilled. Overall, this was a very disappointing and frustrating experience. Basic cleanliness, maintenance, customer service, and the facilities mentioned during booking were not up to the expected standard. My advice to other travellers is to carefully check the recent reviews and confirm the available facilities directly with the hotel before booking. For me, this was a terrible decision and a very unpleasant stay.

text_light: Had made booking for Hotel Hari Mahal online and trust me I haven't had a worse experience in my life than this. This is a complete fraud since the hotel professes heritage experience while the room shown is not part of the hotel but a separate poorly maintained apartment complex with residents living. The room itself was part of 3BHK apartment with a common lobby and pantry which was mightily creepy and scary to stay with wife and kids. The room itself was small, dingy, poorly maintained, with dirty linen and without even the basic amenities. Even a Dharamshala offers a better experience than this. The person manning the reception was extremely rude and unprofessional and refused to cancel booking and refund. He also refused to change room and demanded entire amount for a fresh booking in case we wanted to shift to heritage room in the hotel. Was struck at this dump for the night and cut a very poor face before my family. My kids refused to sleep in the bed, use the washroom or have breakfast and had to literally force them into it.

The property promotes itself as a luxury and pet-friendly stay, but the experience felt comfortable only for guests without pets. While pets are technically allowed, reaching the rooms requires climbing four floors without any lift support, which can be extremely difficult for pet owners as well as dogs, especially larger or older pets. The staff was polite overall, though the service was somewhat slow. Initially, there seemed to be hesitation in helping with luggage, but the issue was eventually managed. The room was decent and the locality was fine for a short stay. However, one major concern for pet owners is the lack of suitable open space nearby for walking pets or taking them out for basic needs, making it inconvenient for both the dog and the owner. Another disappointing aspect was the absence of a menu card with clearly mentioned prices. This lack of transparency resulted in unexpectedly high food charges, which came as an unpleasant surprise at checkout. Overall, the property may suit regular travelers looking for a decent stay, but for people traveling with pets, especially dogs, the experience can be quite challenging.

Pachamama Hostel, Jaipur – A Hidden Gem for Chill Travelers Our stay at Pachamama Hostel was an absolute delight. Though it's not in the bustling city center like Sindhi Camp or Hawa Mahal, it's just a 5-minute walk from Civil Lines Metro Station, making it easy to get around. The hostel is in a local neighborhood, where kids greet you warmly (and curiously stare, which is quite adorable!). The rooftop and spacious common areas were perfect for relaxing, and we spent most of our time there. On the second day, we even asked if we could paint on the wall, and the staff happily agreed—it turned into such a memorable experience. Now, let’s talk about the food—it’s simply incredible. We loved it so much that we ended up eating all three meals here on some days. It’s fresh, flavorful, and made with love. Another highlight? The sweetest cat lives here! She was pregnant during our visit, and we recently heard she gave birth to seven kittens. That gave us the perfect excuse to return, check on her, and enjoy a beer while writing this review. If you’re looking for a peaceful, chill place to stay in Jaipur, Pachamama is the answer. Highly recommended!

This was, without a doubt, one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had. The owner’s behavior was unbelievably disrespectful. Apparently, basic manners—especially when speaking to elders and teachers—are too much to expect here. We were subjected to unnecessary mental harassment throughout the night over a payment dispute, and the owner even shouted at our teachers. That was the absolute low point. The entire incident was recorded, and after their behavior was called out, they were eventually forced to apologize. An apology doesn’t magically erase the way guests were treated. I’ve also seen the owner’s responses to other reviews, where he seems more interested in defending himself than accepting criticism. Don’t worry, I’m not trying to take away your customers. Anyone who wants to experience this level of hospitality is welcome to spend their money here and discover the experience for themselves. And one more thing: please learn to be a little less aggressive with guests taking water bottles. They are going to pay for them. There is absolutely no need to repeatedly poke, pressure, or lecture people with “you have to buy it first.” Jaipur has plenty of hotels. Unfortunately, we chose this one—and that was a mistake we definitely won’t repeat. Excellent Value, Great Location & Warm Hospitality During our recent family holiday in Kerala, we stayed at Classic Fort Inn & Suites, Kochi for three nights. Our plan was simple—we wanted a comfortable hotel in a convenient location where we could relax after a full day of exploring the beautiful city of Kochi. For that purpose, this hotel was an excellent choice. We booked two rooms for our family, and from check-in to check-out, the experience was smooth and pleasant. The hotel is well maintained, clean, and offers everything you would expect from a good three to four-star property. One of its biggest advantages is the location. It made it very convenient for us to explore Kochi’s major attractions, restaurants, and shopping areas without spending too much time travelling. It is definitely a great base for anyone planning to spend most of the day sightseeing. Our package included breakfast and dinner. Since we were out exploring the city during the day, we mainly enjoyed the breakfast at the hotel. The breakfast buffet had a good variety, with a strong focus on authentic Kerala specialities such as idli, dosa, and other local favourites. There was also a live cooking station where fresh omelettes and other items were prepared on request, which was a nice touch. The restaurant staff were courteous, attentive, and always ready to help. Although breakfast officially ends at 10:00 a.m., we found the team to be accommodating and guest-friendly, ensuring everyone could enjoy their meal comfortably. Overall, the hotel offers clean rooms, good food, friendly service, and excellent value for money. It may not be a luxury resort, but it delivers exactly what it promises—a comfortable, well-located stay with warm hospitality. I would happily recommend Classic Fort Inn & Suites to families, couples, and travellers looking for a convenient and affordable base to explore Kochi. Thank you to the entire team for making our stay comfortable and enjoyable. A well-deserved 5 out of 5 stars!

hotel_name: The Hosteller Fort Kochi, Ocean Edge
text_light: Having been a regular at this establishment before the change of ownership, I wanted to try it again. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing: the hotel has lost all its former charm and friendliness, becoming a cold and impersonal place. Here are the main points of my stay: Reception and lack of flexibility: Upon arrival, the young woman at reception (clearly lacking training or experience) refused to let me look at the room before paying, curtly referring me to the "online photos." She gave me the same categorical refusal and made no attempt to find a solution when, as a foreign tourist, I asked if it was possible to pay in cash to avoid any potential banking issues. Endless check-in process: Check-in was a real nightmare. Leaving all administrative tasks to the customer might have been understandable during the COVID period, but today, given the price of the service, it's unacceptable. After a long journey, wasting 30 to 40 minutes filling everything out yourself on a screen is tedious and very uncomfortable. Total loss of human contact: Even though I'm very comfortable with technology and modernity, here it's too much. By digitizing everything, we're not saving time, we're wasting it. The staff is unwelcoming, doesn't smile, and seems overwhelmed by this factory-like operation. Room and pricing issues: The first room wasn't suitable because the electrical wiring for the light near the bed in the dormitory was damaged, which is very dangerous! There was a risk of electrocution during the night, so I had to change to a higher category. They initially tried to charge me the full price, even though the rate on Booking.com was significantly lower. Fortunately, the person who took over for this second reservation was much more professional: she was able to adapt, offered me suitable payment options, and provided proper assistance. It's a shame, because this kind of adaptability and service should be the norm from the moment of arrival. A real effort to train new staff and a return to a more personal welcome are essential. As for me, I will not be returning to this establishment.

I stayed at Hotel Palmyra Grand Inn for 2 days, and this was easily one of the most disappointing hotel experiences I've had during my travels. The hotel claims to be a 3-star property, but the condition of the rooms I received was nowhere close to what I expected from a 3-star hotel. The first room was very dirty and had a strong foul smell. The AC was terribly maintained. The window also wouldn't close properly—it only closed around 80%. I informed the reception, and a staff member came and simply told me that it was "busted" and that I shouldn't worry because nobody could open it. That was not reassuring at all. I had booked a Queen/King-sized bed, but I was given a room with two separate single beds. When I questioned this, I was basically told that the other rooms were also arranged like that. I requested a room change, and the next day I was moved to another room. Unfortunately, the second room was even worse. The bathroom had a terrible smell, and the flush wasn't working properly. I had to use a bucket to pour water into the toilet. The TV display had what appeared to be fungus/moisture inside the screen, and the AC was not cooling properly even at 16°C. In fact, the room felt more comfortable after switching off the AC and using the fan. One or two of the staff members were genuinely helpful, but unfortunately, several others seemed to have very little understanding of basic hospitality and customer service. What makes this even more disappointing is that I booked through Agoda, where the photos showed a much better-looking room. The actual rooms I received were nowhere close to those photos. I've travelled and stayed in many different places, and this is honestly the first hotel stay that has left me this disappointed. I remained calm and respectful throughout my stay despite everything, but the experience was extremely frustrating. If you're booking this property, I strongly recommend confirming the exact room you're going to receive before paying. The room shown online and the room you may actually get can be very different.

Our stay at Taj Malabar was planned as a small family break after our daughter Priyanka’s wedding. We went with the newlyweds, Priyanka and Rohit, and Rohit’s parents, Vijaya Baskar and Krishna Priya. What we expected to be a relaxed family getaway turned into a truly wonderful stay. The experience actually started before we arrived. Paul from Reservations helped coordinate our three bookings and the arrangements for the newlyweds. Elizabeth then connected with me and took care of every small detail before our arrival. I had also written to Lalith Viswakumar, Area Director – Operations & General Manager, and Ankur Gupta responded and personally followed through. That personal attention continued throughout our stay. The welcome was lovely, with Swapna and her team, followed by Shalabha and Cinderella at the Front Office taking very good care of us. Priyanka and Rohit had secretly upgraded both sets of parents to suites as a surprise. Then Cinderella, after checking with Ankur, surprised Radhika and me further with an upgrade to the Grand Suite. A lovely gesture which we certainly did not expect. The renovated rooms are beautifully done, spacious and very comfortable. Food was another highlight. Chef Nihil and especially Chef Anoop took personal care of us throughout. Soorya made our meals at Pepper absolutely fantabulous. Fatimah, Joman, Ajit, Alex and the entire Pepper team were wonderful. Babu at the bar looked after us equally well, with some fantastic cocktails and many enjoyable evenings. The sunset cruise is something I would definitely recommend. Krishna playing the flute throughout the cruise was wonderful, while Shalabha kept us engaged with stories and information about Willingdon Island, the port, Fort Kochi and the places we passed along the way. A beautiful evening for the entire family. Taj Malabar has that rare combination of history, character and quiet luxury. The location, greenery, water, passing ships and beautiful weather made it very difficult to leave. In fact, we did not step outside the property for three nights and four days! We enjoyed ourselves so much that we extended our stay by another night. The spa experience was also excellent. My only small suggestion would be a larger and better-equipped gym for a property of this quality. But what really makes Taj Malabar special is its people. Elizabeth, Ankur, Paul, Shalabha, Cinderella, Swapna and her team, Chef Nihil, Chef Anoop, Soorya, Fatimah, Joman, Ajit, Alex, Babu, Krishna and many others made us feel genuinely looked after. Having spent a large part of my own professional life in hospitality and food service, I tend to notice the small things. Here it wasn't one big gesture that impressed me. It was the consistency, warmth and personal attention throughout our stay. A special thanks to Lalith Viswakumar and his entire team. We came for a family break after a very busy wedding. We left with some beautiful memories. We will definitely be back.

This was my first stay at a Taj hotel in India, and I do not think I would prefer to stay at a Taj hotel again after this sub par experience. I found the food to be very hit or miss. I liked their biryani. The breakfast buffet was only ok by Indian standards. Nothing spectacular. But they are ready to shut it down as quick as possible. The buffet ends at 10:30, but if things run out by 10 they’re not refilling it. As one of the most expensive hotels in town, it would be prudent to offer the breakfast service to its fullest capacity until your mentioned closing time. The dinner buffet for the price was also not worth it. We paid nearly $30 and it was ok. Mutton was overcooked, shahi tukda had an “old oil smell.” In the US, $30 can get you some of pretty great buffets so I was shocked by the lack of quality on this front. And unfortunately, after eating exclusively at this hotel for 2 days, my father and I has upset stomachs. My dad has been in India for 6 months and Ive been here for 3 weeks. To get my first uspst stomach in India at a 5 star hotel is disappointing to say the least. The service was also very hit or miss. Sometimes staff was quite pleasant. But I’d say the dining room is where we were hit a lot of hiccups. For breakfast, there’s a “table service” menu. And for some reason, the staff never came to our table unless we flagged them down. I’m certainly fine with filling my own water, but it feels weird when the white families get an overly enthusiastic welcome from the staff but my Indian origin father and I don’t even get dosa or chai orders taken unless we flagged someone down. This “profiling” of guests was consistent throughout our meals. If you’re white or look a certain way or have a big party, the service seemed very hands on from what I could see. But for us, we didn’t even get our water glasses filled (which of course I’m fine with doing but the contrast was stark). Aside from all this, many of the “cultural activities” were a bit awkward unfortunately. For example when some guests arrived on our final day, there was a “welcome dance.” And the dancers are beautiful and talented. But they literally end up playing music off of an iPad or something? Which ends up being a bit awkward and takes away from their performance. Having a speaker controlled by someone else may be helpful? But in general, many of these sort of things were awkward because of how the music is played off an iPad (e.g. this same thing happened during the classic dance performance). All the dancers are amazingly talented but they certainly need support so that guests don’t see the “puppet strings.” Maybe it isn’t the iPad that makes it weird but in general the vibe was off. The outside area also has tile which is incredibly slippery after rain. Considering many elderly people say at this hotel and kochi is a very rainy city, this is an incredible hazard. The room also is showing its age to an extent. The shower’s cleanliness felt questionable and the wood floor had scratches. Additionally, the resort is surrounded by industrial activity, which can be an eyesore despite the waterfront location.

I had a wonderful 4-night stay at Bharat Hotel (BTH), Kochi, and I would happily recommend it to anyone visiting the city with family. Bharat Hotel (BTH) is one of Kochi's most iconic heritage hotels. Established in 1964 by the late Shri B. Govinda Rao, it has been welcoming travellers for over 60 years and is well known for preserving authentic Kerala hospitality and pure vegetarian cuisine. The hotel has become a landmark on MG Road and continues its legacy with warm, traditional service. The rooms were very neat, clean, and spacious, and we were fortunate to have a beautiful garden-view room. Housekeeping and room service were exceptionally prompt throughout our stay. The hotel interiors are classic and reflect its heritage. While they are not ultra-modern, they have a charming old Kerala touch that gives the property a unique and homely feel. The breakfast was delicious, with fresh South Indian dishes and a few other options. Although the breakfast buffet has limited choices, the quality and taste are excellent. The food is also very reasonably priced. One thing I really appreciated is that this is a 100% pure vegetarian, family-friendly hotel. There is no bar, no non-vegetarian food, and the hotel maintains a peaceful, non-smoking environment, making it ideal for families, senior citizens, and vegetarian travellers. The location is another major highlight. The hotel is situated on MG Road, one of Kochi's best shopping and commercial areas, with plenty of shopping outlets, cafés, and restaurants within walking distance. The beautiful Ernakulam Shiva Temple, believed to be around 2000 years old history, is located just opposite the hotel. Marine Drive and the boat cruise terminal are within 2 km, making sightseeing very convenient. The hotel also offers: * A small children's play area. * Two lifts (one large and one small). * A pleasant and spacious lobby. * Wheelchair assistance for guests with mobility needs. Overall, Bharat Hotel (BTH) offers excellent value for money. If you're travelling to Kochi with family and looking for a centrally located, clean, heritage-style hotel with delicious pure vegetarian food and genuine Kerala hospitality, this is a perfect choice. Highly recommended! 🌿🙏

The moment we entered, there was a strong damp smell that made the room feel uncomfortable and unclean. To make matters worse, there was virtually no ventilation, so the smell lingered constantly. The Wi-Fi barely worked, basic toiletries were not provided, and overall housekeeping and maintenance fell far below expectations. The ambience felt neglected and unwelcoming, and I genuinely felt uncomfortable from the very first day. The location is good, but that's about the only positive. There are plenty of other homestays and hotels in the same area that offer a much better experience. We had originally planned to stay longer, but the condition of the room made us leave and move to another homestay. Looking back, I'm very glad we made that decision. I hope Niyati seriously works on its cleanliness, room maintenance, ventilation, hospitality, amenities, and overall guest experience. The property has potential, but in its current state, I would not recommend it.

Stayed at Niyati Boutique Hotel in Kochi in February 2026, and unfortunately the experience was very disappointing. The check-in process was extremely frustrating. The receptionist on duty spoke only Hindi and had difficulty communicating in English, which made the process confusing and unnecessarily slow. There was also a basic misunderstanding about documents. I provided my Indian passport for identification, but the receptionist insisted that I must show a visa. I had to explain multiple times that as an Indian citizen traveling within India, a visa is not required, but he continued insisting. Eventually, I had to provide another identification card just to complete the check-in, which was very frustrating. Another concern was the check-in procedure itself. The staff took photos of us using his personal phone, saying it was part of the check-in policy. This felt uncomfortable and unprofessional, especially without any explanation of how the photos would be used or stored. We were five people traveling together (four women and one male friend) and had three rooms booked under my name. However, the receptionist initially insisted that I only had one booking. After a long discussion, he eventually located the other bookings and showed us the rooms. However, he assigned the wrong room for the single-occupancy booking, which was meant for our male friend. Instead, he was given a lower-category room that had a bad smell and poor Wi-Fi. We only realized this mistake the next morning after he had already spent the night there and complained about the smell and connectivity issues. The next morning another staff member acknowledged the mistake and moved him to the correct room that we had actually paid for. We also contacted the hotel owner during the check-in issue, but unfortunately no action was taken to resolve the situation at the time. Because of this experience and the lack of response from management, the situation felt very uncomfortable for our group. As women travelers, we did not feel comfortable allowing staff to enter our rooms for housekeeping after this incident, so we avoided room service during our stay. The hotel advertises that staff speak English, Hindi, and Malayalam, but this was not our experience at reception. I am originally from Kerala and can speak all three languages, yet even basic procedures were not handled properly. The only positive aspect of Niyati Boutique Hotel is that it is conveniently located. However, it is also close to a bar, so the area can be loud and noisy at night. Overall, the service and organization were far below what one would expect from a boutique hotel. Apart from the location, I would not recommend staying at Niyati Boutique Hotel, especially if you expect professional service or a smooth check-in experience.

Housed within a restore heritage Dutch-style bungalow likely dating back to 1860s, with very limited rooms available for booking. My room is on the ground that facing the street, which you will find lots of tourists taking their photo outside my window. The room remain nostalgic as it is, even for the furnitures. But at least the toilet comes with bidet. The aircon was set at strong speed for a reason, as it needs sometime to cool down the room. You can remain the fan on to make the room airy. There’s a TV in the room but seems no longer functioning. Bug zapper and electric mosquito repellent also provided in the room to keep mosquitoes and bugs out from your room. One thing I find it very disappointing is the WiFi connection here. You couldn’t load anything on your device if you lay on the bed. The only area with strong connection is at the room entrance door. So I advise you to get your own mobile data. No shower gel provided in the shower room except for a bar soap. You may need to bring your own gel, including toothpaste and toothbrush. Your room is locked with key, which you need to pass to them if you need room cleaning.

The location alone gives Niati Hotel a special charm. We never leave bad reviews but this warrants it. The only positive aspects of our stay were the location and the room's initial presentation. On our second day, we came back to the room and it was filled with an overwhelming cigarette smell, and later that day we came back to an undeniable marijuana odour - it was so strong that our towels hung in the bathroom reeked of the stench. When we raised the issue, the manager was highly defensive, repeatedly denying the smell and attributing it to "200-year-old limestone walls and the rain." His response every time we raised our concerns was genuinely appalling. Not only did he repeatedly deny the problem, but when pressed for a solution, he twice (with no exaggeration) simply…walked away from our room mid-conversation and never returned, offering no apology, solution or form of accountability. Even after we essentially begged him to come into our room to confirm the smell and he conceded (with a laugh???) the room stunk of marijuana, he still provided absolutely no solution (like a room change) and walked off mid conversation AGAIN. The worst moment was his callous response to us expressing our concern about my partners asthma, to which he replied (again - this is no exaggeration) "well, there’s no where for you stay in Fort Kochi." Again, we are very used to subpar accomodation with our many budget travels around SE Asia - we can put up with a great deal when the hospitality is nice. But this was genuinely the worst customer experience we’ve ever received and we implore you to avoid booking here at all costs.

We enjoyed our time here so much that we returned for a second stay of several days—and once again, everything was perfect. We can wholeheartedly recommend Fragrant Nature Kochi and would be delighted to stay here again!

Yays 1. Staff: The staff at the hotel are the absolute highlight. Amazing people. Helpful and courteous. They even carried our 7 month old around so that we could have our breakfast in peace. 2. Great location: All places of interest are reachable working a ten minute car or auto rickshaw (tuk tuk) right. 3. Calm atmosphere. The greenery inside the building, the cover of colours, the decor and the general aesthetic is very calming and spot on. 4. Great views from the rooftop restaurant and swimming pool. 5. Food: Breakfast is a good mix of Indian and international cuisine and varied over the 3 days we were there. Live counters also available. The rooftop restaurant also offers very tasty food. Veg stew at breakfast and Chicken Varatharachathu at dinner were exceptionally tasty. Nays To be honest, nothing that I didn't like. There are a few missing "attention to detail" issues which in my view subtract from a real "Five star" hotel. Things that are easy fixes and will go a long way. 1. Both showering areas for the pools were under renovation at the same time which was in my view bad planning. As a result you couldn't shower before or after a swim. 2. More hooks/ towel racks needed in an otherwise very well appointed washroom. We were a family of 2 Adults and 2 kids. We struggled to dry our towels and swimming clothes. 3. Room door doesn't have a stopper. Bringing luggage, or a baby stroller in and out can become a little inconvenient. 4. Some lamp shades and the accent wall behind the headboard had stains. 5. "High tea" is essentially chai/coffee + 1snack and/or biscuits. This was actually the only thing I was actually disappointed with. 6. The recreation room needs ventilation and some gym equipment needs repair.

Hotel Seagull is right next to the property, and there are plenty of other cafés and restaurants within walking distance. The biggest highlight of this place is definitely the sea view. My experience at Old Harbour Hotel, Fort Kochi was genuinely beautiful and memorable. From the moment we entered the property, what stood out to me was the peaceful atmosphere and the old-world charm. Instead of feeling like a modern hotel, the whole place has a unique heritage character that makes you feel connected to the history and beauty of Fort Kochi. The property itself is one of the biggest highlights. The traditional architecture, antique-style interiors, greenery and beautifully maintained surroundings create a very calm and elegant atmosphere. Every corner has something interesting to look at, and the hotel has a very warm, homely feeling despite being a luxury property. I especially loved the garden and pool area. It is a lovely place to sit, relax and spend some quiet time away from the busy surroundings of Fort Kochi. The greenery gives the property a peaceful feel, and the entire setting is perfect for photographs and for simply enjoying the atmosphere. The rooms were comfortable, clean and beautifully maintained. I liked how the design stayed true to the heritage style rather than trying to make everything look overly modern. At the same time, the basic comforts expected from a good hotel were there, making the stay relaxing. Another thing I really appreciated was the staff and hospitality. The staff were welcoming, polite and attentive, which made the experience feel more personal. Good hospitality can completely change the feeling of a stay, and here I felt that the people were an important part of what made the hotel special. The food and dining experience was also enjoyable. The restaurant has a beautiful ambience, and having food in such a peaceful heritage setting makes the experience more than just a meal. The combination of the surroundings, presentation and hospitality added to the overall experience. The location is another major advantage. Being in the heart of Fort Kochi makes it convenient to explore the area's famous heritage streets, cafés, churches and the Chinese fishing nets. You can enjoy the character of Fort Kochi and then return to a much quieter and peaceful environment inside the hotel. Overall, what I liked most about Old Harbour Hotel was that it didn't feel like I was simply staying in a hotel. It felt like experiencing a small part of Kochi's history while enjoying the comfort of a beautiful boutique property. The heritage atmosphere, greenery, pool, peaceful surroundings, hospitality and excellent location all came together to make the experience special. If you are someone who prefers heritage, peaceful surroundings, beautiful architecture and a more unique stay rather than a typical modern hotel, Old Harbour Hotel is definitely a place worth experiencing. My overall rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 What I loved most: Heritage ambience • Architecture • Garden • Pool • Hospitality • Location • Peaceful atmosphere

I stayed at Victory Dawn by Amatrails for a friends reunion organized by my father's friend. Managed by Taj Hotels, the property and their service is impeccable (as is always)! The property opened in January 2023 and has 6 rooms between 2 floors connected by a vintage wooden staircase from inside the building. It can accommodate a group of 12 people. But to be honest, by the size of each room it can accommodate twice as many people! The attached bathrooms are huge and very functionally designed. Furniture in the bedrooms and living rooms on both floors are subtle, stylish and remind one of old ancestral homes that some of us were privileged to visit. My favourite feature of the Victory Dawn is its collection of pictures of Kochi dating from early 1900s framed by Krishnan Nair Studio which itself was established in 1910. We were served fresh, hot and extremely tasty food. As a person who usually steers clear of fruits or salads from outside home, I was really happy to have it fresh at the table. The starters and soups were very well prepared and no prizes for guessing how the main course turned out to be! Special thanks to the staff who were simply great at what they did. Food was served hygienically and their service was impeccable. While they were always available and amiable, their presence was never intrusive. In general the property scores a 10/10 for hygiene, quality of food and service. It would be a perfect fit for groups or families to enjoy a quick weekend getaway.

Our first stop in Kochi was Brunton Boatyard, and it was a wonderful decision. We arrived around 1.30 am after a long haul flight and they welcomed us with warmth and passion. They have prepared a birthday cake too, which was lovely. The entire hotel is designed for people to slow down and savour the sights - see the port come to life or sit down by the pool and listen to the boats. Breakfast was really outstanding - it's not your regular buffet service: there is a curated menu including local and Western breakfast items, with a pastry cart in the shape of a ship catering to your carb needs. Service at History Restaurant was 10/10. Make sure to order the first class railway mutton shank! I also went for an ayuverdic massage during my stay, and the attendants constantly check in whether you're comfortable with the massage pressure. Their service is well above and beyond. I highly recommend Brunton for your stay in Fort Kochi.

While every review rightly praises the colonial heritage and stunning architecture of Brunton Boatyard, what truly makes this property world-class is its extraordinary, personalized customer service. They do not just offer luxury; they actively care for their guests in ways you rarely see anymore. My husband is a stroke survivor, and though I had requested a first-floor room, the manager, Ms. Priya, thoughtfully placed us on the ground floor to ensure a lower bed height. When the accessible features in that room didn't quite suit our needs, the team immediately stepped up. They checked their availability, moved us to a second-floor room, and even brought in a lower guest bed to test for comfort—doing whatever it took until my husband was fully at ease. The food and beverage team was equally phenomenal. The breakfast staff was exceptionally attentive every morning, and I especially loved the Mattancherry section with local specialties that changed daily. It allowed me to sample a wide variety of Kerala and Kochi food, almost all of it entirely new to me! When I mentioned to the F&B Manager, Mr. Ashish, that a couple of dishes were not quite up to expectations, the entire culinary team made it their personal mission to check on us and get things right for the rest of our stay. Chef Rohit even custom-made a brilliant, light edamame, tomato, and cucumber salad for me—which was so good my husband ordered the exact same thing for dinner! During another meal at the History Restaurant, Chef Rohit personally came over to chat and shared a warm laugh with us about the fresh catch of the day. The standalone moments of thoughtfulness, however, were what truly set them apart. When we left the hotel for a one-night backwater cruise, I told Ms. Priya to throw away an opened bottle of red wine from our mini-bar. Instead, she insisted on keeping it in the fridge for us and had it waiting when we returned the next day. The birthday celebration at breakfast time and fresh flowers in the room that she organized with her team touched my heart. She even helped arrange my birthday dinner at The Rice Boat at Taj Malabar, informing the staff there so we were treated like royalty from the moment we walked in. Combined with the morning yoga taught by a senior teacher, the evening cruise, the guided history walk, and high tea—all of which were thoughtfully provided complimentary—it was an unforgettable stay. Brunton Boatyard is a gorgeous and comfortable property, but it is the warm, genuine, and deeply caring staff who truly make it special.

We stayed three nights in two rooms and we enjoyed every minute. The colonial style is exactly what we love — high ceilings, wooden shutters and lots of character, with comfortable, spacious rooms. Fort Kochi is a lovely town, easy to explore on foot, and the hotel is ideally placed for it. Highly recommended — we would happily return.

Brunton Boatyard CGH is a beautiful heritage property in Fort Kochi that offers much more than just a place to stay. The hotel beautifully reflects Kochi’s maritime and colonial history while maintaining the comfort expected from a premium property. The waterfront setting is one of its biggest highlights. The old-world architecture, wooden details and peaceful atmosphere give the property a distinctive character. Staying here feels like experiencing a small piece of Kochi’s history rather than staying in an ordinary modern hotel. 🌊🇮🇳 Its location is excellent for exploring Fort Kochi. The famous Chinese fishing nets, heritage streets, churches, cafés, galleries and waterfront areas are easily accessible, making walking around the neighbourhood a genuine pleasure. The hospitality and overall ambience complement the heritage setting nicely. Food lovers can also enjoy Indian and Kerala-inspired flavours, including local seafood and traditional beverages. What makes Brunton Boatyard particularly memorable is its sense of place. The property embraces Kochi’s past without feeling outdated, creating a comfortable blend of history, culture and modern hospitality. Overall, it is an excellent choice for travellers who appreciate heritage architecture, peaceful waterfront surroundings, Kerala culture and thoughtful hospitality. A memorable Kochi experience, especially for those visiting Fort Kochi for the first time. 🌴✨

With plenty of activities such as sunset cruises and morning yoga, I would love to visit again and spend more time there. If you're staying in Fort Kochi, this is a hotel you should definitely splurge on.

Warning! ❌ We rented two motorcycles from I-one in Kochi. The owner, Ivan, promised that everything was in perfect condition and that he would be available for any issue — in reality, that was far from the truth. Right at the beginning of our ride to Munnar, a serious clutch problem became obvious. We had already raised concerns during the test ride, but were told everything was new and fine. When we reached Munnar, local garages refused to work on bikes coming from him. After significant effort, one mechanic finally agreed to inspect it — and found the clutch plates completely worn out and in need of replacement. Ivan initially refused to take responsibility and only after repeated arguments agreed not to charge us for the repair. Later on, we were involved in an accident with a bus and had to be taken by ambulance to the hospital, leaving the motorcycles in a safe spot. Instead of offering basic assistance or helping arrange transportation for the bikes, Ivan demanded that we return to the accident site ourselves and find a truck to transport them — while we were dealing with medical treatment. Disrespectful attitude, zero accountability, and clear attempts to squeeze more money out of us — even at the expense of our health and safety. If you want a peaceful motorcycle trip, stay far away from this place.

⭐️⭐️ (2/5) Mr. Ivan and his son Leon, who run this place, came across as rude and adamant. It didn’t feel like a homestay at all, there was no warmth or welcoming vibe, made us stand for 5 minutes for check-in. I’ve reduced three stars for multiple reasons. First, the price charged was ₹3,000, which was far more than what was delivered. The room had red ants, the TV wasn’t working, the AC didn’t cool properly, the bathroom door handle was broken, and no water bottles were provided. After paying ₹3K, basic quality and maintenance are expected, which were clearly lacking. Second, the scooty rental experience was very poor. They rent out their own two-wheelers from the ground floor and charge ₹800–₹900 for scooters that were in bad condition—honestly not worth even ₹400. Since it was our last day and our train was at night, we requested a two-hour extension, but they refused to listen and only focused on charging more. The approach felt money-driven rather than experience-focused. Third, the overall attitude and way of speaking were disappointing. In the hospitality business, behavior matters, but here it felt like everything revolved around money. This was also the first place where we were asked to pay both rent and a security deposit, which felt unnecessary and showed a lack of trust toward guests. Overall, it was one of the worst stays during our Kerala trip. I would not recommend this homestay or their scooter rentals. If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to reach out—I’ll be happy to answer. My wife and I visited Fort Kochi for two days in the last week of December.

I had a very disappointing experience at London Courtyard, Kakkanad. I originally booked the room for two people. Later at night, my sister arrived, and before allowing her to stay, I clearly informed the hotel staff and asked whether there would be any extra charges or issues for three people staying in the room. The staff told me, “No bro, it’s okay,” and said no extra payment was needed. The next day, I even extended the room for one more day, and again nobody mentioned any problem or extra charges regarding three people staying. However, when we returned to the hotel at night, one of the staff members behaved in a very rude and disrespectful manner. He suddenly said that three people were not allowed and told us to vacate immediately. The way he spoke to us was very harsh and unprofessional. I had absolutely no problem paying extra charges if they had informed me properly from the beginning. The issue was not about money — it was about the rude behavior and lack of clear communication. My sister was with me at the time, and she felt very uncomfortable and upset because of the way the staff treated us. On top of that, the room cleanliness was very poor. Both the bedsheet and blanket were extremely dirty. It honestly felt like the blanket had not been washed for a very long time. Very disappointed with the management, staff behavior, and cleanliness. The issue was never about paying extra charges for a third person. I clearly told your staff that I was willing to pay any extra amount if needed. What disappointed me was the way your staff handled the situation. During the second day, we extended the room and throughout the day all the staff could clearly see there were three people with us. We were going in and out multiple times from the 3rd floor, and nobody mentioned any issue at that time. But when we returned at night, one staff member spoke in a very rude and unprofessional manner. Instead of politely explaining the hotel policy, he immediately said, “No bro, it’s not possible,” and even told us either the third person cannot stay or we should check out. A professional hotel staff should first explain the rules respectfully and mention the extra charges properly. I was calm and repeatedly said that I was ready to pay the additional amount, but the behavior and tone were unnecessary and disrespectful. Regarding the bedsheet issue, we only extended the room because my sister was alone at checkout time while I was busy, and she had many luggage bags to manage by herself. That was the only reason for the extension. Also, I still have the photos of the bedsheets and I can upload them if needed. I hope management focuses more on professional customer service and respectful communication in the future.
