We had a truly wonderful stay at Forte Kochi. The property has such a charming vintage, nostalgic character that immediately pulls you in, making it feel cozy rather than just another commercial hotel. Its location is spot-on—nestled right in the heart of Fort Kochi, which made exploring the local sights and walking to nearby spots completely effortless. A huge shoutout to the staff, whose warm hospitality and attentive service genuinely made a difference during our trip. On top of that, the breakfast spread was delicious every morning. We left thoroughly satisfied and wouldn’t hesitate to stay here again. Highly recommended if you’re visiting the area!

We were greeted with warmth, big smiles, kindness and helpfulness by all of the staff and that remained the way throughout our 5 night stay. Radeep was our main point of contact and he was full of charm. The hotel is filled with character and fine furnishings. We loved the cosy bedroom. The bed and bedding were so comfy and clean. The bathroom was excellent with a superb choice of Forest Essentials and there was plenty of hot water. And the breakfasts (oh my goodness) were so delicious with an incredible choice of styles and tastes. Masala chai, local fresh fruits, pazhamkanji, dosas, vada and idlis to name a few of our favourites. The pool and gardens were beautiful with the history of the building treated and reflected in some tasteful ways. We wouldn’t hesitate to recommend Forte Kochi.

A beautiful heritage-style hotel right in the heart of Fort Kochi, located along one of the area’s major streets. The property immediately catches your attention with its aesthetically pleasing colonial architecture, ochre-coloured walls, and charming heritage character. We visited as part of a weekend stay, and the overall ambience was one of the highlights. Although the property is relatively compact, it has been designed beautifully, with a calm and pleasant atmosphere that makes it a lovely place to unwind. The staff were extremely welcoming, friendly, and pleasing throughout our stay. They were also celebrating Onam during our visit, which added a festive touch to the experience. The rooms were spacious, comfortable, and beautifully decorated in keeping with the heritage theme. The pool located at the centre of the property was another lovely feature. There were plenty of picturesque corners around the hotel, and the well-maintained plants and greenery added beautifully to the overall setting. We also enjoyed the complimentary breakfast, which offered a good variety of options, including English breakfast favourites, North Indian dishes, and local Kerala specialties. The food was delicious, and everything was served well. The only major drawback was the limited parking space. Since the hotel is located in the middle of Fort Kochi, parking is mainly available along the street, with space for only around 2–3 vehicles at a time. This could be inconvenient, especially during busy hours. Overall, it was a wonderful weekend stay and felt absolutely worth the experience. If you enjoy heritage architecture, beautiful ambience, greenery, and warm hospitality, this is a lovely place to stay in Fort Kochi.

We stayed at Forte Kochi with our family and our 1-year-old, and honestly, we had a really nice time here. We had just planned a simple weekend trip to Kochi. We reached Kochi Railway Station and the hotel chauffeur came to pick us up, which was already a nice start to the trip. The moment we entered the property, we were welcomed with garlands and aarti in the traditional Kerala style. It was a small thing, but it instantly made us feel special and welcomed. We finished the check-in formalities and went to our room. And the property itself is beautiful. The architecture, the old well, the mikvah and all the little details around the property really make you feel like you are staying in a piece of Fort Kochi's history. We honestly ended up taking photos at almost every corner because there was always something interesting. The food was really good too. We tried quite a few Kerala dishes as well as some Western options, and everything we had was delicious. Since we were travelling with our 1-year-old, one thing we really appreciated was how helpful the staff were with the baby. They even helped us prepare and serve baby food, which might sound like a small thing, but when you're travelling with a little one, these things make a big difference. We also spent some time in the pool just relaxing, and one of my favourite parts was the early morning heritage walk. It was actually a great way to understand the history of the property and Fort Kochi. The location is also perfect if you want to explore Fort Kochi. It's right on Princess Street and most of the popular places are quite close by. Overall, we genuinely enjoyed our stay here. It felt comfortable, relaxed and very personal, and travelling with a baby was surprisingly easy because of how accommodating the team was. Would definitely recommend Forte Kochi if you're planning a weekend in Kochi, especially if you're travelling with family.

⭐ 1/5 – Extremely Disappointing Experience at Zostel Fort Kochi I had a very disappointing experience at Zostel Fort Kochi. I have stayed with Zostel before, including Zostel Varkala, and recently stayed at Zostel Kumbalangi as well. While every property has its own character, I had genuine expectations from the Zostel brand. Unfortunately, this stay was completely different. I had booked and paid for four nights from August 16 to August 20, but I had to leave on August 17, after staying for less than one full day, because I simply could not continue staying there. The biggest issue was poor hygiene and maintenance. The washrooms were in a very bad condition and had a strong unpleasant smell. The overall property felt old and poorly maintained, more like an old mansion with inadequate upkeep than the kind of hostel experience I expected from Zostel. I also noticed issues with pests, including cockroaches. The room and bed conditions were disappointing, and the overall environment was uncomfortable. There was also no proper hostel or traveller vibe. I understand that the atmosphere can vary based on location, but this was not just about the lack of a social vibe, the overall hygiene, cleanliness and maintenance were my major concerns. There was no convenient café or proper space where I could simply grab a coffee or snack. Some basic facilities also felt inconvenient, and my experience with the staff was not particularly helpful or cooperative. What disappointed me the most was that I had planned my trip around this stay and paid for four nights, but I was forced to leave almost immediately. After the stay, I also developed severe cold, cough and fever symptoms and had to seek medical treatment. I am not making a definitive medical claim about the cause, but the poor hygiene and unpleasant conditions significantly added to my discomfort. I genuinely feel that Zostel needs to seriously inspect and improve this property, especially the washrooms, hygiene, maintenance, pest control, room conditions and overall guest experience. I have had better experiences with Zostel before, which makes this even more disappointing. Based on this experience, Zostel Fort Kochi is not a property I would recommend in its current condition. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the property for future travelers.

A stay that felt like a little escape from the city 🌿✨ Our stay at Ramada Kochi was one of those experiences where you slowly realise that the hotel itself has become part of the holiday. The first thing that struck me was the location. Tucked away from the chaos of the city, the property sits beautifully by the backwaters, giving you a sense of calm the moment you enter. There’s something particularly relaxing about waking up, opening the curtains and seeing the water stretching out in front of you. The lake-view room made the stay even more special — spacious, comfortable and with a view that you could simply sit and stare at for a while. The room itself had that luxurious yet comfortable feel you expect from a good five-star property. Everything felt well maintained, and the overall ambience of the hotel was elegant without being overly formal. The service deserves a special mention. The staff were courteous, attentive and genuinely helpful throughout our stay. Nothing felt like an inconvenience, and that makes a huge difference when you’re travelling. And then came breakfast — absolutely excellent! There was a great variety, everything was fresh, and it was the kind of breakfast where you keep thinking, “Okay, one more thing and then I’m done…” only to discover something else worth trying. 😄 One of my favourite parts of the stay was the large warm-water swimming pool. There was something incredibly relaxing about getting into the warm water and spending time there without feeling rushed. After a day of travelling and exploring, it was the perfect way to unwind. What I particularly liked about Ramada Kochi is that you don’t necessarily feel the need to leave the property constantly. The peaceful waterfront setting, comfortable rooms, good food, attentive service and beautiful pool make the hotel itself a destination. If you’re looking for a luxurious and relaxing stay in Kochi, especially if you enjoy waterfront views and a quieter atmosphere away from the city’s hustle, Ramada Kochi is definitely worth considering. A beautiful property, a lovely view, excellent breakfast and genuinely relaxing stay — we thoroughly enjoyed our time here. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

text_light: Very disappointing experience. We visited as a family for lunch and to take a few casual photos. We had a small digital camera, and a staff member told us that photography was not allowed and that using the camera would be considered a “shoot” costing ₹7,000 per hour. We were only taking a few family pictures, not doing a professional shoot. What was more confusing was that other customers were taking photos and videos on their I phones without any issue. If cameras are not allowed or a ₹7,000/hour charge applies, this should be clearly mentioned on the website or at the entrance. Being told this only after we started taking photos felt disrespectful and ruined what was supposed to be a pleasant family outing. Also, being told that we were “randomly coming into a house and taking photos” was quite disrespectful, especially when we were a family visiting the place, not a group coming for a professional shoot. There is no clear photography policy mentioned on the website, while the café is promoted on Instagram as an aesthetic and Instagrammable place. This can easily create the wrong expectations for customers visiting the cafe.

hotel_name: Mãi House Heritage Hotel, Fort Kochi, Kerala, India
text_light: Our stay at Mai House was simply exceptional. Staying in a house with over 120 years of history, perfectly preserved and beautifully designed, makes for a truly unique experience. The interior garden is a genuine oasis of peace, ideal for strolling, reading, meditating, or simply enjoying the surroundings. It's also a perfect spot for taking spectacular photographs. The rooms are impeccably clean, with a lovely aroma, and meticulously cared for down to the last detail. They are equipped with all kinds of toiletries, ensuring that absolutely nothing is lacking. The food is delicious, prepared with great care, and the hotel's true added value lies in its staff: all the personnel treated us with exceptional kindness, warmth, and professionalism, making us feel right at home from the very first moment. Without a doubt, one of the best accommodations we have ever stayed in. Highly recommended.

I booked Kent Baywatch, Edakochi, for a two-night stay and checked in on 25 September. Unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing and far below what I would expect from a hotel charging these rates. It started with something as basic as requesting an iron box. Despite repeated requests, it was very difficult to get one. When it was finally provided, I was specifically told that I had to personally return it to reception immediately after use. For a hotel guest, even such a simple request became unnecessarily inconvenient. The situation became even more surprising when I returned from work in the evening and discovered that BOTH televisions — one in the bedroom and the other in the living room — had been removed from my room without any prior information or consent. When I enquired, I was told that they had been taken for maintenance. The televisions were eventually brought back, but the staff member who installed them then left with my room key card, causing the room’s power to automatically shut off. I had to go down to reception again to get the key card back. When I asked why my key card had been taken, the explanation given to me was that the concerned person was “a bit unstable minded.” I found this response extremely concerning and completely inappropriate for a hotel. However, the worst experience was breakfast. My booking was on a CP (Continental Plan) basis with complimentary breakfast. When I requested an omelette, I was told that it was “not available.” Shortly afterwards, I noticed other guests being served omelettes. When I questioned the waiter, I was then given a completely different explanation — that an omelette was not included in my CP breakfast and that I would have to pay extra for it. The complimentary breakfast itself had an extremely limited selection — essentially items such as appam/set dosa, two curries, one fruit and one juice. To tell a guest that an omelette is unavailable, while serving it to other guests, and then later say that it is actually available but chargeable separately is particularly disappointing. Overall, the experience reflected poor service, poor communication and a serious lack of attention to basic guest expectations. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this hotel. I do not believe the amount I paid for a room with breakfast represented reasonable value for money at all. For anyone considering staying here, I would strongly recommend looking at other options in Kochi before making a booking.

text_light: Even though it's an old property, it's still gold! Congratulations and thanks to the management. It had been 20 years since I last stayed here, and I was genuinely happy to see how well the hotel has been maintained. A few minor things aside, the experience was excellent overall. We landed in Kochi on an early morning flight — the trip was completely unplanned, everything happened in a rush, and in the chaos we forgot to book a room. To make it worse, it was just a day before Onam, so every hotel in the city was full. We took a cab and the driver took us to a random hotel he recommended, which turned out to be a terrible experience. (A word of caution: don't blindly trust cab drivers in Kochi with hotel recommendations.) Luckily, I remembered Abad Plaza, where I'd stayed two decades ago. I booked instantly through Booking.com, and from that point on, everything turned around. We arrived at 2:30 am, and the warmth of the front office and security team put us completely at ease. The entire team — front office, security, housekeeping, and restaurant staff — was wonderful. I've stayed at many hotels, but the hospitality here stood out as the best. The housekeeping and front office staff especially were always smiling, greeting us warmly, and eager to help. A small note for management: a few areas of the room flooring and some minor touch-ups could use attention — nothing major, but addressing them would take the experience from great to exceptional. That said, the linens, towels, bedding, toilet accessories, utensils, and furniture were all in great condition. Rooms and washrooms were spacious, clean, and well-kept. Breakfast was excellent. Thank you again to the management — even after all these years, this place is still gold. We'll definitely be back.

text_light: I have been a long time visitor at Abad. I'm talking years. I used to really like going there for the food. Anytime I had out of town guests, I used to take them for kerala food there. But I have noticed a serious decline in the quality and variety of dishes and yet the prices are either the same or more. The last time I visited was during the LPG shortage. I went to the restaurant upstairs to find that they had closed the kettuvellum restaurant and only had the other open for lunch. They claimed that because of the LPG shortage, they didn't have the "usual dishes". But what I saw was substandard food most of which required little to no cooking and we still had to pay 800 per person. When we went back down, we just popped into the downstairs cafe canopy. We asked what they had in their menu because of the LPG shortage and they told us the entire menu was available. So the passers by can get whatever they want but visitors for the buffet lunch get a tiny variety of random dishes for such a hunge price. We had seen the decline of Abad for a while but we thought it was because of new hotels and restaurants that they can't keep up with. But didn't know it was pure cheapness. Now a majority their cliental are the ones in the cafes and tour groups. The only thing going for the. At this point is the location. Mind you I have visited many cafes and restaurants during the LPG shortage and they all said their menu was unaffected. So Abad, if you are going to continue like this, you will end up like woodlands down the road

Hotel Kempton is a centrally located 4-star hotel on Marquis Street, close to Park Street and New Market. Its location is probably the property's biggest advantage, especially for visitors who want easy access to shopping, restaurants, public transport and some of Kolkata's major attractions. Park Street Metro is only a short walk away, making the hotel convenient for sightseeing. The hotel offers a comfortable and fairly traditional atmosphere rather than the sleek luxury feel of a newer five-star property. The rooms are generally spacious and clean, and recent guest feedback has praised the helpful staff, housekeeping and comfortable accommodation. The hotel has 44 rooms across several categories, including Double Deluxe, Executive, Premium, Imperial, Family Suite and Presidential rooms. Breakfast is another positive point. Recent verified guests have described the breakfast as varied and good, while the hotel also has a multi-cuisine restaurant and a 24-hour coffee shop. Food prices have been described by some guests as reasonable for a centrally located hotel. However, the hotel is not perfect. Some parts of the property are showing their age, and guest feedback has mentioned older bathroom fittings and the need for renovation in certain areas. Parking is also limited, which can be inconvenient for guests arriving by private car. The surrounding Marquis Street/Park Street area is extremely convenient but can be busy and somewhat crowded. Guests who prefer a quiet resort-style environment may not find the location ideal. The hotel is better suited to travellers who value central location and accessibility over large grounds or extensive recreational facilities. Overall, Hotel Kempton is a good practical choice for a centrally located Kolkata stay. Its strongest points are its excellent location, comfortable rooms, friendly service and convenient breakfast and dining options. The main weaknesses are the somewhat dated feel in places and limited parking. Pros: Excellent central location, close to Park Street and New Market, comfortable rooms, helpful staff, good breakfast, nearby metro and restaurants. Cons: Some older fittings, limited parking, busy surroundings and fewer luxury facilities than a modern five-star hotel. Overall rating: ⭐ 4.1/5

Golden Parkk Hotel is a well-located hotel in the Park Street area, and its location is probably its biggest advantage. Maidan Metro is just a short walk away, while Park Street, Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral and several restaurants and cafés are easily accessible. For someone visiting central Kolkata, the location is genuinely convenient. The hotel has a traditional business-hotel feel rather than the modern look of a newly built property. The rooms are generally spacious, comfortable and reasonably well equipped. Recent guests have appreciated the room size, cleanliness, air conditioning and helpful housekeeping. However, the condition can vary between rooms, and some areas could use better maintenance. The staff are one of the better parts of the experience. Front-desk and room-service staff are frequently described as polite and helpful, although service can sometimes be slower during busy periods. The overall experience feels professional but not particularly luxurious. Food is available in-house and recent guests have generally liked the taste. The surrounding Park Street area is an even bigger advantage because there are plenty of restaurants and cafés within walking distance. The only downside is that hotel dining can feel somewhat expensive compared with nearby options. One important negative point is night-time noise. There are nightlife facilities in the building, and several guests have reported hearing loud music, particularly on floors close to the club. Guests who stayed on lower floors have sometimes had a quieter experience. If you are a light sleeper, I would specifically request a room away from the nightclub. Walkability is excellent. Maidan Metro is only around a three-minute walk, Park Street is roughly 15 minutes away on foot, and Victoria Memorial is also reachable without a long journey. The hotel is therefore particularly convenient for travellers who want to explore central Kolkata without depending on taxis all the time. Overall, Golden Parkk is a good central Kolkata hotel with an excellent location, spacious rooms and friendly staff, but it is not completely flawless. Nightlife noise and some ageing facilities are the main things I would keep in mind before booking. Pros: Excellent location, spacious rooms, helpful staff, good connectivity, nearby restaurants and easy access to central Kolkata attractions. Cons: Possible nightclub noise, some ageing facilities, occasional maintenance issues and comparatively expensive in-house food. Overall impression: ⭐ 4.0/5

Booked a 2-night, 3-day stay (room only) from May 3rd to 5th, 2026, via Agoda. The price was just under 8,000 yen. * The door was closed from night until early morning, making it very difficult to find the entrance on a first visit. * Arrived near midnight, but the door was closed. I rang the bell above the door and was allowed in. I was grateful they allowed me to check in even in the middle of the night. * The door remained closed until around 8 AM. To go out, you need to wake up the employee (who sleeps at the front desk!) to unlock the door. It felt a little awkward. * The room quality is about average for India. As others have mentioned, there's a faint sewage smell throughout the building, which is a bit unpleasant. There's no elevator. * Located on College Street, the soundproofing is poor, and you'll be woken up by the noise from outside early in the morning. * There are sometimes stray dogs near the entrance and inside the building. When I woke up this morning, there was poop in front of my room. * The room had air conditioning, and it worked on the first night, but for some reason it stopped working from the second night onwards. When I asked the innkeeper (probably the owner), he replied rather sternly, "No AC Plan! Check your reservation!!" Indeed, the booking details didn't mention air conditioning. Luckily it wasn't the middle of summer. * The toilet and shower were in the same room. The shower had a water heater, and although the water pressure was weak, hot water did come out. * Wi-Fi was also usable, albeit weakly. * The chai from the chai shop in front of the inn was delicious. Also, the man at the pharmacy asked me, "Any problem?" * They held my luggage even after check-out. * The customer service from the man who seemed to be the owner was poor, leaving a bad impression. The location is decent. The cost-performance ratio isn't that great, so I probably won't stay again.

This is an overdue review, coming after a second stay at the hotel. Our first stay was nearly a year and a half ago, when we hosted a marriage ceremony and reception here, along with arranging rooms for family members attending the wedding. I wanted to share my experience of both occasions. 1. Food served at the marriage and reception There were well-curated menus for both events, featuring food from Poiisse’s own restaurant and Byepass Dhaba, which is owned by the same group. The spread was a mix of Indian and Mughlai cuisine, and the food was one of the highlights of the events. Even now, a year and a half later, our guests still talk about the food whenever we meet. 2. Banquet and service The hotel has two banquet floors, offering an exceptional city view overlooking the Bypass, ITC Royal Bengal and JW Marriott. The banquet hall was well air-conditioned, and the open terrace was also available, ensuring that guests were comfortable wherever they chose to be. The banquet staff were excellent and particularly attentive towards our elderly guests. Their service and willingness to assist made a big difference during the wedding. 3. Rooms and guest feedback We received excellent feedback from our family and friends who stayed at the hotel. They were particularly appreciative of the housekeeping and the service provided by the attendants. The rooms offered great views, comfortable beds and, in almost all cases, a mini-fridge, making their stay both comfortable and pleasant. Overall, it was a great experience back then, and it has been equally pleasant now that we have returned a year and a half later and booked a couple of rooms for our second stay. A special mention to Kaushik at the reception, who was exceptionally cooperative when we hosted the marriage here especially overlooking the banquet and the entire stay. He was equally helpful during our recent stay. Debasish from Housekeeping also deserves a special mention. He took particularly good care of my elderly mother and went out of his way to support us throughout our stay. His attention and kindness were truly unforgettable. I must mention Samiran and Sourav, our restaurant servers, they were polite, respectful and attentive throughout our meals, especially considering that we had my elderly mother with us. I would also like to mention Rupkotha at the reception, who was extremely helpful and supportive during the time we hosted the marriage here. Overall, the hotel has given us wonderful experiences on both occasions, and the personal attention from the staff is something we genuinely appreciate.

The Aster Heritage is a charming heritage-style guest house located on the fifth floor of the historic Stephen Court building on Park Street, one of Kolkata's most lively and convenient areas. The property combines the character of an old heritage building with modern room facilities, making it quite different from a standard chain hotel. The biggest advantage is undoubtedly the location. Park Street's restaurants, cafés, shopping areas and nightlife are right outside, while New Market, Victoria Memorial, Maidan, St. Xavier's College and several other attractions are easily accessible. Park Street Metro Station is also within walking distance. Tripadvisor gives the property a 100/100 walkability score, which reflects how convenient the surrounding area is for visitors. The rooms are another positive aspect. The property offers individually designed rooms with a mixture of vintage and modern elements. Current listings mention comfortable bedding, air conditioning, private bathrooms, Wi-Fi, television and work areas. Some rooms are around 200 sq. ft., while the heritage building provides attractive high ceilings and vintage character. Staff service is generally appreciated. Recent verified reviews have praised the helpful reception team and the property's friendly atmosphere. The hotel also provides cooked-to-order breakfast, housekeeping, laundry facilities and luggage storage. However, the property is not without weaknesses. It is important to remember that this is a guest house in an old heritage building rather than a modern luxury hotel. Some external reviews have reported maintenance problems, including wall cracks and water leakage. Booking-platform scores are also considerably more moderate than the Google rating, with some guests giving lower scores for cleanliness, amenities and property condition. The food offering is convenient, particularly the cooked-to-order breakfast and home-style meals available on request, but guests expecting a large hotel restaurant or extensive buffet may find the facilities limited. Overall, The Aster Heritage is best suited to travellers who value location, heritage character, spacious rooms and a homely atmosphere more than extensive luxury facilities. It can be an excellent base for exploring central Kolkata, but guests should keep realistic expectations about staying inside an older heritage property. Pros: Outstanding Park Street location, excellent walkability, heritage character, comfortable rooms, friendly staff, breakfast, Wi-Fi and pet-friendly policy. Cons: Older building, some reported maintenance issues, limited hotel-style facilities and mixed feedback about cleanliness/property condition. Overall rating: ⭐ 4.2/5

Location: Near Sealdah Station, Kolkata Type of Stay: Overnight / Emergency Stop If you are looking for a comfortable place to stay, look elsewhere. Booking a room at Hotel Icon International near Sealdah was rough, and what was supposed to be a simple overnight stop turned into a deeply frustrating experience. It is close to transit and gets somewhat cool if you just need a temporary crash pad, but that's where the benefits end. Do yourself a massive favor and skip this place unless you are in a desperate bind. There are plenty of cleaner, more honest budget accommodations elsewhere in the city if you have the time to look!

I expect an immediate resolution, including: A confirmed alternative accommodation of similar standard, or An immediate full refund and compensation for the inconvenience caused. text_light: Great hotel. The service is exceptional. Whether the food or manners, its exceptional. The food had been the best. Very fast room service. Book the deluxe rooms though. The normal ones are on ground floor and I doubt a pleasant stay due to the restaurant visitors making sound as stated by other reviewers. On 1st floor, we got room 16 initially. Whilst it was bigger in size, the bathroom had a bathtub that we had to get onto to take a shower. It was a hazard. They should just remove that. Then that room number will be the best. We asked for a room change and they shifted us to another room. While it had a better bathroom, the room size was smaller and fewer tables and chairs. Also, remove carpets. They smell a lot. We asked the staff to remove them from the rooms. There was no smell after that. The bathroom showers and handles have become old. Water doesn't come out properly sometimes. Need to fix that. They have 2 ceiling fans in the room above 2 beds near the feet. It feels so much better than just an AC. Though the ceiling fans in the new room no. 19 were a bit old and made weird sound on starting. Should change when possible. Old aesthetic. Not actually old. Its more pleasant that way. Despite stating these problems, I'm actually very satisfied overall. I'm listing these issues as a recommendation on what to fix. The staff actually remember you and your exact needs. They are attentive and speak very nicely. The rooms have an aesthetic that is hard to dislike. There is a ceiling fan in bathroom. Very comfortable. Definitely adding one to my own bathroom. It feels homely in here. The shower gel, shampoo and moisturizer were from biotique. Very nice to use. The beds were very comfortable. The pillows were even better than those in Taj Hotels. Had a very comfortable sleep. The neck support is excellent on the pillows. They don't have elevator as this is an old property. So if anyone with mobility issues to walk up to 1st floor needs to get ground floor rooms. I didn't look at the ground floor rooms myself so I cannot speak for that. Maybe ask the staff before you book for pictures of ground floor rooms. The 1st floor rooms are nice except for room 16 bathroom. They sometimes prepare breakfast on order when not many guests are present. In that case, they should inform the guests beforehand. If some guest was planning on a quick 5 minutes breakfast before going somewhere urgently, that'd have been an issue. Not the case for us. It was better for us as the food was prepared fresh within a few minutes and tasted much better than buffet system. The red idli chutney was especially good. The hash browns and aloo paratha tasted much better cooked fresh as well. Just listing communication of this change as a possible improvement. Guests want to know that beforehand if they have plans. One main issue, the hotel is old. Like 236 years old. And it shows. The stairs have become uneven at places. And the property look aged in some places. So I'm not sure about structural safety. Though, it is now managed by Oberoi after purchasing from previous owner. I trust they'll keep these issues in mind. Overall, we had a very satisfying and comfortable stay. The issues listed are to help both the future guests and hotel management.

hotel_name: The Elgin Fairlawn - Kolkata - Heritage Hotel (Since 1783)
text_light: One of the worst-behaving staffs I’ve ever dealt with. I booked The Elgin Fairlawn, Kolkata on 14th August for a pre-wedding photoshoot on 12th September. There were 13 email exchanges regarding the booking and photoshoot policies, so everything had been discussed well in advance. The main condition communicated to us was very clear: we had to pay a certain amount for one hour of photoshoot, and if we wanted to continue for another hour, we would pay the same amount again for the additional hour. Based on this understanding, I made the booking. When we arrived, the person I had made the booking with had left the property, so despite having the complete email trail and booking proof, we had to explain everything again. The number I had used for the booking was actually provided by the manager himself. It's not our look out that their employees are working or not I had payed and booked it in way advance. One of the major guidelines given to us was that we had to ensure that the hotel guests were not disturbed. We followed and moved to a completely empty area and even waited whenever guests walked by. After our one-hour slot ended, we were willing to pay for additional time and only asked for 10–15 minutes to finish up. Instead, we were spoken to extremely rudely, given absolutely no explanation and literally shouted at to pack up and leave. An employee was even sent to keep an eye on us while we packed. It's felt very humiliating. We were also informed that if we used additional electricity from the property for lights or other equipment, we would have to pay extra for the electricity. Again, completely fair. But nowhere in the guidelines communicated to us was it stated that lights could not be used at all. Refusing extra time is one thing. Treating paying customers like they’re a nuisance is completely different. After 13 emails, advance booking, payment and following all their guidelines, this was honestly one of the most humiliating and disappointing experiences I’ve had. The property may be beautiful, but the behaviour of the staff completely ruined the experience. Would definitely not recommend this place for photoshoots. Please do not ruin you special moments like they ruined ours.

hotel_name: The Elgin Fairlawn - Kolkata - Heritage Hotel (Since 1783)
text_light: I had a very different experience of The Elgin Fairlawn compared with the usual modern hotels in Kolkata. The biggest attraction here is not luxury or brand-new facilities, but the history and old-world character of the property. The building dates back to 1783, and you can genuinely feel that history when you walk through the hotel. The location is excellent if you want to explore central Kolkata. It is on Sudder Street, very close to the Indian Museum and New Market. Many restaurants, cafés, shops and street-food options are also nearby. Victoria Memorial, Maidan and Eden Gardens are easily accessible from here. Booking.com currently gives the location a very strong 9.3/10. The common areas are probably my favourite part of the property. There are old photographs, antique-style furniture, sitting areas and a beautiful garden/terrace that give the hotel a lot of personality. It doesn't feel like a standard chain hotel where everything looks the same. The heritage atmosphere is the main reason I would choose this place. The rooms are quite spacious and have period-style furnishings, but this is also where you need to keep realistic expectations. Some rooms look charming and full of character, while others can feel dark or slightly dated. Recent guests have mentioned that some furniture has seen better days and that certain bathrooms need improvement. There have also been occasional complaints about older facilities. The staff are one of the strongest positives. Recent verified reviews regularly describe them as courteous, attentive and helpful. Expedia currently gives staff and service 9.2/10. Food is another good part of the experience. The hotel serves breakfast and has a restaurant with both Indian and Western choices. The garden terrace is a particularly pleasant place to sit and eat. Recent guests have praised both the food and restaurant service. One minor drawback is that some guests would like more snack options between meals. One important point is that this is not a modern luxury hotel. If you are expecting polished contemporary interiors, a large swimming pool, extensive facilities or completely modern bathrooms, you may be disappointed. But if you appreciate history, heritage architecture, old photographs, antique décor and a unique Kolkata atmosphere, the imperfections are actually part of the experience. Overall, I would recommend The Elgin Fairlawn more for its heritage, atmosphere, location and character than for modern hotel facilities. It feels like staying in a piece of old Kolkata rather than simply booking another hotel room. Pros: Incredible history, excellent location, beautiful common areas, spacious rooms, friendly staff, good food and strong heritage atmosphere. Cons: Some rooms and bathrooms look dated, certain facilities need renovation, rooms can be dark, and it doesn't offer the facilities of a modern luxury hotel. Overall: ⭐ 4.3/5

hotel_name: The Elgin Fairlawn - Kolkata - Heritage Hotel (Since 1783)
text_light: We stayed at this property for four nights as a couple, paying around €70 a night, which is a considerable price for India. The hotel is charming, having hosted great intellectuals and prominent figures (Tiziano Terzani being one example); it's not only a quiet and welcoming refuge from the madness of Calcutta, but also a pleasant place, with an old-world elegance. We were initially given a "standard" room on the ground floor: unfortunately, these are old rooms, with a strong smell of mold and damp, and adjacent to the restaurant's interior. We complained, and fortunately there was a room available on the first floor, and we were moved at no extra charge. The room was recently renovated, very spacious and airy, with a TV, AC, and ceiling fans; it was beautiful, elegant, and very clean. Daily room cleaning is not automatic; you must specifically request it at reception in the morning. The reception staff seemed very friendly and eager to help in any way they could. The breakfast was plentiful and good. We dined at the hotel restaurant two nights in a row: the food was good, but the service depended heavily on the waiter; some were very helpful and kind, while others struggled to understand English and sometimes made mistakes. On a negative note: one evening we saw a mouse in the garden with the dining tables; sure, this is perhaps inevitable given the city's extremely low standards of cleanliness, but it was still very unpleasant.

Hotel Gallery 67 is a boutique-style hotel in the New Town area of Kolkata, offering a comfortable stay with a relatively modern and intimate atmosphere. It can be a practical choice for business travellers, couples and visitors who want to stay around the New Town/Rajarhat side of the city. One of the property's positive points is its location. Guests can access New Town's offices, restaurants, shopping centres and attractions without having to travel into central Kolkata. Eco Park, Biswa Bangla Gate and other New Town attractions are also reasonably accessible by taxi. The hotel has a contemporary appearance, and the smaller size gives it a more personal feel than a large chain hotel. Rooms generally provide the basic facilities needed for a comfortable short stay, including air conditioning, television, Wi-Fi and attached bathrooms. The property is more focused on practicality than luxury. Staff service is another positive aspect, with guests generally finding the staff helpful and courteous. The hotel can work well for short business trips or leisure stays when location and reasonable comfort are more important than extensive facilities. There are also some limitations. Hotel Gallery 67 does not have the scale or range of facilities expected from a major five-star property. Guests looking for a large swimming pool, extensive recreation facilities or several high-end restaurants may find the options limited. Room size and maintenance can also vary depending on the category and individual experience. The surrounding New Town area is modern but somewhat spread out. Although several attractions and commercial areas are nearby, walking between them is not always convenient, so taxis or app-based transport are useful. Overall, Hotel Gallery 67 is a practical boutique hotel for visitors staying around New Town. Its main strengths are location, comfortable accommodation, helpful service and a quieter atmosphere. Its main weaknesses are limited luxury facilities and less convenient walkability compared with hotels located in central Kolkata. Pros: Convenient New Town location, modern atmosphere, comfortable rooms, helpful staff and suitable for short stays. Cons: Limited luxury facilities, not ideal for walking-based sightseeing, and the overall experience is less extensive than a large five-star hotel. Overall rating: ⭐ 4.1/5

Overall, the hotel provides a clean and decent room, making it suitable for solo travelers and couples. The location is a major advantage, especially for those visiting the VFS Global Visa Application Centre, as it is conveniently situated just 50–100 meters away from The Inn Hotel. However, the pricing does not seem justified. The hotel charges ₹2,500 for a one-day stay (12 PM to 11 AM), which is quite expensive considering the limited amenities provided. The complimentary items include only one water bottle, a low-value shampoo sachet, soap, tissue, and basic tea and coffee supplies , amounting to minimal value for the price paid. Additional water bottles are charged at ₹28, even though they cost significantly less in the local market. Payment practices were also concerning. Guests are encouraged to pay in cash to avoid additional charges, but no bill or receipt is provided in such cases. If payment is made via UPI or card, extra charges apply, although a bill is issued at checkout. This practice gives the impression of avoiding proper tax compliance. In my case, I stayed for only 11 hours, yet I was charged the full day rate of ₹2,500, with no consideration for a short stay or any discount. To conclude, while the hotel offers a comfortable stay and courteous staff, the pricing is excessively high for the services and facilities provided. I would sincerely request the management to reconsider their pricing strategy and avoid taking advantage of guests who choose the hotel primarily due to urgent or unavoidable requirements.

He said there are no rooms at the Inn, but they have a 'very nice' hotel 2km away and he could put us up there. This was their scam ran smoothly for years. People book rooms at the Inn solely for their location and when they reach there, they are informed the hotel is full and offered a hotel 2 km away. Be very very careful when you deal with this guys. They have zero credibility and they not only have no qualms, but actually want people to come expecting a room when they are full. We eventually booked a room at Vivanta, which was 10 minutes walk away and offered a very good stay. I almost called the police on the Inn. To begin with, I want to apologise for such a late review. @ The owners, Please accept my sincere apology for being late. I have been talking about it to all those who want to visit Kolkata. Last year we were there when Kolkata faced cloud burst and we were stuck there as the whole area was submerged in waist deep water. Neither could we go out for work or lunch, nor we could order anything as no one could come there. So we had nothing after our breakfast. When the owners came to know about it in the evening, they brought snacks for us. enough for two meals. They kept it in the common area for anyone who wanted to eat. Although the place doesn't serve meals, the staff was asked to prepare dinner for all those who were staying there and we were not supposed to pay for it. This wonderful gesture will NEVER be forgotten. Thank you so much. 2 days later we had a late evening flight back home, but we were too scared to venture out. The owners told us to vacate the room as it was already booked for the day and move to common area which had an AC, a clean bathroom and allowed us to use their kitchen too. We got our food from outside but used their crockery to eat it. Made our evening tea in the kitchen. And when it was time to leave, the staff helped us with the luggage as we both are senior citizens. Mind you, the arrangements over there are so good that you don't miss the staff when they leave around noon time. But they came back in the evening only to help us with our luggage. We really felt that we were leaving one home to reach another home. Thank you once again.

Sapphire Suites is a centrally located 4-star hotel on Lindsay Street, close to New Market and the busy Dharmatala area. Its biggest advantage is the location, making it convenient for travellers who want easy access to shopping, restaurants, public transport and several central Kolkata attractions. The hotel offers a practical stay with spacious rooms, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, a restaurant, room service, breakfast and a fitness centre. Some rooms also feature separate sitting areas and kitchenettes, which can be useful for longer stays. Guest feedback generally appreciates the convenient location, friendly staff and reasonable room comfort. The surrounding area is lively and full of activity, with New Market, Sudder Street, Indian Museum and Park Street all within reasonable walking distance. This makes Sapphire Suites particularly useful for tourists who want to explore Kolkata without depending on taxis for every trip. However, the experience is somewhat mixed. Recent guest reviews have mentioned dated rooms, unpleasant odours and inconsistencies in room allocation or maintenance. The hotel's facilities also do not feel as modern or polished as those of newer four- or five-star properties. The property is therefore better suited to travellers who prioritise location and convenience over luxury. It can be a practical choice for short stays, sightseeing and business trips in central Kolkata, but guests expecting a premium four-star experience may find the property somewhat dated. Pros: Excellent central location, close to New Market, spacious rooms, breakfast, restaurant, helpful staff and good access to public transport. Cons: Some rooms and fittings feel dated, occasional cleanliness/maintenance complaints, busy surroundings and facilities that are less impressive than modern luxury hotels. Overall, Sapphire Suites is a convenient central Kolkata hotel with good location and reasonable comfort, but the property could benefit from renovation and more consistent maintenance. Overall rating: ⭐ 3.9/5

We absolutely loved our stay at Abode Hotel Mumbai. The hotel has a gorgeous Art Deco-inspired style, with beautiful communal areas full of books, artwork, vintage furniture and little touches that give the whole place a warm, relaxed atmosphere. There are also workspaces, an art space and yoga classes, so it feels like much more than simply somewhere to sleep. One of the things we really liked is that there are rooms to suit different budgets. You can opt for one of the larger, more spacious rooms with more facilities, or choose a smaller, more affordable room with shared toilet facilities. Whichever you choose, we found the hotel clean and well maintained. Breakfast is another lovely touch, with a traditional breakfast that gives you a taste of India rather than the usual uninspiring hotel offering. The communal spaces are fantastic - comfortable, quirky and perfect for sitting with a book, having a coffee, catching up on some work or simply relaxing after a busy day exploring Mumbai. Most importantly, the staff are attentive, welcoming and always on hand to help, which really adds to the experience. For us, Abode manages to combine location, affordability, style and character brilliantly. Whether you want a little more luxury or you're travelling on a tighter budget, there's an option here. Clean, quirky, welcoming and full of character - don't overlook this little Mumbai gem! Would we stay again? Absolutely!

I had a fantastic stay experience at Abode Bombay. The hotel is beautifully preserved within a stunning heritage building, and the interiors are exceptionally well-curated, blending vintage charm with modern local details. While the rooms are on the smaller side, they are incredibly cozy, clean and comfortable. Because the hotel sits right in the middle of a bustling market and heavy tourist spot, it can get a bit noisy at times, but the central location makes exploring the neighborhood on foot incredibly safe and convenient. We were just steps away from iconic landmarks like the Gateway of India and the endless street shopping along Colaba Causeway. The on-site cafe offers great basics, but not full, proper meals; luckily, the location is such that there are plenty of incredible dining options right outside your door, including legendary but overhyped spots like Leopold and Cafe Mondegar. What truly made our visit unforgettable, however, was the amazing staff. We were traveling with friends who had a toddler, and the hotel team was incredibly helpful and completely hands-on with helping out with the baby, making the stay stress-free for everyone. Their warm hospitality, unique character, and perfect location make this a highly recommended stay in Mumbai!

My recent four-night stay at The Abode in Mumbai was exceptional from start to finish. The hotel's location is unbeatable, right in the heart of South Mumbai, with iconic landmarks such as the Taj Mahal Palace, Colaba Causeway, Leopold Café, and many other attractions just a short walk away. What truly made the stay memorable was the warmth and professionalism of the team. Every member of staff was genuinely courteous and attentive. A special mention goes to Nilesh and Ganesh, who were outstanding hosts and ensured every aspect of our stay was seamless. The rooms are beautifully designed, ultra-modern while retaining a nostalgic charm that reflects old Mumbai. The thoughtful artwork throughout the guest rooms and public spaces adds character and creates a wonderful sense of place. The breakfast deserves special recognition. While the selection is intentionally curated rather than extensive, every item is of exceptional quality. From the freshest seasonal fruit and outstanding sourdough bread to the homemade organic jams and freshly prepared juices, every bite was a delight. It ranks among the finest breakfasts I have experienced. The breakfast team was knowledgeable, friendly, and took the time to explain the locally inspired dishes, making the experience even more enjoyable. The Abode perfectly blends relaxed luxury with authentic Mumbai character. If you're looking for a stylish boutique hotel with outstanding hospitality, incredible food, and an unbeatable location, I couldn't recommend it more highly.

They checked me in, took my payment, and then took me two or three streets away to another building. text_light: Worst stay I've ever had - absolutely not worth the price. This experience was extremely disappointing, especially considering that the property is located in Colaba, right behind the Taj Hotel. For a location like this, we definitely did not expect such poor hygiene, maintenance and basic facilities. We paid around ₹3,600+ for the room, but the stay was nowhere close to being worth the price. One thing I would suggest to future guests is to check which room category the reviews are actually referring to. Some of the higher-rated reviews appear to be from guests who stayed in the ₹3,600 room category with an attached bathroom, whereas guests staying in the smaller room with common bathroom facilities can have a very different experience. Major issues: 1. No separate bathroom for hotel rooms- There are no attached or separate bathrooms for the rooms. Guests have to use common washrooms, which were poorly maintained and offered very little privacy. 2. Stinky and poorly maintained washrooms- The common bathrooms had a strong unpleasant smell and were clearly not maintained to an acceptable standard. 3. Water leakage- There was even a "Save Water" board in the washroom, yet water was leaking from the ceiling whenever we opened the door. This was both ironic and unacceptable. 4. Unclean bedding - The blankets and bedspreads had a bad smell and did not feel freshly cleaned or hygienic. 5. Unhygienic staircase - The staircase was dirty and poorly maintained, adding to the overall unhygienic environment. 6. Extremely uncomfortable surroundings- The lower area of the hotel was being used by intoxicated people for drinking and sleeping. Their behaviour was extremely unpleasant and made us feel uncomfortable during our stay. 7. Very cramped room - The room was highly congested for the price we paid, with very limited space. 8.Unsealed/used water bottle provided - We were given a water bottle that was already opened and not properly sealed. The water also appeared to have a chlorine-like smell/taste and did not seem to be properly filtered. For drinking water provided to guests, this was extremely concerning. 9. Insects in the room - We also noticed insects inside the room, which further added to the hygiene concerns. 10. Misleading parking information - During booking, the property mentioned that parking was free and parking space was available. However, there is no separate parking space provided by the hotel. Guests have to park on the roadside at their own risk. What was even more disappointing was that we were charged ₹100 for 12 hours for a bike for parking, despite the booking information stating that parking was free. Overall, this was a very disappointing experience. Being in Colaba and located right behind the Taj Hotel, we expected at least basic cleanliness, hygiene, privacy and proper facilities. Unfortunately, none of these expectations were met. ₹3,600+ is definitely not justified for this kind of accommodation and experience. The property needs significant improvement in cleanliness, maintenance, hygiene, bathroom facilities and overall guest management. Based on our experience, I would not recommend staying here. A room requirement should not require this much unnecessary back and forth.The purpose of having a Sales team is to make the process easier for clients, not create additional hurdles. A simple enquiry that could have been addressed over a phone call has instead turned into an unnecessarily complicated email exercise, followed by complete lack of communication. Honestly, the entire experience has been extremely disappointing and has completely put me off considering this hotel for any future event or group booking. I would not recommend this hotel for event or group bookings based on my experience with the Sales team.If this is how a potential client is treated even before making a booking, it does not inspire any confidence in proceeding further. text_light: This hotel is nice and in a great location in South Mumbai. Located close to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus and several markets to the north, and the Gateway of India a short walk to the south, it's in a nice, semi-walkable area (assuming you're willing to brave crossing the streets) with several great spots to explore. We enjoyed our stay at the hotel immensely. The staff were polite and friendly, and the in-hotel restaurant serves great food. I particularly liked the egg curry and the chicken kolhapuri, which were exceptional. Close by, there is a National Hindu restaurant. While it doesn't look like much, the food was delicious, and it's a place local workers tend to gather for a quick lunch/dinner. The room we were in was a family room with two large beds. The room was a little worn due to the age of the building, but in our opinion, it just adds to the rustic charm of the hotel. However, it might be a turn-off for some; for us, it was not a problem. The rooms are well air-conditioned, as is the lobby/restaurant. Overall, we are extremely happy with our stay, and we are considering a repeat visit to Mumbai soon. This hotel is high on our list of places to stay.

Amma's Palace - An All-in-One Destination for Celebrations and Comfort Dining ​Intro: Amma's Palace is a refreshing discovery that effortlessly bridges the gap between grand celebration spaces and a high-energy dining hotspot. From a massive banquet setup and cozy stay options to a dedicated lounge vibe, it functions as a complete, versatile entertainment hub suitable for everything from quiet family dinners to large-scale events. ​Food: The culinary spread here was genuinely impressive across cuisines. The appetizers set the bar high, particularly the crisp Masala Papad and the juicy, spicy Chicken Lollipops. The standout starter, however, was the Kasundi Fish Tikka - melt-in-the-mouth flaky fish elevated by a sharp, zesty Bengali mustard punch. For mains, the pairing of decadent Cheese Garlic Naan with a velvety, rich Butter Chicken hit all the right comfort notes. But the undisputed showstopper was the authentic coastal Kori Rotti, where crisp rottis soaked in a deeply aromatic, spiced gravy delivered pure bliss. We capped off the meal with warm, ghee-rich Moong Dal Halwa and a platter of creamy, multi-flavored kulfis, which rounded off the feast perfectly. ​Ambience: The atmosphere shifts seamlessly depending on what you're there for. The dining area offers comfortable, spacious booth seating with a relaxed vibe, while the party zone amps up the energy with an electrifying dance floor, DJ setup, and a well-stocked bar. The property is expansive, well-maintained, and thoughtfully planned, catering equally well to relaxed diners and party-goers. ​Service: The hospitality throughout our visit was commendable. The staff was polite, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu recommendations. Dishes arrived fresh, piping hot, and at a well-paced cadence without long waiting intervals between courses. ​Value for Money: Considering the generous portion sizes, rich flavors, quality ingredients, and the sheer scale of the amenities provided, Amma's Palace offers great value for money. Whether you are dropping by for their signature coastal specialties or planning a full-scale banquet celebration, it delivers an experience well worth the spend. ​Ratings: • Food: 5/5 • Ambience: 4.5/5 • Service: 4.5/5 • Value for Money: 4.5/5 • Overall Experience: 5/5

Hotel Causeway was a solid and reliable stay for us, especially given the circumstances of our arrival. We arrived around 6am in the morning due to a change in our sleep and had contacted the hotel in advance via Booking.com to let them know. They advised that if a room was available on arrival, they would try to accommodate us. Luckily for us, a larger room was available, and we were allowed to check in straight away, which we really appreciated after a long night. We had initially planned to move rooms the following morning, but in the end, we weren't asked to move and were allowed to stay in the larger room for the duration of our stay, which was a nice bonus. From the outside, the hotel looks a bit rough and doesn't give the best first impression, but inside it's clean, practical, and perfectly sufficient for what you need. The staff were attentive and helpful, and housekeeping came in daily to make up the room, which kept everything fresh and comfortable. This is very much a no-frills, back-to-basics kind of hotel - if you're looking for luxury, this isn't the place for you. However, if you want somewhere clean, efficient, well-located, and good value, it does exactly what it needs to do. Overall, Hotel Causeway suited us perfectly and we'd happily stay here again. ⭐ Very Disappointing Experience - I Would Not Recommend This Hotel I have stayed at this hotel several times, but unfortunately, my experience has been consistently disappointing, and this latest stay was the final straw. Every time I make a booking, I clearly mention my arrival time, request for a clean room, and that a KING-SIZE BED IS MANDATORY, as I am travelling alone. Despite repeatedly making these requests, the hotel staff continues to ignore them. During my latest stay: ❌ I specifically requested a clean room, but the room provided was not properly clean. ❌ I clearly requested a king-size bed, yet the check-in staff gave me a triple room with three separate beds, even though I was travelling alone. This is completely unnecessary and does not match my booking request. ❌ I specifically paid extra for a street-view room and mentioned that I wanted a room facing the Starbucks side. Instead, I was given one of the worst street-view rooms, where I could barely even access the window to enjoy the view I had paid extra for. When I contacted reception and politely requested a better room, the response was essentially that if I wanted better service, I should book directly with the hotel instead of booking online. This attitude is extremely disappointing. A guest should receive the service they booked and paid for regardless of whether the reservation was made directly or through an online booking platform. I genuinely hope the hotel management reviews this situation and looks into the behaviour and attitude of the front-desk staff. Hotel employees should be focused on welcoming guests, respecting their reasonable requests, and providing a comfortable stay, rather than making guests feel that their online bookings are less important. I have given this hotel several chances because I have stayed here multiple times, but unfortunately, the repeated issues have completely changed my opinion. After this experience, I will not recommend this hotel to anyone, and I do not plan to stay here again. Hotel management should seriously consider improving the room allocation process, housekeeping standards, and customer service at reception.

Unfortunately, due to a genuine oversight, we did not have a physical ID at the time but assured the staff that we would provide the required identification first thing the next morning. Despite our repeated requests and explaining our situation - including the presence of a small child - Mr. Shahid (or Mr. Shajid) at the reception refused to allow us to check in or even let the child enter the room to rest or order food. We found this approach to be extremely insensitive and unaccommodating, especially considering the late hour and the fact that we were traveling with a baby. While we understand the importance of ID verification as per hotel policy, a more empathetic and solution-oriented approach, especially in situations involving infants and late-night arrivals, would have been appreciated. By far the worst hotel experience I have ever had, for several reasons. First and foremost, the person who cleaned my room stole my gold bracelet. I went through several procedures with the hotel and its management to obtain the relevant CCTV footage, and I was eventually provided with video evidence showing the staff member taking my bracelet from my room. This was an extremely distressing experience, particularly because the bracelet had significant sentimental value to me. Having a personal belonging stolen from your hotel room by a member of the cleaning staff is simply unacceptable. Unfortunately, the problems did not stop there. The hotel was extremely dirty. On several occasions, my bed linen and pillowcases were replaced with visibly stained ones, including brown stains. This is absolutely not what I would expect from a hotel, regardless of its price point. The hotel also turns off the air conditioning in the rooms whenever guests leave for the day. I understand the intention of saving electricity and reducing unnecessary energy consumption. However, the design of the hotel means that most of the property is essentially open-air, with corridors that are more like outdoor terraces with railings rather than enclosed hallways. As a result, the entire hotel becomes extremely hot and humid. Coming back to the room after being out all day and having to wait for it to cool down again is very uncomfortable. DISGUSTING !!. The choice of room also matters enormously. Some of the smallest rooms are genuinely awful, with two tiny beds and essentially no window. I strongly recommend checking exactly which room you are booking before staying here. I have travelled to around 20 countries and stayed in countless hotels, including in countries with considerably fewer resources than India, and I have nevertheless had far better experiences. Even if you are travelling on a tight budget, I would strongly recommend looking at other options. There are plenty of affordable hotels where you can have a much better experience. For me, however, the theft of my bracelet is what makes this experience particularly unacceptable. It was not simply a hotel stay that fell below expectations.

Extremely disappointing and disrespectful experience at Hotel Imperial, Mumbai. We had called the hotel in advance and clearly explained that we were a family group visiting Mumbai for Lalbaug Ganpati darshan and only needed a room for around 3 hours to freshen up. We were initially told that one room could be provided. However, after reaching the hotel, the manager checked our Aadhaar cards and noticed that our surnames were different. He then suddenly refused to give us one room and insisted that we take two rooms instead. His reasoning was that although we were cousins, we could not be considered "family" because our surnames were different. He even said that we might be siblings, but cousins were apparently not considered family. When we explained that we are cousins and obviously part of the same family, instead of handling the situation professionally, the manager started speaking to us very rudely. When we asked to speak to the owner regarding this issue, he simply said that the owner was not there. If the hotel had any such policy or restriction regarding different surnames or cousins sharing a room, they should have clearly informed us when we called beforehand. Firstly, we had booked a Deluxe Room, but upon arrival we were informed that it was not available. The biggest issue was the hotel's complete lack of responsibility for guests' belongings. We had requested the reception to keep a Myntra return parcel so it could be handed over to the delivery executive. The parcel went missing while it was in the hotel's care. Despite repeatedly asking the staff, no one took responsibility or provided a satisfactory explanation. To make matters worse, while changing rooms, I accidentally left behind my brand-new night suit in the previous room. When I went back to collect it, I was simply told that nothing had been found. It was also missing. Losing two personal belongings during a single stay is completely unacceptable and raises serious concerns about the hotel's housekeeping and security standards. The housekeeping service was equally disappointing. Even though we stayed for three days, the towels were not replaced daily, toiletries were not replenished, and the room was not cleaned to the standard one would expect from a professional hotel. Instead of showing concern or trying to resolve the issues, they were careless and unhelpful throughout. As guests, we expected accountability, but we were met with excuses and a lack of professionalism. Overall, this stay caused unnecessary stress and frustration. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone who values good customer service, cleanliness, or the safety of their belongings. Please think twice before booking, and be extremely careful with your personal items if you choose to stay here.

Subject: Formal Complaint Regarding Extremely Poor Stay Experience (26/06/2026 - 30/06/2026) Dear Management, As I checked in on 26/06/2026 at around 11:00 hrs, I checked into Room No. 205 and checked out on 30/06/2026 at 09:00 hrs. It was only when I informed him that my friends had already been occupying two rooms for over 13 days and would likely continue staying for another 2-3 months that he seemed to realise the significance of the matter. This entire experience reflects a serious lack of management control, accountability, guest care, and operational efficiency. Such standards are unacceptable for any professionally managed hotel. The hotel hallways were also poorly maintained, with leftover food from other rooms left unattended for long periods, showing complete negligence from the staff. The staff themselves were intimidating and aggressive, behaving more like goons than hospitality personnel. We didn’t feel safe raising complaints at the front desk, fearing possible manhandling. 4-Star Claim, 1-Star Experience — Absolutely Not Worth ₹13,291 a Night. I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights and paid ₹13,291 per night for the room alone—a price that is comparable to, and sometimes even higher than, established Marriott-branded hotels. After this experience, I can say one thing with complete confidence: I genuinely regret choosing this hotel. For a property calling itself a 4-star hotel and charging ₹13,291 per night, the service standards are shockingly poor. In fact, based purely on the level of service and facilities I experienced, I would not consider this experience worth even ₹3,000 per night. Here are some of the unacceptable experiences:. 1. Even basic amenities are missing. No comb. No hand towels. These are basic hotel necessities, not luxury requests. How can a hotel charging ₹13,000+ per night fail to provide such fundamental amenities?. 2. Completely dysfunctional communication and service. The intercom was not working properly. I called more than 20 times over approximately 3 hours simply to place a dinner order. Despite repeated attempts, nothing happened. Eventually, I had to physically walk down to reception to escalate the matter. Think about that: a guest paying ₹13,291 a night has to leave the room and walk to reception just to get someone to take a dinner order. That is not hospitality—it is a complete service failure. 3. Pathetic buffet breakfast service. The breakfast experience was extremely disappointing and nowhere close to what one expects from a property positioning itself as 4-star. The service standards were simply unacceptable. 4. Customer service at its worst. The overall customer service was one of the worst and most unprofessional hotel experiences I have ever encountered. There was a serious lack of responsiveness, ownership and basic courtesy towards guests. The biggest question is: what exactly are guests paying for?. At ₹13,291 per night, I expect professional service, functioning facilities, basic amenities and genuine hospitality—not excuses, repeated follow-ups and having to personally chase the hotel staff. The price-to-experience gap here is simply ridiculous. If this is what the hotel considers a 4-star service standard, then the property seriously needs to reconsider both its pricing and its understanding of hospitality. My recommendation: AVOID unless you have absolutely no alternative. There are plenty of hotels where you can spend ₹13,000+ per night and actually receive the level of service you are paying for. I would never choose this property again and would certainly not recommend it to friends, family, colleagues or fellow travellers. ₹13,291 per night for this level of service? Absolutely not justified. In my personal assessment, this experience wasn’t worth even ₹3,000 per night. Extremely disappointing. Extremely overpriced. Extremely poor service

text_light: ⭐️ Extremely disappointing and frustrating experience. I would not recommend this hotel based on how my reservation was handled. I had a confirmed and fully paid booking for 5–6 September 2026 through a third-party booking platform. I had all the confirmation details with me when I arrived at the hotel. Despite this, at the reception I was told that there was no booking under my name. Imagine arriving at a hotel with a confirmed, prepaid reservation and being told that your reservation simply cannot be found. This was extremely frustrating and completely unacceptable. Because of the hotel's inability to properly handle/locate my reservation at the time of check-in, I was put in a situation where I had to make a direct payment at the hotel, creating a double-payment/refund issue. What is even more disappointing is that the booking was subsequently found/acknowledged, yet I was still left dealing with the consequences of the reservation mishandling. I then sent a formal complaint email to the hotel management explaining the entire incident, including the additional payment and refund issue. Even after sending a detailed complaint, the management has not bothered to reply to my email. No proper acknowledgement, no explanation, no resolution and no meaningful communication. This is extremely disappointing customer service. The issue is not simply that there was a booking error. Mistakes can happen. What is unacceptable is how the situation was handled afterwards — the inconvenience at check-in, the additional payment, the resulting refund issue, and then complete silence from the management despite a formal complaint. For a hotel operating under a premium brand, I expected basic professionalism, accountability and customer support. Instead, I was left to chase the matter myself. A confirmed booking should mean exactly that — the hotel should be able to identify the reservation when the guest arrives. And when something goes wrong, the least a customer should expect is a proper response to a formal complaint. Very disappointing experience from start to finish. The way my reservation was handled and the complete lack of response from management has seriously damaged my confidence in this hotel. I hope future guests do not have to go through a similar experience.

text_light: Tucked away at the Erangal Inspection Bungalow grounds on Madh Island (Malad West, Mumbai—note: often mistakenly geotagged online as Navi Mumbai), Beach House Madh Island by amã Stays & Trails (a premium boutique villa brand under the IHCL/Taj umbrella) is an absolute dream for city dwellers. If your goal is to trade corporate gridlock for swaying coconut groves, a private yard, and direct access to the quiet sands of Erangal Beach, this two-bedroom rustic-luxury villa serves as a phenomenal private sanctuary. The Villa Experience: Vintage Charm Meets Taj Hospitality The property operates as a private homestay, masterfully combining a laid-back, coastal Koli-village lifestyle with the refined service standards of the Taj group. The Intimate Layout: The villa features two beautifully styled bedrooms with elegant, minimalist interiors, clean lines, and large glass windows that look out onto a manicured green lawn. The central courtyard and outdoor sit-outs are perfect for late-night family chats or enjoying the cool sea breeze. The Personalized Kitchen: You are not dealing with a chaotic, commercial resort buffet here. The property features a dedicated private chef (with chef John frequently receiving rave reviews from past guests) who curates highly customized, home-style meals. From incredibly fresh, spicy local Koli-style fish fry and prawn curries to simple, comforting North Indian and Continental spreads, the food quality is excellent. The Pet-Friendly Paradise: Unlike typical rigid luxury hotels, this villa welcomes pets with open arms. The expansive outdoor garden spaces provide a safe, free-roaming playground for your furry family members. Pros and Cons Pros: Elite Privacy and Exclusivity: Because you book the entire villa, it offers an incredible, uninterrupted bonding experience for families, close friends, or couples looking for absolute peace. Impeccable Caretaker Service: The on-ground hospitality team manages the property with signature Taj warmth—prompt, polite, and completely non-intrusive. The Sunset & Barbecue Factor: The team can easily set up an elegant evening barbecue session out on the lawn. Eating fresh grills while watching the sun sink into the Arabian Sea is worth the premium price tag alone. Cons: The Narrow, Confusing Approach Roads: Reaching the villa can test your driving skills and patience. The final stretch cutting through the rustic Erangal village involves incredibly tight, winding, and congested lanes. If you are bringing a large SUV, navigating past local traffic and oncoming vehicles is a stressful task. The Coastal Fish-Drying Aroma: Because it sits directly on a living beachfront shared with the local fishing community, depending on wind directions and the season, a strong smell of drying fish can occasionally waft into the outdoor garden area. While authentic to the geography, it can catch sensitive noses off guard. Premium Pricing Tiers: Being a curated amã Stays & Trails property, the per-night villa pricing sits high on the luxury scale. While the service and property layout are beautiful, the lack of a large private swimming pool on-site can make the steep tariff feel slightly high for some travelers. Overall, Beach House Madh Island comfortably earns a well-deserved 4-star rating. While the surrounding village roads and localized coastal scents require a bit of adaptability, the unmatched peace, stunning ocean-facing lawn, incredible customized dining, and pet-friendly freedom make it one of the finest upscale staycation gems hidden inside Maximum City!
