hotel_name: Mumbai House Luxury Apartments, Santacruz East
text_light: Great Homely Space & Views for Families, But Policy Rigidity and Missing Amenities Need Fixes! We recently travelled all the way from Tamil Nadu and stayed at the Mumbai House Luxury Apartment in Santacruz East for 4 nights in a 2 BHK apartment. I was travelling with my wife and two daughters. Overall, the stay was a good experience with a very homely feel, but there are several areas where the management desperately needs to improve. The Highlights (Pros) Homely & Spacious: The 753 sq. ft. apartment feels like a real home rather than a cramped, ordinary hotel room. Spotless Cleanliness: The rooms were neat, and the bathrooms were crystal clean. They provided all essential toiletries (handwash, shower gel, shampoo, and towels). Excellent Housekeeping: Most appreciatively, they cleaned the rooms and changed the towels daily. Amazing Plane-Spotting Views: The views from all sides were wonderful. The living room view was a massive hit—we could watch more than 50 planes take off daily. Good In-Room Amenities: There were TVs attached in the living room and both bedrooms. They provided two 1-litre water bottles daily, alongside an in-house Kent RO water purifier. The kitchen also had basic cooking setups. Great Location Perks: There is a lovely park right adjacent to the apartment, which is perfect for a daily morning or evening walk. Polite Ground Staff: Most of the staff members were incredibly polite, responsive, and answerable. Areas that Need Immediate Improvement (Cons) Arrogant Front Desk Staff: While the ground staff is great, there is a specific man (likely the manager/in-charge) who sits on the reception sofa glued to his laptop. He is quite arrogant, dismissive, and lacks basic politeness. He needs to realize that a business runs on customer money and should treat guests with respect. Strict "Headmaster" Checkout Policies: Their direct website advertises flexible early check-in and late checkout. In reality, they are as strict as school headmasters. Even though we checked in very late the next day, they showed zero consideration and charged us a half-day amount for a slight late checkout. They need to show flexibility when rooms are available. Intrusive Daily Inventory Checks: Every single day, staff comes in for an inventory check. It is highly disturbing and annoying—as if they are storing gold and platinum in the room! Uncomfortable Living Room Sofa: While the living room looks good, the sofa is highly uncomfortable. You cannot sit on it for long. The management must prioritize comfort and convenience over aesthetics. The Subpar Kitchenware: The kitchen cutlery is extremely basic, and the current teacups are highly annoying and awkward to handle. Hard Towels & Poor Water Taste: The towels provided are incredibly hard and harsh on the skin—they need to be replaced with softer ones. Additionally, the RO machine seems to lack a TDS/salt purification system, making the water taste quite bad. No In-House Dining or Travel Help: There is no in-house restaurant, forcing you to rely entirely on Swiggy or Zomato. Furthermore, they provide zero assistance with local sightseeing or cab drops. To make matters worse, the front desk staff completely lacks knowledge about Mumbai's tourist spots—whenever asked, their standard reply is "don't know." Final Verdict: It is a fantastic property for families from a space and cleanliness perspective, but the management needs to stop acting like a strict boarding school, upgrade their furniture/towels, and train their reception head to be customer-centric.

My room had no windows at all, neither in the bedroom nor the bathroom, which made the space feel closed and uncomfortable. It can feel quite suffocating over time. The property also allows hourly bookings for unmarried couples, so there is frequent movement of guests in and out, which may not feel appropriate or comfortable for families. The entrance is inconvenient as well — you have to pass through the banquet hall. If there’s a wedding or event, you’ll need to use the same lift and walk through the crowd, which can be awkward. Noise is another concern. Events in the banquet hall can go on late into the night with loud music, making it difficult to rest. The staircase is accessible to delivery personnel (Zepto, Instamart, etc.), so there’s constant buzzing and movement around the premises. The surroundings outside the hotel are not very clean or pleasant either. Finding the hotel can also be confusing, as there’s only one small sign near the society gate and little guidance after that. Although breakfast is included, it’s served only in the room since there’s no dining area or restaurant. Overall, while it may work for a quick solo stay, I wouldn’t suggest this place for families or anyone looking for a comfortable, peaceful hotel experience.

I stayed at this hotel for 8 days, and unfortunately, my overall experience was very disappointing. The room and facilities did not match my expectations from the booking. My room was advertised with a city view and a window, but I did not receive a proper city view. Wine glasses listed among the room facilities were not provided, and the toiletries were very limited. The actual room also did not feel like the room presented during booking. I had specifically mentioned a quiet room preference, but there was frequent noise outside my room late at night and early in the morning, making it difficult to sleep properly. There were several issues with service as well. After going to sleep around 2:30 AM, I received a call asking about breakfast, followed by another call that they later admitted was made by mistake. On another occasion, a staff member opened my room door directly without knocking or waiting for permission, which was a serious privacy concern. The included breakfast had very limited choices. When I asked for something simple like bread and jam, I was told they did not have it. The food quality was also inconsistent: the pav bhaji served looked more like a mixed vegetable curry, and the poori bhaji was served cold. I ate only one poori and returned the rest. I was offered reheated food, but I declined because breakfast should ideally be served properly in the first place. There were also smaller service issues, such as asking for a plate and not receiving one, and poor coordination with breakfast orders. To be fair, Afroz was very nice, humble and polite, the room was cleaned during my stay, and the à la carte food was good. However, these positives were not enough to make up for the multiple issues with the room, noise, breakfast, service coordination, and privacy. Overall, my experience did not match what was advertised or what I expected for the stay. The hotel seriously needs to improve its service standards, guest privacy, room accuracy, and breakfast quality and variety.

The host and crew are super warm, chilled out, and always ready with great recommendations for local food and hidden spots. The rooftop common area is an absolute game-changer—the ultimate spot to unwind, sip chai, and swap travel stories with fellow backpackers. *Spotless Cleanliness*: For a dorm-style setup, the upkeep is remarkably impressive. The bunk beds are comfortable, the linens are fresh, and the washrooms are kept clean and hygienic. *Prime Location*: You are right in the heart of Mumbai's coolest neighborhood. Historic churches, heritage lanes, bustling street shopping on Hill Road, and iconic cafes (like Candies) are all just a short walk away. text_light: Amazing Facilities Ruined by a Disrespectful Manager (3/5) This property is located very close to Mumbai Airport T2, making it super convenient if you are flying. I originally planned to give this place a 5/5, but I had to drop it to a 3/5 because of a terrible experience with one specific staff member on my last day. Here is the honest breakdown of my 3-day stay: The Positives (Facilities & Comfort): An Introvert’s Dream: I started in the business class private cabin. It was fully air-conditioned, incredibly clean, and had fresh sheets and pillows. It had everything I needed. Pristine Shared Bathrooms: As a first-timer, I was terrified of shared bathrooms, but my biggest fear became my favorite part! There are multiple toilets and bathrooms, and they are maintained immaculately. Odor control is fantastic, and they are cleaned periodically. If anything is ever messy, you just tell the polite cleaning staff and they fix it immediately. The Deluxe Room: On my second day, a friend joined me, so we upgraded to a deluxe room. It was huge, fresh, and beautifully clean. Despite being in a very busy, high-traffic area, the room was perfectly dark and silent. Polite Staff (Mostly): The cleaning staff and the managers on duty during my first two days were incredibly polite, respectful, and welcoming. The Negatives & The Dealbreaker: Delayed Check-In: When moving to the deluxe room, we waited in the lounge from 10:30 AM. Official check-in was at 12:00 PM, but we were given constant excuses and didn't get our room until 12:40 PM. The Disrespectful Manager: On my third day, I booked the business cabin again because I found an amazing deal on Agoda. However, the manager on duty that day completely denied the booking, saying the price was too low, and demanded more money. We declined and asked for a refund, which he refused. He was incredibly rude and actually told us, "You can get a room at slums at this price." My Verdict: Agoda eventually stepped in and refunded my money, but the manager's insult really stuck with us. I would like to apologize for the scene I made in the lobby, but it was purely triggered by his highly disrespectful and unacceptable comments. If the property addresses this management issue, it is easily a 5-star hostel. Until then, be cautious of who is at the front desk!

Recent reviews also mention that the property feels old and that the actual rooms can look quite different from the promotional photos. For me, this would be a “location + budget” stay rather than a hotel experience. If you only need a simple overnight stay in central Pune, especially when the price is attractive, it can make sense. Best suited for: 📍 Excellent central location 🚇 Very convenient for Bund Garden Metro 🚆 Close to Pune Railway Station 💰 Budget overnight stay 🛏️ Fine if you mainly need a place to sleep Not ideal if: ❌ You expect modern interiors ❌ You want a polished/renovated property ❌ Hotel ambience and facilities are important

hotel_name: House of KP by Union Living
text_light: I’ve been staying at House of KP for the last two months, and it has been a great experience so far. The location is convenient while still being tucked away from the noise. Bund Garden Metro Station is about a 5-minute walk away, while Prime Koregaon Park is roughly a 5-minute drive or 30-minute walk. The locality and property itself are quiet, calm, and peaceful. The rooms are moderately spacious and well equipped with an induction, oven, TV, mini fridge, AC, and a comfortable bed and mattress. There is also ample storage for someone living independently. The bathrooms are compact and do not have windows, so this is something I would recommend checking personally before moving in if ventilation and space are important to you. Otherwise, the water pressure and hot water are good, and since the building is relatively new, the overall quality, fittings, and maintenance are good. For anyone working from home, the internet speeds are generally 200+ Mbps, and Airtel mobile coverage is good. There have been some recent internet downtime issues, but hopefully those get resolved soon. The rooms have biometric locks and can also be locked from the inside for privacy. The property has 24/7 security, CCTV, and power backup. Visitors are logged and can visit residents but need to leave by 9 PM. Two-wheeler and four-wheeler parking are also included. Breakfast and dinner are included for full-time coliving residents, with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options and sufficient portions. Dinner has a good variety, and Sunday brunch is available until 1 PM. Dinner is served in the common rooftop area. Rooms are cleaned once every two days with good attention to detail, and the common areas are well maintained. There are three washing machines and drying racks for residents, along with a small elevator and a basic gym. The staff, including security, housekeeping, catering, and management, are friendly and welcoming. The property manager is particularly helpful and available to address concerns. Issues can be logged through the app and are generally resolved quickly. I also appreciate that there is a clearly defined escalation matrix. Overall, I would recommend House of KP to working professionals and people new to Pune who are looking for a convenient, peaceful, fully serviced PG or coliving experience. I would recommend personally checking the bathroom size and ventilation before finalising, as that may be an important consideration depending on your preferences.

hotel_name: House of KP by Union Living
text_light: I stayed at House of KP for three months. During my stay, the overall service was good and I did not have any major issues with the day-to-day experience. However, my experience after vacating was extremely disappointing. At the time of moving out, I was told that my security deposit/refund would be processed within **30–45 days**, which I already feel is quite long compared to what is generally expected in the co-living industry. Unfortunately, even after that period, I had to follow up continuously through numerous emails and calls, often speaking to different people each time, just to get an update on my refund. I finally received my refund **after around two months**. The amount may eventually come back, but the process of getting it back was unnecessarily stressful and frustrating. Another thing to be mindful of is the washroom design. The washrooms are quite **compact and claustrophobic**, and they do not have windows. They may look fine during an initial visit, but after living there, the limited space and ventilation can become an issue. So, if you are an outsider considering House of KP, I would strongly suggest that you **compare it with other co-living options before making a decision**. The stay itself may be fine, but please think carefully about the security deposit and, more importantly, the process and timeline for getting it back after you move out. **My advice: be very mindful before choosing this place, especially if getting your deposit back on time is important to you.**

text_light: Easy To Go is one of the best co-living spaces I've stayed in. The rooms are practical and feel like compact studio apartments, with almost everything you need—TV, fridge, microwave, induction, a comfortable couch, and a well balanced attached washroom. The location is excellent, just a short walk from the metro, and they even have parking for four-wheelers. They also have a dedicated app for maintenance and room-cleaning requests, and the response is always quick. A special mention to the property manager, Ashish, who was incredibly helpful, responsive, and made the entire stay smooth and hassle-free. They've recently started serving food, which is decently good and convenient to have, and for the laundry they do provide couple of washing machines, with only a small inconvenience when it comes to drying clothes. They also offer rooms for short stays or for per night stay, which are great value for money compared to nearby hotels while providing the same amenities. The bathroom wasn't well thought out either — poor placement of the shower, and the geyser wasn't working. The AC made the dorm quite cold at night, so I asked staff for an extra blanket and pillow. Instead of just helping, I was told I needed "permission" for this, and when I followed up, I was spoken to rudely and even insulted in front of other guests over something as basic as an extra blanket. Throughout the stay, staff were unfriendly and seemed to monitor guests' every move rather than focus on hospitality. To add to this, I felt repeatedly pushed to extend my booking, with hints that otherwise I'd be shifted from the 4-bed dorm to an 8-bed dorm — which felt more like a sales tactic than genuine service. Given how close this property is to the OSHO International Resort, I'd specifically caution fellow OSHO sannyasins and meditators against staying here — the poor facilities and staff behavior can really take away from the calm, reflective experience you're there for. Even before check-in, there was unnecessary stress — a day before my arrival, I was informed by the lady handling bookings that the hostel was full. However, when I actually checked in, it clearly wasn’t full at all. The cleanliness and maintenance were extremely disappointing. The bedsheets and blankets did not appear to have been changed, the bathrooms were not clean, and the shower barely worked. I stayed here for 4 nights, and almost every morning there were issues with water. On the second day, I was literally stuck in the shower for around 45 minutes with no water. I called and messaged Renu for help, and after waiting 30–45 minutes, the only response I received was that she was on a week off. The hostel was also not cleaned properly. Used plates with leftover food were left lying around in the room for days. The AC wasn’t functioning properly either, and for an entire day after 1 PM there was no electricity or power backup — no fan, no AC, nothing. The amenities advertised online were also misleading. Towels are supposedly provided, but only if you specifically ask for them, and there was no hair dryer despite it being listed. The photos shown online are very different from reality. To make matters worse, on my fourth day, ₹5,000 was stolen from my wallet even though it was locked inside my bag, which completely destroyed any sense of safety I had. The night shift staff member was very rude. The only helpful person throughout my stay was Charan. Overall, the service was pathetic, cleanliness was poor, amenities were misleading, and safety was a serious concern. I would not recommend staying here.

I recently had the unfortunate experience of staying at Excellent Homes, and I must say it was one of the worst hotel stays I've ever had. From start to finish, this hotel fell far short of even the most basic expectations. Upon arrival, I was met with a lackluster welcome from the front desk staff. They seemed disinterested and unhelpful, providing minimal information about the hotel's amenities and services. The check-in process itself was slow and inefficient, leaving me frustrated after a long journey. The room I was assigned was nothing short of a disappointment. The outdated decor and worn-out furniture gave the impression that the hotel hadn't been renovated in decades. The carpets were stained, and the overall cleanliness left much to be desired. The bathroom was equally unsatisfactory, with moldy grout and a persistent musty odor. To make matters worse, the noise level in the hotel was unbearable. Thin walls allowed every sound from neighboring rooms and the hallway to filter through, making it nearly impossible to get a good night's sleep. It felt like there was no consideration for the comfort of guests whatsoever. The dining experience at Excellent Homes was equally underwhelming. The breakfast buffet lacked variety and freshness, and the service was incredibly slow. It seemed like the staff was overwhelmed and unable to keep up with the number of guests. In terms of customer service, the staff at Excellent Homes continued to disappoint. Requests for simple amenities were met with delays and excuses, and the overall attitude of the staff was indifferent at best. It was evident that guest satisfaction was not a priority for them. I can confidently say that I will never be returning to Excellent Homes and would strongly advise others to steer clear as well. For the price paid, the level of comfort, cleanliness, and overall experience were shockingly subpar. There are far better options available in the area that offer value for money and genuinely care about their guests' experiences.

hotel_name: Sheraton Grand Pune Bund Garden Hotel
text_light: I am writing to share our feedback regarding our recent stay at the Sheraton Grand Hotel Pune on the night of the 15th, checking out on the 16th. I was traveling with my wife and our 2-year-old son, and I must say that this stay is one we will truly cherish for a long time. From the very beginning, the experience was exceptional. During check-in, we were warmly welcomed with traditional Indian culture, including an Arathi and the applying of a Tilak on our foreheads. The team went out of their way to make our little one feel special by presenting him with a lovely painting book and colors. Later, when my boy was looking for some toys to play with, a single phone call request was all it took for the staff to promptly provide a toy piano for him. The absolute highlight and most awesome surprise was a gift given to us. During our welcome, Nirjala took photos of our family, and they thoughtfully printed those memories onto beautiful white mugs. It looks incredibly nice and caught us completely by surprise. This entire seamless experience was curated by Nirjala. She was a fantastic welcomer who made our stay at the Sheraton completely unforgettable. A lovely thank you to Nirjala from my entire family—it was very nice meeting you! We also want to extend our sincere thanks to Harshal, who assisted us during breakfast. He was incredibly humble, consistently checking in to see what we needed, and swiftly serving everything we ordered. He even went the extra mile to pack some fresh fruits for our son, which we highly appreciated. Thank you, Harshal! In addition to the world-class service, we found the big rooms to be impeccably maintained and the food absolutely delicious. Overall, it was a truly amazing stay experience at the Sheraton Grand, with a well-deserved special mention to Nirjala for her outstanding hospitality. We look forward to visiting you again soon.

The OSHO International Meditation Resort is the perfect place to take care of yourself and find inner peace. Safety and cleanliness are top priorities, allowing you to be completely relaxed and present in the moment.

Rating: ⭐☆☆☆☆ (1/5) A heartfelt warning to genuine Osho followers If you are coming here out of love for Osho's teachings, prepare for a deep disconnect. The resort has become heavily commercialized and operates with a rigid, militaristic environment that feels completely contrary to Osho’s vision. Important precautions if you plan to visit: Do not stay inside: The guest house is overpriced, offers minimal basic amenities (even simple requests like water can be a struggle), and feels very restrictive. Stay at a hotel outside in Koregaon Park instead. Aggressive Security & Staff: The welcome desk lacks basic hospitality, and the security staff can be extremely rude, hostile, and invasive. Strict Timings: Arrive early and do not attempt to leave meditation sessions early or enter late, or you will be blocked and confronted by security. Financials & Food: Eat outside the resort. Do not pay large sums in advance, as they have zero refund flexibility. Visit purely for the meditation spaces if you must, but keep your expectations strictly administrative rather than spiritual.

A Terrible Experience at the Osho Ashram I , recently visited the Osho Ashram with the expectation of spending a peaceful and meaningful five days in meditation and reflection. Unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing and far removed from what I had expected from a place associated with meditation and inner peace. From the very beginning, there appeared to be a serious lack of organisation and crowd management. There was excessive crowding, with no proper system to ensure that visitors could meditate peacefully. At Chuang Tzu, for example, the space appeared suitable for approximately 50 people, yet nearly 200 people were attempting to enter. As a result, many visitors were left wandering around without proper arrangements or an appropriate place to meditate. The situation became so chaotic that I approached the administrator, Dhyanesh Bharti, to request that the situation be managed properly. I also informed him that, given the circumstances, I wished to cancel my five-day stay because the facilities and arrangements were not what I had expected. Instead of addressing my concerns professionally, I was told that my money would not be refunded. I found his manner of speaking extremely rude and intimidating. During the interaction, he allegedly told me that he did not fear the police and that I could call them if I wished. I found this statement particularly disturbing, especially when I was simply raising a legitimate concern about my stay. The situation became even more uncomfortable when a security person who was standing beside him appeared to act aggressively towards me. I felt intimidated and unsafe during an interaction that should have been handled calmly and professionally. My purpose in visiting the Osho Ashram was to meditate, find peace and have a meaningful five-day experience. Instead, I encountered overcrowding, poor organisation, inadequate arrangements and an extremely unpleasant interaction with the administration. I believe that visitors who pay for a stay and come with genuine expectations of meditation and peace deserve proper arrangements, respectful treatment and a safe environment. I hope the management takes such complaints seriously, improves crowd management and ensures that visitors are treated with dignity and courtesy in the future. This article reflects my personal experience and concerns regarding my visit, and I hope it encourages the concerned authorities and management to look into the matter.
